GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3518 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
RESPIRATORY TRACKING SYSTEM FOR WORKERS OF MINING 
SECTOR 
3518. SHRI ARUN BHARTI: 
  SMT. SHAMBHAVI: 
  SHRI RAJESH VERMA: 
  DR. D. PURANDESWARI: 
  SHRI ATUL GARG: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a)whether the Government has operationalised the National 
Occupational Health Registry to track respiratory and long -term 
health metrics among mining workers and if so, the details thereof; 
 (b)the details of the non -intrusive wearable sensor systems deployed 
in May 2026 to track toxic gas exposures in real-time; 
 (c)the details of structural checks established within the central health 
portal to instantly alert regional medical units during high -risk 
environmental shifts; 
 (d)the details of criteria used to disburse targeted performance -linked 
health infrastructure grants to mining cooperatives managing 
localized medical check-up hubs; 
 (e)the details of measures taken by the Government to integrate the 
said worker health records with the central ESI database for 
seamless specialized hospital transfers; and 
 (f)the details of projected reduction in peak occupational health 
incidents following the nationwide deployment of the said proactive 
digital monitoring network? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (f): The Central Government has enacted the Occupational 
Safety, Health and Working Conditions (OSH&WC) Code, 2020, which 
has come into force with effect from 21.11.2025 to regulate 
occupational safety, health and working conditions of the persons 
employed in m ining. The Central Government has also notified OSH & 
WC (Central) Rules 2026 on 08.05.2026.  
Contd..2/- 

:: 2 :: 
  The third schedule of the code specifies the list of twenty -
nine (29) notifiable diseases including Coal miners' pneumoconiosis, 
silicosis etc. 
  Rule 8 of the OSH&WC (Central) Rules mandates that the 
employer shall send a notice to the Inspector -cum-Facilitator or the 
Chief Inspector -cum-Facilitator whenever a worker contracts any 
disease specified in the Third Schedule to the Code. 
  Rule 109  of the OSH&WC (Central) Rules, 2026 also 
mandates that the employer of every mine shall arrange for the initial 
medical examination of every person seeking employment, as well as 
annual periodical medical examinations. In cases where the medical 
examining authority confirms suspected dust -related diseases, the 
employer shall also arrange for medical examinations at frequent 
intervals, including x -rays or both, as required. In case of worker 
affected, the employer shall be liable to pay compensation in 
accordance with the provisions of Code on Social Security, 2020. 
  The OSH&WC Code, 2020 mandates employers to provide 
training and supervision, safe and without risk workplace, maintain 
occupational safety and health standards, personal protective 
equipment (PPE), welfare facilities, emergency preparedness, first -aid, 
firefighting arrangements and other safety measures as prescribed. 
  The health record of workers registered with ESIC are 
maintained in Dhanwantri portal of ESIC.

entries.t: SOP for Scientific Identification of threatened Species
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3519 
                                         TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
 
SOP for Scientific Identification of threatened Species 
 
3519. SHRI MANISH TEWARI:  
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) the details of the 159 plant and 173 animal species currently officially designated and notified 
as threatened under Section 38 of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 across the identified 17 
States and 3 Union Territories, State-wise; 
(b) the targeted execution timeline, structural budgetary allocations and implementation 
guidelines provided in the new Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) to assist State Biodiversity 
Boards and Union Territory Biodiversity Councils in launching mandatory species recovery and 
conservation action plans; 
(c) the precise scientific validation criteria and field-assessment methodologies deployed by the 
Botanical Survey of India and the Zoological Survey of India to authenticate local field data and 
traditional ecological knowledge during the local identification process; and 
(d) the specific statutory enforcement mechanisms under the 2025 Benefit-Sharing Regulations 
that mandate differential financial obligations and benefit-sharing collections for biological 
resources derived exclusively from these newly notified threatened species? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (d): As per Section 38 of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 (as amended in 2023), the 
Central Government, in consultation with the concerned State Government, may from time to 
time notify any species which is on the verge of extinction or likely to become extinct in the 
near future as a threatened species and prohibit or regulate collection thereof for any purpose 
and take appropriate steps to rehabilitate and preserve those species.  
 
So far, 159 plant and 174 animal species have been notified as threatened species under Section 
38 of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 (as amended in 2023), and the list of threatened species 
notified under Section 38 of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 (as amended in 2023) across 
17 States and three Union Territories is published on the National Biodiversity Authority 
website www.nbaindia.org. 
 
As per the recently published Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) of the National Biodiversity 
Authority on 16.06.2026, the State Biodiversity Board or Union Territory Biodiversity 
Council, in association with the Botanical Survey of India, Zoological Survey of India, Forest 
Departments, scientific institutions, or any other organization, shall undertake a scientific 

assessment that shall include population trends, geographic range, habitat quality, habitat 
fragmentation, exploitation pressures, reproductive biology, ecological requirements, and 
extinction risk. The objective of the SOP is to establish a transparent, science-based, 
participatory framework for the identification, assessment, notification, conservation, 
rehabilitation, monitoring, and periodic review of threatened species under Section 38 of the 
Biological Diversity Act, 2002 (as amended in 2023).  
 
In the SOP, there is no mention of execution timelines, structural budgetary allocations, or 
implementation guidelines to assist State Biodiversity Boards and Union Territory Biodiversity 
Councils in launching mandatory species recovery and conservation action plans, as the Central 
Government, in consultation with the concerned State Government, may from time to time 
notify the threatened species under Section 38 of the Act.  
 
The Access and Benefit Sharing Regulations, 2025 under regulation 4 and 5 states that in case 
of biological resource having conservation value or high economic value such as red sanders, 
sandalwood, agarwood or any other items as decided by the Authority from time to time, and 
including threatened species notified under section 38 of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 (as 
amended in 2023), the benefit sharing shall not be less than five percent of the proceeds of the 
auction or sale amount or the purchase price, as the case may be, as determined by the Authority 
on case to case basis, as upfront payment.

(a) to (e) : Under the Government of India’s Skill India Mission (SIM), the Ministry of Skill 
Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re-skill and up-skill training through an 
extensive network of skill development centres / institutes unde r various schemes, viz. Pradhan 
Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Sikhshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship 
Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsman Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training 
Institutes (ITIs), to all the sections of the society across the country including the rural and 
aspirational areas of Tamil Nadu. The SIM aims at enabling the youth of India to get future-ready, 
equipped with industry-relevant skills.  
Amongst the schemes of MSDE, under PMKVY, placements were tracked in the Short -Term 
Training (STT) component in the first three versions of the Scheme - PMKVY 1.0, PMKVY 2.0 
and PMKVY 3.0, implemented from FY2015 -16 to FY 2021 -22, wherein more than 56 lakh  
candidates were certified under Short Term Training (STT), out of which 24.38 lakhs were 
reported placed under the short-term training component of the scheme. Further, under PMKVY 
4.0, the focus is to empower the trained candidates to choose their varied career paths, and they 
are suitably oriented for the same. 

The details of number of training centres established, candidates enrolled, trained and certified 
under various schemes of MSDE in the Tamil Nadu during the last three years and the current 
year, district-wise are at Annexure.

coverage of Scheduled Castes/ Scheduled Tribes / Women beneficiaries and geographic areas 
such as Aspirational Districts, LWE, Tribal districts, etc. Special attention has been  given to 
women, tribal communities, and other marginalized groups in rural areas to promote their 
participation in the skill development programs. In order to increase inclusivity, Boarding and 
Lodging (B&L) and transport facilities are provided to specia l groups (Women and PwD) and 
Special Areas, as defined in Common Norms, for training within and outside Special Areas. 
Conveyance facility is also permissible for special groups in case of non -residential training as 
per Common Norms. 
The JSS Scheme  aims to provide skill training in a non -formal mode at the doorstep of 
beneficiaries through 100% financial assistance from the Government of India, special emphasis 
is placed on women, Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), Other Backward Classes 
(OBCs), minorities, and individuals from rural and urban low-income communities.  In the state of 
Tamil Nadu, more than 90% of the total beneficiaries belong to Scheduled Castes (SCs), 
Scheduled Tribes (STs) and other disadvantaged groups, with women constituting 86% of the 
beneficiaries. Livelihood cells have been created at each JSS, headed by the Programme Officer 
of the JSS and supported by other staff members. This cell forms linkages of the trained JSS

entries.head:

MINISTRY OF EDUCA TION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3525

Promotion of Punjabi Language in Higher Education 
3525.   Shri Malvinder Singh Kang: 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
(a) the measures taken by the Government to encourage higher education, management 
education and social science research in Punjabi language; 
(b) whether any textbooks, digital learning material and research publications have been 
prepared in Punjabi under the National Education Policy, 2020, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the details of funds allocated for this purpose during the last five years; and  
(d) the future roadmap for strengthening Punjabi as a medium of higher education in Central 
educational institutions?  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (d): The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 highlights the importance of 
multilingualism and places strong emphasis on the promotion of all Indian languages. In 
alignment with the objectives of NEP 2020, the Government has undertaken several initiatives 
for the preservation, promotion and development of Indian languages through dedicated 
institutions and academic programmes.  
 
The All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), a statutory body under the 
Ministry of Education, has undertaken several initiatives to promote technical and management 
education in all 22 Scheduled Indian Languages, including Punjabi, by facilitating the creation 
of a digital knowledge base and enhancing the availability of quality technical learning 
resources in Indian languages. The major initiatives are as follows: 
 

 AICTE has made provisions for AICTE-approved Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) 
to offer technical education in Indian languages, including Punjabi, by permitting the 
introduction of one additional division with 30 or 60 supernumerary seats. 
 AICTE launched the Technical Book Writing and Translation Scheme during the year 
2021-22 to facilitate the availability of Engineering (Degree and Diploma) textbooks 
in Indian languages, including Punjabi. 
 AICTE has developed the e-KUMBH portal as a digital repository of technical 
textbooks in English and Indian languages, providing free access to quality technical 
learning resources. The portal provides free access to technical learning resources for 
institutions, faculty members, students and other stakeholders.  
 The AICTE–V AANI (Vibrant Advocacy for Advancement and Nurturing of Indian 
Languages) Scheme has been launched to promote the use of Indian languages, 
including Punjabi, in technical education. The Scheme provides financial assistance for 
organizing Conferences, Seminars and Workshops in 22 Scheduled Indian Languages, 
enabling academicians, researchers and industry professionals to disseminate 
knowledge, innovations and research in emerging areas of technical education and 
contribute to the creation of a knowledge base in Indian languages. 
The Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR), a premier body of the 
Government of India for research in the social and human sciences, promotes social science 
research through Research Projects, Fellowships, Collaborative Studies and Special Research 
Programmes. Under these programmes, ICSSR has supported research on Punjabi language 
and literature & also provides Senior Fellowships, Post-Doctoral Fellowships and Doctoral 
Fellowships for scholars working on Punjabi language, literature and allied themes. 
To strengthen the use of Punjabi and other Indian languages in higher education ecosystem, 
the Ministry of Education has taken several measures through its institutions and autonomous 
bodies. Central Institute of Indian Languages (CIIL), Mysuru, a subordinate office under the 
Ministry of Education, undertakes research, documentation, propagation, teaching, protection 
and preservation of all Indian languages. To provide quality academic resources in Indian 
languages, the National Translation Mission (NTM), implemented by CIIL, Mysuru 
undertakes the translation and publication of knowledge texts across disciplines taught in 
colleges and universities, while also promoting translator training and the development of 
translation resources. Under the Mission, knowledge texts in print and e-books, Translation 
Equivalents resource in History and Popular Science books have been published. In addition, 
141 Punjabi translators have been trained through Intensive Training and Skill Development 
Programmes.

Linguistic Data Consortium for Indian Languages (LDC-IL), implemented by CIIL, Mysuru

including Punjabi. As on date, more than 70 datasets have been released which includes text,

entries.t: Politically Exposed Persons in the Banking Sector
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
DEPARTMENT OF FINANCIAL SERVICES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3526 
 ANSWERED ON MONDAY, AUGUST 10, 2026/SHRAVANA 19, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
Politically Exposed Persons in the Banking Sector 
 
3526.  SHRI MAGUNTA SREENIVASULU REDDY: 
 
 Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the term "Politically Exposed Persons" (PEPs) is used in the banking and financial 
sector, if so, the definition and categories of persons, including family members and close 
associates, covered thereunder; 
(b) the details of public positions, professions/occupations or categories of persons classified or 
treated as PEPs under the extant rules/guidelines; 
(c) whether the Government is aware of concerns that such classification may result in enhanced 
scrutiny, restrictions or hardship in availing banking and financial services for elected 
representatives, other persons holding public positions, their family members and close 
associates, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) whether the Government proposes to review the existing PEP guidelines to ensure that such 
classification does not result in unwarranted discrimination or hardship to persons covered 
thereunder and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a) to (d): As per the Master Direction of Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Know Your Customer 
(KYC), 2025, the term “Politically Exposed Person” (PEP) is defined to cover individuals who 
are or have been entrusted with prominent public functions by a foreign country, including the 
Heads of States/Governments, senior politicians, senior government or judicial or military 
officers, senior executives of state-owned corporations and important political party officials.  
The RBI’s Master Direction on KYC mandates banks to have the option of establishing a 
relationship with PEPs (whether as customer or beneficial owner) provided that, apart from 
performing normal customer due diligence, the following procedures are to be followed:  
i.banks to have in place appropriate risk management systems to determine whether the 
customer or the beneficial owner is a PEP; 
ii.reasonable measures are taken by the banks for establishing the source of funds / wealth; 
iii.the approval to open an account for a PEP to be obtained from the senior management; 
iv.all such accounts are subjected to enhanced monitoring on an on-going basis; 

v.in the event of an existing customer or the beneficial owner of an existing account 
subsequently becoming a PEP, senior management’s approval is obtained to continue the 
business relationship; 
These instructions also apply to family members or close associates of PEPs. 
RBI has directed banks to use the PEP classification solely as a risk assessment tool. Further, 
it emphasizes that while enhanced due diligence is necessary for PEPs; this should not lead to 
discriminatory practices.

Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the details of total number of artists supported by the Zonal Cultural Centres (ZCCs) 
during the last five years, State/UT-wise and category-wise, including folk, tribal, 
classical and contemporary artists; 
(b) the details of the financial support, including honorarium, scholarships, grants and other 
assistance provided to tribal artists, other artists, cultural institutions and art 
organizations during the last five years, along with the number of beneficiaries benefited 
under each scheme, year, scheme and State-wise; 
(c) whether the Government maintains separate data on beneficiaries belonging to the 
Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) under its various schemes for artists 
and, if so, the details thereof, including the number of SC and ST beneficiaries, scheme 
and State/UT-wise; and 
(d) the details of steps taken by the Government to strengthen further financial support for 
tribal artists, enhance their livelihood opportunities, and preserve, promote and revive 
endangered folk, tribal and traditional art forms across the country?

MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM  
(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT)

throughout the country, the Government of India has set up seven Zonal Cultural Centres 
(ZCCs) with headquarters at Patiala, Nagpur, Udaipur, Prayagraj, Kolkata, Dimapur and 
Thanjavur. These ZCCs organize various cultural activities and programmes on regular basis 
for which they engage folk/ tribal artists including classical artists from their member States. 
These artists are paid honorarium, TA/DA, local transportation, boarding & lodging etc. to 
enable them to earn their livelihood. The State-wise number of artists supported by ZCCs 
alongwith financial support (including honorarium) provided to them during the last five (05) 
years are at Annexure-I.

financial support, scholarships, grants and other assistance is provided to tribal artists, other 
artists, cultural institutions and art organizations, the details of which are as under:

Grant):  The objective of this scheme component is to provide financial support for all 
genres of performing arts activities like dramatic groups, theatre groups, music ensembles, 
children theatre etc. and imparting training of artists by their respective Guru on regular 
basis in line with Guru–Shishya Parampara. As per the scheme, support is provided to 1 
Guru and maximum 18 Shishyas across all art forms. 
 

ii. Financial Assistance to Cultural organizations with National Presence: The 
objective of the scheme component is to promote and support cultural organizations with 
national presence involved in promotion of art and culture throughout the country. This 
grant is given to such organisations that have a properly constituted managing body, 
registered in India, having a pan-India character with national presence in its operation, 
adequate working strength and have spent Rs. 1.00 crore or more during 3 of the last 5 
years on cultural activities. 
 
iii. Cultural Function & Production Grant (CFPG):  The objective of this scheme 
component is to provide financial support to NGOs/ Societies/ Trusts/ Universities etc. for 
Seminars, Conference, Research, Workshops, Festivals, Exhibitions, Symposia, 
Production of Dance, Drama-Theatre, Music etc. 
 
iv. Financial Assistance for Veteran Artists:  The objective of this Scheme is to 
provide financial assistance maximum upto Rs. 6.000/- p.m. to the old artistes and 
scholars aged 60 years above having annual income not exceeding Rs. 72,000/- who have 
contributed significantly in their specialized fields of arts, letters etc. In the event of death

Initiative for Promotion of Emerging Technologies in Schools 
 
3528. Shri Ganesh Singh:  
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the details of the initiatives undertaken by the Government across the States to promote digital 
transformation, Artificial Intelligence (AI), coding and other emerging technologies in school education along 
with the status of their implementation, State and district-wise;  
(b) the number of schools equipped with digital infrastructure including smart classrooms, computer 
laboratories and internet connectivity, State and district-wise; 
(c) the number of students and teachers who have been provided training in AI, coding and digital skills under 
various Government programmes, State and district-wise; 
(d) the details of the financial allocation and expenditure incurred for promoting digital and technology-
enabled learning in schools during the last three years, State-wise; and  
(e) the details of the progress made in Madhya Pradesh, particularly in Satna Lok Sabha Constituency in 
regard to the above initiative and the measures being taken by the Government to bridge the digital divide and 
ensure equitable access to future-ready education across rural and urban areas? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
(a): Education is part of the Concurrent List of the Constitution and most of the Government schools are 
under the administration of the State Government and its bodies. The Ministry of Education implements ICT 
and Digital initiatives such as PM eVidya and DIKSHA under Samagra Shiksha to enhance and transform 
digital learning and strengthen technology enabled teaching in Government schools across the country 
including the State of Madhya Pradesh and particularly Satna Lok Sabha constituency. The initiatives aim to 
enhance the quality of education by integrating technology into teaching and learning processes. Under the 
scheme, funds are provided for setting up ICT Labs and Smart Classrooms according to the requirement of 
the State submitted in the Annual Work Plan & Budget (AWP&B).  
A comprehensive initiative called PM eVidya has been launched, which unifies all efforts related to 
digital/online/on-air education to enable multi-mode access to education across the country. The key 
components of PM eVidya are also aligned towards enhancing digital literacy and include 200 DTH TV 
channels and 400 Radio channels to enable all States/UTs to provide supplementary education in various 
Indian languages for classes 1-12. 
Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing (DIKSHA) is the Nation’s One Nation, One Digital 
platform for providing quality e-content for school education in States/UTs along with QR coded Energised 
Textbooks (ETBs) for all grades. As a participant in DIKSHA, States/UTs/ABs have generated and 
contributed over 3.67 lakh content in mother local/regional languages enabling multilingualism. The 
platform supports both online and offline access, enabling learners to download content and continue 
learning without internet connectivity. The stakeholders have access to more than 836 Virtual Labs and 100 
Virtual skill labs (50 each in Hindi and English) on DIKSHA that help students with simulation of real-
world laboratory environments.  
  

Further, the Government has introduced AI enabled features on DIKSHA like Personalised 
Adaptive Learning (PAL) for students of Class 9 and 10 for Science and Mathematics, Ask DIKSHA (Chat 
with Books), Video Keyword Search, Read Aloud, AI-based Translation are available nationwide for all 
users. The Summary feature provides the user a brief overview of the entire chapter by summarising key 
concepts and important points for quick revision. As part of the Podcast feature, AI generated conversational 
discussion helps explain a topic or chapter, enabling students to learn through listening. Through the Join 
the Conversation feature, users can join the podcast conversation anytime to ask questions and get their 
doubts addressed in real time.

(https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?kecs1=ps-11) and Informatics Practices class XI (Chapter 2) 
(https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?keip1=ps-8) talk about AI, Internet of Things (IoT) and other emerging 
technologies. NCERT has also included a project on Animation and Games in the vocational education 
textbook for Grade 6. Further, CBSE offers a skill module on Artificial Intelligence for classes VI-VIII and 
an optional skill-based subject on Artificial Intelligence for classes IX- XII. States/UTs are free to adopt / 
adapt NCERT curriculum. Currently, DIKSHA holds 59 courses on AI and Digital Learning with 9.4+ lakh 
enrolments.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. †3530 
ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
PROTECTION OF CULTURAL HERITAGE AND TRADITIONAL ARTISTS UNDER KSVY 
 
†3530 Shri Darshan Singh Choudhary: 
Shri Tharaniventhan M S: 
Shri Bharat Singh Kushwah: 
Will the MINISTER OF CULTURE be pleased to state 
(a) whether the Government has conducted any evaluation of the impact and progress of Kala Sanskriti 
Vikas Yojana (KSVY) in promoting traditional art forms, folk culture, performing arts and cultural 
activities across the country during the last five years, if so, the details thereof, State/UT- wise, 
particularly in Arani Lok Sabha Constituency of Tamil Nadu;  
(b) whether the Government has received requests from cultural organisations and artists regarding 
delays in approval, release of grants or procedural difficulties under the said scheme, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(c) the details of steps taken/being taken by the Government to ensure wider outreach, transparency, 
timely financial assistance, greater participation of artists and cultural institutions, development of 
cultural infrastructure and linkages with cultural tourism for young and emerging artists particularly 
from rural, tribal and economically weaker sections;  
(d) the details of targets set for 2026–27 and upcoming years, proposed new initiatives and financial and 
technical support to be provided to the States;  
(e) whether the Government is considering implementing any special plan/scheme to preserve and 
promote the rich cultural and music traditions, connect local artists and cultural institutions with the 
said scheme and expand cultural activities in Madhya Pradesh, especially the Gwalior Lok Sabha 
constituency; and 
(f) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM 
(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) Yes, Sir. The Ministry of Culture undertakes third-party evaluations of the Kala Sanskriti Vikas 
Yojana (KSVY) prior to each Finance Commission cycle to evaluate the impact, progress and cultural 
outreach of KSVY Scheme across the country including the state of Tamil Nadu. The State/UT-wise 

details of the number of organizations and individual artists supported, including folk and traditional 
artists, under various components of KSVY during the last five years are given at Annexure. However, 
constituency-wise data is not maintained by the Ministry. 
 
(b) Requests received from cultural organizations and artists regarding the implementation of the 
schemes are examined promptly and appropriate corrective and facilitative measures are taken in a 
proactive and timely manner to ensure effective implementation of the schemes. 
 
(c) and (d)The Ministry of Culture has been taking continuous steps to ensure wider outreach, 
transparency and timely financial assistance under its schemes to support cultural organizations and 
artists, including those from rural, tribal and economically weaker sections and provides assistance for 
the promotion of traditional art forms and development of cultural infrastructure. For this, the scheme 
Guidelines and application forms are uploaded on the Ministry's website and wide publicity is given 
through newspapers, the official website and social media platforms of the Ministry and the concerned 
nodal agencies and also through ZCCs and akademies. Further, the scheme guidelines and eligibility 
criteria have also been simplified to facilitate greater participation of eligible artists and cultural 
institutions. 
   
(e) and (f) At present, no separate special plan or scheme is under consideration specifically for Madhya 
Pradesh or the Gwalior Lok Sabha Constituency. However, eligible artists, cultural organizations and 
institutions from Madhya Pradesh, including Gwalior, are eligible to avail benefits under the various 
schemes of the Ministry of Culture, subject to fulfilment of the prescribed eligibility criteria and 
provisions of the respective Scheme Guidelines.

entries.t: National Level Study on Students Suicides
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3534 
ANSWERED ON 10/08/2026 
 
National Level Study on Students Suicides 
 
†3534. Shri Imran Masood: 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has conducted any national-level study on the incidents of suicide 
by students in schools, colleges and higher educational institutions during the period from 
January to June, 2026; 
(b) if so, the details of such cases, the major reasons therefor along with the psychosocial 
support provided to the affected students, State-wise and institution-wise; 
(c) whether the Government has prepared any national action plan to address academic stress, 
ragging, mental health issues and to strengthen counselling services, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether the Government proposes to provide trained psychological counsellors and a 24x7 
support system in all higher educational institutions; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?     
     
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
(a) to (e): National Crime Record Bureau (NCRB) collects data on suicides from police 
recorded suicide cases. Comprehensive analysis of the data related to the accidental deaths and 
suicides in the country is published in the yearly Accidental Death & Suicide in India (ADSI) 
reports by National Crime Record Bureau (NCRB). Year wise , State wise, Gender and Age 
group wise details of student suicides are available in the ADSI reports which are accessible at 
https://ncrb.gov.in/accidental-deaths-suicides-in-india-year-wise.html .  
As per these Reports, there are various causes of suicides like professional/career problems, 
sense of isolation, abuse, violence, family problems, mental disorders, addiction to alcohol, 
financial loss, chronic pain etc. 
To address the issue of suicide, the Government is taking multi-pronged measures and provides 
psychological support to students, teachers and families for mental and emotional well-being 
to avoid incidences of suicide.  
An initiative of Ministry of Education, MANODARPAN, covers a wide range of activities to 
provide psychological support to students, teachers and families for mental and emotional well-
being such as National toll-free helpline to provide guidance to callers through trained 
counsellor; live interactive sessions ‘Sahyog’ and Webinars ‘Paricharcha’ that are organized 
regularly to create awareness about the importance of mental health among all stakeholders, 

including students in all States/UTs etc. These sessions are telecast on PM e-Vidya channels 
and are also available on ‘NCERT Official’ YouTube Channel. 
The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has mandated the appointment of 
Counsellor & Wellness Teacher in every Secondary and Senior Secondary school affiliated 
with it in its Affiliation bye laws. In Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti (NVS), there is a provision 
for engagement of two counsellors (one male and one female) in each Jawahar Navodaya 
Vidyalaya (JNV) on contractual basis and total 830 counsellors have been engaged on 
contractual basis in JNVs across the country as of February, 2026. Further, directions have been 
issued to all KVs to appoint counsellors in all schools on contract basis for the time being. 
UGC has issued advisory to HEIs in January, 2023 circulating the National Suicide Prevention 
Strategy framed by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. UGC also issued Guidelines on 
13.04.2023, which provide for promoting physical fitness and sports activities for students; 
creating safeguards against academic pressure, peer pressure, behavioral issues, stress, career 
concerns, depression and other issues on the mental health of students; to teach positive thinking 
& emotions in the student community; and to promote a positive and supportive network for 
students. 
UGC has launched an extensive anti-ragging outreach initiative across all of its official social 
media channels, including X (Twitter), Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, and 
YouTube. These campaigns feature short videos, banners, and other creatives disseminated in 
21 languages to ensure wide accessibility and engagement.  
 
Further, UGC has taken action as per the UGC Regulations on curbing the menace of ragging 
in higher educational institutions, 2009. Anti-ragging measures viz. establishment of 24x7 
National anti-ragging helpline, anti-ragging workshops and seminars, mandatory inclusion of 
severe consequences of ragging in prospectus of institutions, mandatory online undertaking by 
students and parents every academic year, display of anti-ragging posters at prominent places 
in the institutions etc. have been taken to ensure compliance of the regulation.

mental well-being of students in Higher Educa

state: 
(a) whether the Government has identified the district recording the highest temperatures in the

last 10 years; 
(b) whether the Government has implemented any special action plan or programme for the 
highly affected districts, including Buxar, Rohtas and Kaimur to mitigate the impact of rising 
temperatures and heatwaves; 
(c) the reasons for the rise in temperature in Bihar during the last 10 years, and whether any 
investigation or study has been conducted in this regard; and 
(d) if so, the details of the funds spent on temperature control, expansion of green cover, water 
conservation, and climate adaptation-related works in all the districts of the State, including 
Buxar, Rothas and Kaimur during the last five years, year-wise along with the outcomes

(a) : According to climate vulnerability and seasonal weather tracking reports published by the 
Indian Meteorological Department (IMD), Rohtas (specifically Dehri), Buxar, Aurangabad, 
and Kaimur districts in south-western Bihar are consistently identified as recording the highest 
maximum temperatures and severe heatwave conditions in the State. The Bihar Mausam Sewa 
Kendra (BMSK), Government of Bihar has established the Automatic Weather Station (AWC)

has done the heat wave mapping for the State and prepared the Bihar State Heat Action Plan.

overarching framework for India’s climate actions, the Government of Bihar has prepared State 
Action Plan on Climate Change (SAPCC). The State Governments are expected to provide the

entries.t: Implementation of Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan in Uttar Pradesh
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION  
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION AND LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO - 3538 
ANSWERED ON – 10/08/2026 
 
 
Implementation of Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan in Uttar Pradesh 
 
†3538. Shri Arun Kumar Sagar: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of new High Schools and Intermediate Colleges required in the State of Uttar 
Pradesh in accordance with the norms of the Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan; 
(b) whether the Central Government has taken any steps for the establishment of High Schools 
and Intermediate Colleges in Uttar Pradesh, particularly in the Shahjahanpur Lok Sabha 
Parliamentary Constituency in accordance with the norms of the Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha 
Abhiyan; and 
(c) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a)  to (c):  The Department of School and Literacy has launched an integrated Centrally 
Sponsored Scheme for School Education – Samagra Shiksha with effect from 2018-19 by 
subsuming the three erstwhile Centrally Sponsored Schemes of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), 
Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA) and Teacher Education. 
 
  The infrastructural requirement of setting-up of new schools, strengthening of existing 
schools and upgradation of existing schools are worked out every year by the respective 
State/UT as per their need and priority and reflected in their Annual Work Plan and Budget 
(AWP&B). These plans are then appraised and approved by Project Approval Board (PAB) in 
consultation with the States and Union Territories as per the programmatic and financial norms 
of the scheme, physical and financial progress of works sanctioned earlier and availability of 
budgetary resource. 
 
  Under Samagra Shiksha, for providing universal access to quality secondary education, 
the neighbourhood norms notified by the State/UT would be applicable for opening of new 
secondary and senior secondary schools. As informed by the State Government of Uttar 
Pradesh, opening of a new Government High School is considered in habitations where a 
Government Secondary School is not available within the prescribed neighborhood distance of 
7-10 km. Similarly, up-gradation of a Government High School to Intermediate level is 
considered based on enrolment, availability of infrastructure, feeder requirement and school 
mapping.  
 
  Presently, under Samagra Shiksha, total 240 Government High Schools and 82 
Government Intermediate Colleges have been sanctioned in the State of Uttar Pradesh. Further, 
5 Government Secondary Schools have been opened in Shahjahanpur district.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCA TION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 3543 
ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Placements for Engineering Graduates 
 
3543. Dr. M K Vishnu Prasad: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the total number of students graduating as engineering professionals during the last five years, year-
wise and State-wise; 
 
(b) whether the Government has any data on the number of engineering graduates getting placement after 
graduation each year, if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(c) the details of steps taken by the Government to create placements for engineering graduates in 
Government sectors/PSUs in the country during the last five years, State-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) & (b): As per All India Survey on Higher Education (AISHE), the latest available State/UT-wise total 
students enrolled in engineering courses from the year 2019-20 to 2023-24 is given in the Annexure-I 
 
From the Annual Report of Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), 2025, the estimates of Worker 
Population Ratio (WPR) for ‘graduates’ are 58.8 and for ‘post graduates and above’ is 63.6 in India. 
 
As per Periodic Labour Force Surveys (PLFS), the estimated Worker Population Ratio (WPR) for 
‘graduates’ has increased from 50.6 during 2019-20 to 57.5 during 2023-24 and for ‘post graduates and 
above’ has increased from 59.5 during 2019-20 to 62.2 during 2023-24. 
 
(c): Education being in the Concurrent List is the responsibility of both Central and States Governments. 
To enhance employability of the students and achieve the objectives of NEP 2020, the National Credit 
Framework (NCrF) has been issued enabling integration of Skill Education into academia. It also enables 
credit accumulation through diversified domains such as Skill Enhancement Courses, Value Addition 
Courses, Ability Enhancement Courses alongwith Internships and Projects. The NCrF also has a provision 
for the accumulation of a maximum of 50% of the total credit required through skill-based courses. These 
provisions have enabled Higher Educational Institutions to provide relevant knowledge to the students, 
making them industry ready. 
 
The All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) has taken several steps to ensure the 
availability of industry-relevant knowledge to students of technical institutions, inter alia: 
 
i. Development and periodic revision of Outcome-Based Model Curricula aligned with 
industry requirements and emerging technologies. 

 
ii. Promotion of mandatory internships under the AICTE Internship Policy through the 
National Internship Portal. 
 
iii. AICTE Placement Portal to facilitate interaction between employers and students, 
particularly those from institutions located in rural, tribal and aspirational districts. 
 
iv. Promotion of industry-academia collaboration through internships, apprenticeships, 
innovation, entrepreneurship and skill development programmes; and  
 
v. Capacity building in emerging technologies through Faculty Development Programmes, 
AICTE internship portal, NEAT, SWAYAM, IDEA Labs and other employability 
enhancement initiatives.  
 
UGC has issued ‘Guidelines for Internship/Research Internship for Under Graduate Students’, with 
an aim to improve their employability and understanding of the world of work. Further, UGC has 
formulated ‘Guidelines for Higher Educational Institutions to Offer Apprenticeship Embedded Degree 
Programme (AEDP)’ to enhance the employability of students. 
Further, The Ministry of Education, in collaboration with IIT Madras, has launched the SWAYAM 
Plus platform. The platform offers skill related courses in collaboration with industry partners, helping 
learners reskill, upskill, and become employment ready. This platform offers more than 500 employability-
focused courses. These courses have been curated from more than 80 industry partners across 15 sectors, 
including Information Technology, Artificial Intelligence, Semiconductor Manufacturing, BFSI, 
Healthcare, and Advanced Manufacturing etc. More than 06 lakh learners have enrolled on SWAYAM Plus 
platform for their Skill augmentation.  
The Ministry of Education implements the National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS) to 
impart on-the-job training and enhance the employability of students of AEDP, graduates and diploma 
holders. Currently, apprentices are undergoing apprenticeship training in various sectors such as IT/ITeS, 
Automobile and Auto components and BFSI, among others. At present, 17,625 establishments are 
registered under NATS across the States/UTs in various sector. In the year 2025-26 more than 5 lakh 
apprentices enrolled and completed under the NATS.A recent third-party evaluation of the NATS stated 
that 74% of trainees engaged in employment after the apprenticeship. 
Union Budget 2026-27 has announced setting up of 5 University Townships in the vicinity

entries.t: Industrial Pollution in Ramganga River, Uttar Pradesh
entries.head:
OIH 
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3545 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Industrial Pollution in Ramganga River, Uttar Pradesh 
3545. MRS RUCHI VIRA: 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether any assessment has been conducted to evaluate industrial pollution affecting the 
Ramganga River in Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh, if so, the details thereof;  
(b) whether any investigation has been conducted into heavy metal contamination caused by metal 
processing industries; 
(c) if so, the details thereof and the action taken against the industrial units found responsible 
during the last five years; and  
(d) whether any river restoration programme has been prepared for the Moradabad stretch of the 
Ramganga River? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE 
CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
(a) to (d): Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) monitors water quality of aquatic resources in 
the country in association with the State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs)/ Pollution Control 
Committees (PCCs) at 4922 locations including 2265 locations on rivers under National Water 
Quality Monitoring Programme (NWMP), to regularly assess status of water quality of water 
resources to facilitate prevention and control of pollution in water bodies.  
 
Ramganga River is presently being monitored at three locations under NWMP, including one 
monitoring location each at Bijnor, Pauri Garhwal and Farrukhabad.The water quality data under 
NWMP is utilised for identification of Polluted River Stretches (PRS), the location / stretches of 
rivers that are not meeting the Primary Water Quality criterion for outdoor bathing for 
Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) parameter (indicator of organic pollution) are identified as 
polluted location/ stretches. The PRS are classified under Priority Class I to V, Priority I being 
most polluted and Priority V least polluted.  
 
Under NWMP, in 2018, CPCB identified total 351 PRS including one PRS of Ramganga river 
from Muradabad to Kannauj in Uttar Pradesh under Priority class IV (BOD 6 mg/L – 10 mg/ L).  
The comprehensive action plans including plan for Industrial pollution control were prepared for 
bringing the water quality of polluted river stretches to the quality level fit for bathing purposes 
(i.e. BOD ˂ 3 mg/L). Progress of implementation of action plans is reviewed by the River 
Rejuvenation Committees (RRC) at State level and Central Monitoring Committee (CMC) 
constituted under the Chairmanship of Secretary, Ministry of Jal Shakti at Central Level. With 

concerted efforts, the total number of PRS in 2025 has been reduced to 296, which include one 
PRS of Ramganga river from Kalagarh to Bijnaur under Priority class IV. 
 
Further, CPCB organizes annual inspection of Grossly Polluting Industries (GPIs) operating in 
river Ganga and Yamuna main stem States having potential to discharge into river Ganga & its 
tributaries, by joint teams of officials from third party technical institutes and State Pollution 
Control Boards/ Pollution Control Committees (SPCBs/PCCs) since 2017. Inspection also 
includes the GPIs discharging into river Ramganga. The Online Continuous Effluent Monitoring 
Systems (OCEMS) are installed by Grossly Polluting Industries (GPIs) in the country as per 
directives issued by CPCB. Based on the alerts generated from OCEMS, CPCB also conduct 
surprise inspection of selected industries. 
As informed by CPCB, Grossly Polluting Industries (GPIs) in the Metal Processing sector located 
in Moradabad were inspected by joint team from third-party technical institutes and concerned 
SPCB. During 2021 and 2022, no Metal Processing units has been listed under GPI category in 
Moradabad District. However, 55, 51 and 23 Metal Processing units were found to be non-
compliant during inspections conducted in 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively. Out of the total 129 
non-compliant units, Show Cause Notice has been issued to 124 units and 05 units have been 
closed. 
****

entries.t: Preservation and Protection Measures for Rushikulya River Estuary
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3546 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Preservation and Protection Measures for Rushikulya River Estuary 
 
3546. DR. PRADEEP KUMAR PANIGRAHY: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of specific conservation and monitoring measures undertaken by the Government to 
protect the sensitive coastal eco-system of the Rushikulya River estuary, particularly for the mass 
nesting of Olive Ridley sea turtles; 
(b) the details of funds allocated and utilized under the Integrated Coastal Zone Management 
(ICZM) project in Odisha during the last three years; and 
(c) whether any technical studies have been conducted on the impact of coastal climate change along 
the Ganjam coast and if so, the details thereof along with the mitigation strategies adopted? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
(a)  Management and protection of wildlife including Olive Ridley turtles is carried out by the 
concerned States and Union Territories. During the Olive Ridley turtle nesting season, the Forest 
Departments, in coordination with relevant stakeholders, undertake various measures for the 
protection of turtles, which include seasonal restrictions on mechanised fishing in nearshore waters, 
patrolling, surveillance in coordination with the Indian Coast Guard and Fisheries Department, 
besides curtailing public access to nesting beaches to minimize disturbance. In addition, regular 
monitoring of nesting activity, hatchling emergence and turtle strandings are also undertaken, along 
with awareness generation and community participation programmes. 
The Zoological Survey of India and Wildlife Institute of India have undertaken scientific studies, 
including flipper tagging and satellite telemetry, to assess turtle movement ecology and habitat use, 
thereby supporting scientific conservation and management of Olive Ridley turtles. 
(b) The Integrated Coastal Zone Management (ICZM) Project implemented in the State of Odisha 
ended in 2020. 
 
(c) The Ministry has not undertaken any specific study on the impact of coastal climate change 
along the Ganjam coast.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO - 3547 
ANSWERED ON – 10/08/2026 
  
LOW EMPLOYMENT RATE UNDER PMKVY 
  
†3547. SHRI NEERAJ MAURYA: 
            SHRI DEVESH SHAKYA: 
            SHRI BABU SINGH KUSHWAHA: 
            SHRI LALJI VERMA: 
  
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to 
state:- 
  
(a) the main reasons for 22 lakh youth dropping out midway from their training under 
the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) between the years 2015 and 2022; 
  
(b) whether out of 1.10 crore certified youth, only 23 lakh could secure verified placements, 
and the reasons for 87 lakh youth not getting employment even after receiving training; 
  
(c) the reasons for the extremely low employment rate of about 21 percent, along with the 
reasons for the failure of the massive budgetary amount spent on these 87 lakh youth; 
  
(d) the fundamental changes the Government proposes to bring into its policy to 
ensure hundred percent employment as per industry demands in the future, rather than 
merely distributing paper certified to the youth including its impact on Jaunpur Lok Sabha 
Constituency; 
  
(e) whether the Government is considering to develop a more effective placement system 
for youth by linking skill training to employment as per industry demand in the country, including 
the Etah-Kasganj Lok Sabha Constituency; 
  
(f) whether the Government proposes to make policy improvements to strengthen skill 
training in accordance with the demand of industries, mandatory placement, apprenticeship and 
monitoring of employment after training and if so, the details thereof; and 
  
(g) the assessment made by the Government regarding the low employment rate under the 
said scheme and the accountability fixed to ensure the effectiveness of public funds spent on 
training?  
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
  
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
  
(a)       Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) has been successfully 
implementing its flagship scheme, Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), since 2015 
to impart skill development training through Short -Term Training (STT) and up -skilling and re-
skilling through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) to youth across the country. The objective 
is to enhance the employability of youth by equipping them with industry-relevant skills. 
  

Under PMKVY, a real-time dashboard has been developed on the Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) 
to monitor key training indicators, including enrolment, attendance, training progress, and 
dropouts. According to SIDH data, a total of 5,22,538 candidates were re ported as dropouts 
under PMKVY during FY 2015 –16 to FY 2021 –22. Candidate dropouts occur due to various 
reasons such as academic examinations, seasonal employment opportunities, early placement 
offers, migration, and personal circumstances.  
  
(b)&(c)     Under PMKVY scheme, placements were tracked in the Short -Term Training (STT) 
component in the first three versions of the Scheme - PMKVY 1.0, PMKVY 2.0 and PMKVY 3.0, 
implemented from FY 2015 -16 to FY 2021 -22. In these versions of PMKVY, out of 56.89 lakh 
candidates that have been certified in STT, 24.3 lakh candidates have been reported placed 
which makes the overall placement rate at 42.8%.  
 
Further, MSDE’s flagship scheme PMKVY was evaluated by NITI Aayog in October 2020 across 
several states. As per the study, about 94% of the employers surveyed reported they would hire 
more candidates trained under PMKVY. Further, 52% of the candidates who were placed in full 
time/part time employment and oriented under the RPL component received higher salary or felt 
that they will get higher salary compared to their un-certified peers. 
 
A third-party impact evaluation of PMKVY was also conducted by the Indian Institute of Public 
Administration (IIPA). As per the evaluation, about 70.5% surveyed candidates received 
placement in their desired skill sector. 
  
(d), (e)&(f)  The Government has undertaken various measures to strengthen the linkage 
between skill development and employment opportunities under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal 
Vikas Yojana (PMKVY). Under PMKVY 4.0, training is being imparted in industry -relevant and 
future-ready job roles developed in consultation with industry -led bodies and aligned to the 
requirements of emerging sectors such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Robotics, Mec hatronics, 
Drone Technology and other Industry 4.0 domains. 
 
To ensure better alignment of training with labour market requirements, District Skill 
Development Plans (DSDPs) are prepared by District Skill Committees (DSCs) to identify local 
skill gaps and employment opportunities. Training programmes under PMKVY are  planned 
keeping in view industry demand and local economic potential. The Skill India Digital Hub

REDESIGNING OF PMKVY COURSES 
  
3548. SHRI KALI CHARAN SINGH: 
  
            Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP  
be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government proposes to redesign and update Pradhan Mantri Kaushal 
Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) courses to meet the skill requirements of emerging sectors such as 
Artificial Intelligence, semiconductors, electronics, green energy, electric vehicles,  drones, 
cybersecurity, robotics and advanced manufacturing and if so, the details thereof; 
  
(b) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of post -
certification employment, job retention and placement outcomes of candidates trained under 
PMKVY and if so, the details and findings thereof; 
  
(c) the number of candidates trained, certified and secured employment under the PMKVY 
during the last three years and the current year, State/UT-wise, year and sector-wise;

(a) Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) has been implementing its 
flagship scheme Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), since 2015, for imparting 
skill development training through Short-Term Training (STT) and up-skilling and re-skilling 
through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL), to all sections of the society. Under PMKVY 
4.0 which is under implementation since FY 2022 -23, the focus is on imparting training in 
emerging and new-age courses such as Artificial Intelligence, semiconductors, electronics, 
green energy, electric vehicles, drones, cybersecurity, robotics, etc., as per the industry 
requirement. To meet emerging technology demands, 600+ new-age and futuristic courses 
have been introduced. As on 30.06.2026, around 5.44 lakh candidates have been trained in 
new-age and futuristic job roles under PMKVY 4.0 across the country.

3.0, implemented from FY 2015-16 to FY 2021-22. In these versions of PMKVY , out of 56.89 
lakh candidates that have been certified in STT, 24.37 lakh candidates were reported placed 
which makes the overall placement rate at 42.8%. Under PMKVY 4.0 which is u nder 
implementation since FY 2022 -23, the focus is to empower trained candidates to choose 
their varied career path and they are suitably oriented for the same through On-Job Training 
(OJT) embedded industry relevant skill courses. 
  
PMKVY was evaluated by NITI Aayog in October 2020 across several states. As per the

will get higher salary compared to their un -certified peers. Also, a third -party impact

Administration (IIPA). As per the evaluation, about 70.5% surveyed candidates received 
placement in their desired skill sector.

Institute of Financial Management (AJNIFM) in 2025 observed that PMKVY training has led 
to a measurable improvement in employment outcomes for Short -Term Training (STT) 
candidates, with the combined share of employed and self -employed respondents 
increasing from 26.6% prior to training to 45.4% post-training, reflecting a significant rise of 
18.8 % points. Moreover, 41.4% of STT candidates and 48.9% of RPL candidates reported 
an increase in income following PMKVY training and certification.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO-3549 
ANSWERED ON-10.08.2026 
 
Status of Implementation and Utilisation of the ONOS Scheme 
 
3549. Shri Abhishek Banerjee: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of institutions eligible, onboarded and actively using the One Nation One 
Subscription (ONOS) platform, State-wise and institution-category-wise; 
(b) the details of the number of registered users, active users, logins, full-text downloads and failed 
access attempts recorded under ONOS, institution-wise and publisher-wise; 
(c) the details of the amount paid or committed to publishers under the ONOS initiative, publisher-
wise and year-wise; 
(d) the number of eligible institutions that have not been onboarded under ONOS, as well as the 
number of onboarded institutions that have recorded no usage along with the reasons therefor; 
and 
(e) whether the Government has conducted any audit to assess duplication with pre-existing 
institutional subscriptions, under-utilisation, access denial or disparities in usage between 
Central institutions and State universities under ONOS and if so, the details thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) & (b): The One Nation One Subscription (ONOS) scheme was launched in January 2025 
for a period of three years. The scheme envisages country-wide access to scholarly research 
articles and journal publications to all Higher Educational Institutions (HEIs) of Central 
government, HEIs of State Government and Research & Development (R&D) Institutions of 
Central government. Details of institutions onboarded, registered users, full-text downloads 
state-wise and institution-category-wise and publisher-wise full-text downloads is available at 
https://www.onos.gov.in/   
(c): The details of the amount paid to publishers under ONOS, publisher-wise and year-wise is 
given at Annexure. 

(d): All Higher Educational Institutions (HEIs) of Central government, HEIs of State 
Government and Research & Development (R&D) Institutions of Central government are 
eligible to access ONOS. The onboarding of these institutions is an ongoing process. As of 
now, 6,215 eligible institutions have successfully been onboarded under ONOS. To address 
issues such as dela in onboarding and lower usage, the Government of India, through the 
Information and Library Network Centre (INFLIBNET), has launched several initiatives to 
promote awareness and enhance utilisation of the scheme nationwide. These include 
conducting special lectures and organising webinars with nodal officers at the institutional 
level. In addition, offline awareness sessions have been delivered in collaboration with 
universities to reach institutions with limited digital access. To provide continuous support, 
INFLIBNET also regularly uploads Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) to resolve queries and 
facilitate smoother adoption of ONOS. 
(e): The ONOS Scheme has integrated earlier initiatives of various Ministries and Departments, 
which previously subscribed to library consortia individually to provide access to research 
publications. This consolidation was undertaken to eliminate duplication of expenses and 
streamline access under a single comprehensive scheme. Access to ONOS is granted to eligible 
institutions possessing a unique AISHE code. The scheme ensures equitable access, with no 
issues of under-utilisation, denial, or disparities in usage.

3550.      SHRI M MALLESH BABU: 
   
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has considered the findings of the Youth 
Well-being Index 2025 highlighting that nearly 23 per cent of the 
youth population below 35 years in Karnataka is outside

thereof;

employment opportunities, career guidance, labour market

initiatives supported by the Government in Kolar;

youth unemployment, migration for employment, women's workforce

MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE)

are derived from the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), conducted by 
the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation since 2017–18.  
 
 

 
As per latest PLFS report 2025, the estimated percentage of 
persons not in employment, education or training (NEET) on usual status 
was 17.1% for persons of age 15 -24 years, 20.8% for persons of age 15 -
29 years and 23.2% for persons of age 30 -59 during the year 2025 in the

Further, the estimated Worker Population Ratio (WPR) indicating

Also, the estimated UR for youth of age 15 -29 years has decreased

State of Karnataka. 
 
Further, Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India, 
is running the National Career Service (NCS) Portal which is a one -stop 
solution for providing career related services including jobs from private 
and government sectors, information on online & offline job fairs, job

PROMOTION OF INDIAN CLASSICAL DANCES AMONGST STUDENTS 
 
†3551.  SHRI GYANESHWAR PATIL 
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether the Government has issued any directions to include various forms of Indian 
classical dances in the school curriculum in the country, especially in Madhya Pradesh; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; 
(c)  whether the Government has started any scholarship for meritorious students of schools in 
Indian classical dances; 
(d)  if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(e)  the details of funds utilized by the Government for promoting Indian classical dances 
among school students during the last five years, year-wise? 
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM 
(GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
(a)&(b) The Government promotes the inclusion of Indian classical dances in school education 
in alignment with the objectives of the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020, which 
emphasizes art-integrated, experiential and multidisciplinary learning. The Centre for 
Cultural Resources and Training (CCRT), an autonomous organization under the 
Ministry of Culture, conducts training programmes for teachers and students of 
Government and Government-aided schools incorporating Indian classical and folk-
dance traditions. In Madhya Pradesh, these programmes include dance forms such as 
Kathak, Rai, Matki, Karma and Grida. CCRT also has a Regional Centre at Damoh 
(Madhya Pradesh) for promoting local and regional art forms. 
  
Further, the Sangeet Natak Akademi organizes the Kala Dharohar series comprising 
lectures, workshops and performances to promote Indian performing arts among school 
children. 
  
(c)&(d) The Centre for Cultural Resources and Training (CCRT) implements the Cultural Talent 
Search Scholarship Scheme (CTSS) for meritorious students in the age group of 10-14 
years studying in recognized schools and children belonging to families practicing 
traditional performing arts. The Scheme provides specialized training in Indian classical 
dance and other cultural disciplines. Each scholarship holder receives ₹3,600 per annum 

along with reimbursement of tuition fees paid to the Guru/Teacher up to ₹9,000 per 
annum, subject to the Scheme guidelines. The scholarship is initially awarded for two 
years and is renewable based on satisfactory progress.

MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3552 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Plantation under CAMPA in Uttarakhand 
 
3552. SHRI ASADUDDIN OWAISI: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the total areas under Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority 
(CAMPA) plantation being planned by the Forest Department in Uttarakhand; 
(b) the  details of land category on which CAMPA plantations are being planned including the plant species 
planned for plantation; 
(c) whether the Annual Plan of Operations (APO) for implementation of CAMPA projects requires 
compliance with Forest Rights Act (FRA) as one of the stipulated conditions; and  
(d) if so, the details of process of consent undertaken, compliance of Forest Rights Act (FRA) and 
engagement of communities like Van Gujjars during the implementation of CAMPA projects? 
 
ANSWER 
 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE 
CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI V ARDHAN SINGH)  
 
(a) and (b): As per information received from the State Government of Uttarakhand, during the year 
2026-27, an area of 800 ha of land is being taken up for plantation. 
 
The land for raising compensatory afforestation (CA) is identified in accordance with the provisions of 
the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Rules, 2023, which provides that compensatory afforestation 
shall be undertaken over non-forest land or degraded forest land. Accordingly, compensatory 
afforestation is carried out on land identified and approved as part of the approval granted by the Central 
Government under the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980, and in accordance with 
the provisions of the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016, and the Rules and guidelines made 
thereunder. The Government of Uttarakhand has informed that both non-forest land and degraded forest 
land are being identified for raising compensatory afforestation using indigenous tree species. These 
plantations comprise a mix of timber, fuelwood, fodder, fruit-bearing, medicinal and other locally 
suitable species. 
 
(c) and (d): The Annual Plan of Operations (APO) for implementation of activities under the 
Compensatory Afforestation Fund is prepared and implemented in accordance with the Compensatory 
Afforestation Fund Rules, 2018. As per rule 5 of the said Rules, activities undertaken on forest land are 
carried out in consultation with the concerned Gram Sabha or Village Forest Management Committee, 
as the case may be, and in consonance with the provisions of the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional 

Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, and the guidelines issued thereunder, 
wherever applicable, by the respective State Governments/UT Administrations.

Rojgar Yojana (PMVBRY), to promote employment generation, enhance 
employability, and strengthen social security across all sectors including 
MSMEs, with a particular focus on the manufacturing sector. The scheme 
has a registration period of two years from 01.08.2025 to 31.07.2027 and 
a budgetary outlay of ₹99,446 Crore for the period FY 2025-26 to FY 2031-
32. 
  The scheme comprises two parts, i.e. Part A and Part B, and 
focuses on providing support to both employees and employers by way of 
incentives. 
   Under Part A of the scheme, the first -time employees of both 
existing and new establishments shall be eligibl e for an incentive 
equivalent to one month’s EPF wage, subject to a maximum of ₹15,000. 
This incentive will be payable in two instalments during the first year of 
employment. The first instalment, up to ₹7,500, shall be disbursed after 
completion of six mo nths of continuous employment. Eligibility for the 
second instalment shall arise after completion of twelve months of 
employment and successful completion of the prescribed Financial 
Literacy Programme. This second instalment shall be credited to an 
appropriate savings instrument/savings account for a specified period.  
   Part B incentivizes employers by providing up to ₹3,000 per 
month for each additional employment sustained for at least 6 months for 
two years , with extended benefits for another two year s for the 
manufacturing sector.  
   The scheme aims to incentivise creation of more than 3.5 Crore 
jobs all across the country, over a period of 2 years. The scheme provides 
for incentives for 1.92 crore eligible first -time employees under Part A. 
Incentive for the creation of approximately 2.59 crore additional jobs to 
employers is provided for under Part B of the scheme. 
  Comprehensive Scheme Guidelines, outlining the eligibility 
criteria for incentives to both employees and employers, have been 
issued. The scheme and its provisions have been widely disseminated 
through extensive outreach efforts across the country. 
  A dedicated portal (pmvbry.epfindia.gov.in) has been 
developed to facilitate all scheme -related processes and for real -time 
monitoring of beneficiaries and sector-wise progress. 
  For effective implementation of the scheme, a robust 
monitoring framework has been instituted. A steering Committee with 
representation from various labour -intensive and related 
Ministries/Department and an internal Executive Committee have been 
constituted to ensure effective monitoring of the scheme.

since the implementation of the Scheme, a total of 99,92,924 first

Protection and Monitoring of Saplings 
 
3554. SHRI AJENDRA SINGH LODHI:  
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
 (a) whether the Government is aware that despite large-scale tree plantation drives in various 
States, the expected increase in forest cover is not being achieved due to tree felling and 
inadequate protection of saplings; 
(b) if so, the details of survival rate of saplings planted across the country during the last three 
years, State-wise; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to implement any new action plan for the protection and 
monitoring of saplings as well as for controlling illegal felling to ensure the effectiveness 
of tree plantation drives; and  
(d) if so, the details thereof?  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (d): The Government accords high priority to the conservation, protection, restoration and 
enhancement of forests and tree cover in the country, in accordance with the applicable legal 
and policy framework. Increase in forest and tree cover is a gradual ecological process 
influenced by several factors, including local climatic and edaphic conditions, species 
characteristics, genetic potential, silvicultural practices, protection from biotic and abiotic 
disturbances, and the age and growth stage of plantations. The outcomes of these afforestation 
and restoration interventions become evident gradually over time. As per the India State of 
Forest Report 2023, the total forest and tree cover of the country has increased by 1445.81 km2 
as compared to the last assessment of 2021. 
 
Further, conservation of natural forests and restoration of degraded forest landscapes are 
undertaken through assisted natural regeneration, artificial regeneration, Compensatory 
Afforestation under the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980 and the 
Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016, the Green India Mission, Nagar Van Yojana, 
MISHTI and other afforestation and restoration programmes. The approved operational 
guidelines of these programmes provide for site-specific species selection, plantation 
maintenance, protection measures during the prescribed maintenance period and periodic 
monitoring by the implementing agencies. 
 
Protection of forests against illegal felling and other forest offences is primarily the 
responsibility of the respective State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. 
Action in this regard is taken by States/UTs under the provisions of the applicable forest and 
other relevant laws. Similarly the survival of plantations is monitored by the respective 
implementing agencies and State Governments as part of scheme implementation and project 

monitoring. The State-wise database on the survival rate of saplings across all afforestation 
programmes is not maintained centrally by the Ministry.
