entries.t: Insurance Claim Repudiation and Consumer Protection
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
DEPARTMENT OF FINANCIAL SERVICES 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 3556 
ANSWERED ON MONDAY, AUGUST 10, 2026/SHRAVANA 19, 1948 (SAKA) 
Insurance Claim Repudiation and Consumer Protection 
 
3556. SHRI SRIBHARAT MATHUKUMILLI: 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) Whether the Government is aware of instances of insurance claims being rejected or delayed 
on grounds arising from ambiguous or unclear policy terms, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) The number and value of insurance claims repudiated in the country during each of the last 
five years, along with the number subsequently overturned by the Insurance Ombudsman, 
consumer forum or courts, State-wise particularly in Andhra Pradesh, including Visakhapatnam; 
(c) Whether the Government has assessed the financial impact of unjustified claim repudiation 
on policyholders and families, if so, the details thereof, particularly in Andhra Pradesh and 
Visakhapatnam; and 
(d) The steps being taken by the government to ensure clear and standardised policy language, 
prevent arbitrary claim repudiation, strengthen accountability of insurers, and provide timely 
grievance redressal to affected policyholders? 
 
ANSWER  
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a): Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) monitors policyholder 
grievances relating to repudiation of insurance claims and delay in settlement through analysis 
of regulatory returns submitted by insurers, supervisory reviews and complaints registered on the 
Bima Bharosa Portal. Based on such analysis, IRDAI undertakes appropriate regulatory, 
supervisory and follow-up measures, wherever necessary.   
Rejection or delay generally arise due to several factors, including  non-disclosure or 
misrepresentation of material facts, incomplete, inaccurate or inconsistent documentation, 
exhaustion of the sum insured, non-fulfilment of policy conditions, applicability of waiting period, 
fraud investigations, delays in completion of loss assessment surveys, judicial proceedings in the 
case of Motor Third Party claims, and delay in submission of records or other information by 
hospitals, garages and other entities. 
(b): The data on insurance claims repudiated is maintained by IRDAI at the aggregate level and 
is not maintained State-wise or city-wise. A detail containing data of claims repudiated during last 
5 years is at Annexure-I.  The state-wise data on Reason for Grievance referred to Insurance 
Ombudsman, including any partial or t otal repudiation of claims by an insurer, as received from 
Council of Insurance Ombudsman Office is attached as Annexure-II.  

 
 
 
(c) and (d):  IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations, 2024 and t he IRDAI (Protection of 
Policyholders' Interests, Operations and A llied Matters of Insurers) Regulations, 2024  require 
Insurers to use clear, simple and policyholder-friendly language in policy documents, disclose all 
key features, benefits, exclusions and terms through prospectuses, provide proposal forms and 
policy documents in simple language (including scheduled languages, wherever feasible), offer 
a 30-days free-look period, publish a Citizens' Charter specifying service standards, timelines 
and grievance redressal mechanisms, ensure fair and timely settlement of cla ims. Health 
insurance claims can not be repudiated without approval of the Product Management Committee 
(PMC) or Claims Review Committee (CRC) and where delay occurs in settlement of claim, the 
insurer is required to pay penal interest. If the customer is not satisfied with the service of the 
insurer they may approach Insurance Ombudsman for redressal.  Any delay in honouring the 
award of the Insurance Ombudsman attracts a penalty of ₹5,000 per day.  
In addition, the complaints can also be registered on Centralised Public Grievance Redress and 
Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) portal of the Government of India, which is monitored regularly 
from the appropriate level in Department of Financial Services (DFS) for redressal of grievances 
registered.  
These measures are applicable uniformly across the country, including Andhra Pradesh.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3557 
ANSWERED ON MONDAY, 10 AUGUST 2026/SHRAVANA 19, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
UPI-Favara Integration Scheme 
 
3557. SHRI ANTO ANTONY: 
            
 
 
           Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) -Favara Integration Scheme signed  between 
India and the Maldives, including its salient features; 
(b) the present status of the project and the time by which it is expected to become fully  operational; 
and 
(c) whether the scheme is likely to enable Indian nationals working in the Maldives to transfer  their 
salaries to India through it and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (c) The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has informed that an agreement was signed in July 2025 between 
NPCI International Payments Limited (NIPL) and the Maldives Monetary Authority (MMA) to integrate 
India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI) with the Maldives’ fast payment system, Favara. Such integration 
facilitates real-time cross-border person-to-person (P2P) remittances between the two countries. Further, it 
provides instant credit to beneficiaries’ accounts, 24x7 availability, and real -time payee validation. The 
facility became operational on July 30, 2026 for remittances from the Maldives to India and enables Indian 
nationals working in the Maldives to transfer money to India subject to applicable transaction limits and 
regulations.

CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY INVESTMENT NORMS 
Question 
 
3559. Shri Tanuj Punia: 
Will the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has introduced major amendments to the Corporate Social 
Responsibility (CSR) investment norms to allow companies to directly invest their CSR 
funds, in Non-Profit Organisations (NPOs) listed on the Social Stock Exchange (SSE); 
 
(b) if so, the details thereof along with the primary objective behind this move; 
 
(c) whether investments made by companies under these revised norms are likely to 
be treated as valid CSR expenditure under Schedule VII of the Companies Act, 2013, if 
so, the details thereof; and 
 
(d) whether the Government has conducted any assessment regarding the extent to 
which this policy intervention is likely to boost the inflow of institutional capital into 
the social sector and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS  AND MINISTER OF 
STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
                                                                                      [SHRI HARSH MALHOTRA] 
 
(a) to (c): Yes Sir. The Ministry has vide notification dated 27.05.2026 widened the 
ambit of Schedule VII of the Companies Act, 2013 (‘Act’)  by introduction of new item 
no. (xiii) namely “Subscription to zero coupon zero principal instruments on Social 
Stock Exchange." As per the said amendment, the CSR mandated company shall not 
subscribe to ZCZP instrument for more than ten percent of the total CSR expenditure 
for that financial year. This amendment is aimed at providing significant ease of 
compliance to the companies and will also help Not for Profit Organisations to raise 
funding for public welfare projects in a transparent and regulated manner. 
 
(d) No such assessment has been conducted by the Ministry.

entries.t: Illegal Tree Felling and Forest Conservation
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3560 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Illegal Tree Felling and Forest Conservation 
 
3560. DR. AMAR SINGH: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the increasing incidents of illegal tree felling in various 
parts of the country; 
(b) the details of  number of cases of illegal tree felling reported during the last five years, 
State/UT-wise, along with the action taken against the offenders; 
(c) whether the Government has assessed the impact of such illegal felling on forest cover, 
biodiversity and climate resilience and if so, the details thereof; 
(d) the details of measures taken by the Government to strengthen monitoring, surveillance, and 
enforcement to prevent illegal tree felling, including the use of technology; and 
(e) whether the Government proposes to introduce any new schemes or policy measures to 
enhance afforestation, community participation and protection of forests and if so, the details 
thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (e): Instances of illegal tree felling are reported from time to time from different parts of 
the country. The protection and management of forest and tree resources are primarily the 
responsibility of the respective State Governments and Union Territory Administrations, which 
take appropriate action under the provisions of the Indian Forest Act, 1927, Van (Sanrakshan 
Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980, and the respective State Forest Acts, Tree Preservation 
Acts and Rules. The instances regarding the illegal felling of trees as and when detected are 
booked by the respective State Governments/UT Administrations under the relevant Acts and 
proceeded against the offenders before the competent authorities. The details in this regard are 
maintained by the concerned State Governments/UT Administrations.  
 
The Ministry through Forest Survey of India carries out biennial assessment of forest and tree 
cover of the country through the India State of Forest Report (ISFR) using satellite-based remote 
sensing and field-based ground truthing. As per the India State of Forest Report-2023 published 
by the Forest Survey of India, Dehradun, the forest cover and tree cover in the country have 
increased by 156.41 square kilometers and 1289.40 square kilometers respectively, as compared 
to the assessment published in ISFR-2021. Illegal tree felling may adversely affect forest 

ecosystems, biodiversity and the ecological functions of forests. The impact of specific incidents 
is dealt with by the concerned State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. 
  
The Ministry provides technical and financial support to the States and Union Territories 
through various schemes and programmes of the Central Government for increasing forest 
and tree cover, including protection, conservation and sustainable management of forests in 
the country. These include, inter alia, the National Mission for a Green India (GIM), Nagar 
Van Yojana (NVY), Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats and Tangible Incomes 
(MISHTI), Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority 
(CAMPA), Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats, and forest fire prevention and 
management schemes. 
  
Further, the plantation campaign "एक पेड़ माँ क े नाम (#Plant4Mother)", launched on the occasion 
of World Environment Day 2024 and continued during the current year, promotes plantation 
activities across the country, through a "Whole of Government" and "Whole of Society" 
approach with participation of all stakeholders for increasing the green cover. 
  
The Ministry issues advisories to States/UTs to protect forests and trees as per the provisions of 
the law including prevention of illegal logging. Measures taken include survey and demarcation 
of forest land, boundary pillars, regular patrolling, legal action under extant laws and community 
participation through Joint Forest Management Committees. 
 
*****

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
                  MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
                 LOK SABHA 
                     UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3561 
            TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
 
             Rising Wild Animal Attacks 
 
3561. ADV. ADOOR PRAKASH: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of rising human casualties in escalating wild animal attack 
in many States including Kerala; 
(b) whether the Union Government has received request from States including Kerala to make 
necessary amendments in the relevant sections of the Wildlife Protection Act to address the 
escalating man-animal conflict; 
(c) if so, the details thereof and the response of the Union Government thereto; 
(d) whether the Union Government is aware that the State of Kerala has passed a Bill to amend the 
Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 to address the rising human-animal conflict in the State, if so, the 
response of the Government thereto; and 
(e) whether the Union Government is likely to convene a meeting of the State Forest Ministers to 
review the situation and prepare a national plan considering the severeness of the issue, if so, the 
details thereof? 
 
       ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a):  Incidents of human-wildlife conflict have been reported from various parts of the country, 
including Kerala. Management of wildlife and mitigation of human-wildlife conflict are primarily 
the responsibility of the respective State Governments/Union Territory Administrations, which 
maintain details of such incidents and the species involved. 
 
(b) to (e): The Ministry received the “Wild Life Protection (Kerala Amendment) Bill, 2025”, for 
amendment of certain provisions of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972, which was not agreed to, 
as the existing provisions of the Act already provide a regulatory framework for addressing human-
wildlife conflict.   
     
The Ministry engages with the State Governments/ Union Territory Administrations including with 
the State Forest Ministers/public representative on the issue and has recently set up Centre of 
Excellence for Human–Wildlife Conflict Management at the Salim Ali Centre for Ornithology and 
Natural History (SACON), WII–South India Centre, Coimbatore, to strengthen the scientific and 
institutional framework for managing human–wildlife conflict and also launched the Human 
wildlife conflict portal as the national repository for human-wildlife conflict incident data and as a 
decision-support tool.                                                   
*****

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA

TO BE ANSWERED ON 10TH AUGUST, 2026 
 
STATUS OF EMPLOYMENT IN BHUBANESWAR LOK SABHA 
CONSTITUENCY 
 
3562.      SMT. APARAJITA SARANGI: 
   
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of total number of registered unemployed youth in the 
Bhubaneswar Lok Sabha Constituency as on June 2026; 
(b) the details of steps taken by the Government to boost local job 
creation in the said Constituency; 
(c) the details of central welfare schemes currently implemented for 
the safety, health and social security of unorganised and migrant 
construction workers in Khordha district; and 
(d) whether the Government plans to establish a new National Career 
Service (NCS) Centre or mega -skill hub in Bhubaneswar to bridge 
the industry -academic employability gap and if so, the details 
thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (d): Official estimates of employment and unemployment in India 
are derived from the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), conducted by 
the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation since 2017–18.  
 
As per latest PLFS report 2025, the estimated Unemployment Rate 
(UR) for youth of age 15 -29 years has decreased from 17.2% in 2022 to 
10.6% in 2025 in the State of Odisha (including Bhubaneswar Lok Sabha 
Constituency). 
 
Further, the estimated Worker Population Ratio (WPR) indicating 
employment on usual status for persons of age 15 years and above has 
increased from 55.1% in 2022 to 61.3% in 2025 in the State of Odisha 
(including Khordha district of Bhubaneswar Lok Sabha Constituency). 
 

 
Employment generation coupled with improving employability is a 
priority of the Government. Accordingly, Government is implementing 
various employment generation schemes/ programmes in the country 
(including Khordha district of Bhubaneswar Lok Sabha Constituency). 
The details of various employment generation schemes/ programmes 
being implemented by the Government may be seen at   
https://dge.gov.in/dge/schemes_programmes.  
 
Additionally, Government is also implementing Skill India Mission 
(SIM) to deliver skill, re -skill and up -skill training through an extensive 
network of skill development centres/ schools/ colleges /institutes etc. 
under various schemes, viz. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 
(PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship 
Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) 
through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) in the country. The SIM aims 
at enabling youth of India to get future ready, equipped with industry 
relevant skills. 
 
The Ministry of MSME launched Udyam Registration Portal on 
01.07.2020 for formalizing enterprises, expanding access to government 
support and strengthening the MSME ecosystem. A total of 8.9 crore 
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) have been registered on 
Udyam Registration Portal, including Udyam Assist Platform (UAP), 
providing employment to over 39 crore people across the country. 
 
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has 
initiated ‘FutureSkills PRIME’ a programme for Re -skilling/Up-skilling of 
IT Manpower for Employability in 10 new/emerging technologies 
including Artificial Intelligence. 
 
Also, the Government is implementing Employment Linked 
Incentive (ELI) Scheme named as the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat 
Rozgar Yojana to support employment generation, enhance employability 
and social security across all sectors, with special focus on the 
manufacturing sector. The scheme with an outlay of Rs 99,446 Crore 
aims to incentivize the creation of more than 3.5 Crore jobs in the 
country, over a period of 2 years.  
 
 
 

Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India, is 
running the National Career Service (NCS) Portal which is a one -stop 
solution for providing career related services including jobs from private 
and government sectors, information on online & offline job fairs, job 
search & matching, career counselling, vocational guidance, information 
on skill development courses, skill/training programmes etc. through a 
digital platform [www.ncs.gov.in]. Government has approved 407 Model 
Career Centres across the country including 32 in the State of Odisha.

E-SHRAM REGISTRATION IN BAHRAICH AND GONDA DISTRICT 
 
3563. SHRI KARAN BHUSHAN SINGH: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a)the details of the number of unorganised sector workers registered 
on the e-Shram portal, based on district-wise data from July 2023, 
in the Bahraich and Gonda districts of Uttar Pradesh; 
(b)the details of number among the said workers whose registration 
has been verified and updated during the year 2024 and 2025; 
(c)whether an assembly constituency -wise breakup of the said 
registrations is maintained and if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(d)the details of the steps being taken by the Government to improve 
registration and profile -updation among migrant and agricultural 
workers in the said districts? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (d): The Ministry of Labour and Employment launched eShram 
portal (eshram.gov.in) on 26 thAugust, 2021 for creation of a 
comprehensive National Database of Unorganised Workers (NDUW) 
including platform workers, migrant workers etc. The eShram portal 
registers the unorganised workers including gig and platform workers 
and provides them a Universal Account Number (UAN) on a self -
declaration basis. 
 
  Over 31.84 crore unorganised workers have already been 
registered on eShram portal including 8.46 crore unorgan ised 
workers in Uttar Pradesh. 
 
  Since July 2023, a total of 48,532 unorganised workers 
have been registered in Bahraich district and 22,595 unorganised 
workers have been registered in Gonda district. 
 
Contd..2/- 

:: 2 :: 
  In the eShram portal, registrati ons are undertaken only 
after successful Aadhaar -based eKYC authentication. This process 
ensures that duplicate or fraudulent registrations are effectively 
eliminated. Further, key fields such as Name, Gender, Date of Birth, 
Permanent Address, and Photograph are directly fetched from UIDAI 
to maintain data authenticity and accuracy. These measures 
collectively safeguard the integrity of the portal and prevent any 
misuse. 
 
  The eShram portal contains State/UT-wise and district -
wise details of registrations of unorganised workers across the 
country. Further, the details are also available occupation-wise, 
gender-wise, and age-wise on eShram portal. 
 
  To enhance registrations under the eShram initiative and 
ensure wider coverage of u norganised workers, including migrant 
and agricultural workers, across all States/UTs, including the 
Bahraich and Gonda districts of Uttar Pradesh, the Government has 
adopted a comprehensive strategy. In addition to enabling self -
registration through the web portal and mobile application, assisted 
registration modes have been introduced via Common Service 
Centres (CSCs), State Sewa Kendras (SSKs), and the UMANG 
platform to facilitate easy access for workers. eShram also allows 
provisions where registered wo rkers can update their profiles 
through eShram portal or Common Service Centres (CSCs).  The 
Ministry of Labour and Employment is conducting targeted 
awareness campaigns comprising registration drives, community 
outreach programs and locally tailored commun ication efforts. To 
further strengthen outreach, the Ministry leverages social media 
channels to disseminate videos, tutorials, and other informative 
content, making the initiative more accessible and engaging. 
 
  To further enhance the availability and ac cessibility of 
eShram and its associated services to unorganised workers, the 
Ministry of Labour and Employment officially launched the eShram 
mobile application on 24th February 2025. This application facilitates 
real-time access to welfare schemes integr ated with the eShram 
platform, thereby significantly strengthening both accessibility and 
user convenience.

entries.t: Impact of Rising Inflation on Household Consumption
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
DEPARTMENT OF ECONOMIC AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3564 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026/ Shravana 19, 1948 (Saka) 
Impact of Rising Inflation on Household Consumption 
3564. Dr. Raj Kumar Chabbewal: 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether the Government has taken note of the recent Monthly Economic Review, which observed that 
inflation developments warrant continued vigilance and that household consumption may face headwinds, 
if so, the details thereof; 
(b)  whether the Government is aware that retail inflation has recently exceeded the Reserve Bank of India's 
medium-term inflation target, if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether the Government has assessed the impact of rising food, fuel and wholes ale prices on household 
purchasing power and private consumption, if so, the details thereof;  
(d)  the details of the fiscal measures proposed or undertaken by the Government to protect low and middle -
income households from inflationary pressures; and 
(e)  whether the Government proposes to review indirect tax rates on essential commodities in view of the 
prevailing inflationary outlook and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a): The May 2026 edition of the Monthly Economic Review  stated that “… overall consumption demand 
may face headwinds in the coming months” as the forecasts at that time were pointing “…to a below-normal 
monsoon and a likely moderation in economic activity ”. The statement, “The inflation outlook warrants 
vigilance”, was made against the backdrop of a hike in pump prices of petrol and diesel in mid-May, as well 
as the possibility of some pass-through of upstream cost pressures, as signalled by the build-up in wholesale 
prices consequent to the war in West Asia. 
(b): The average retail inflation had declined steadily from 5.4 per cent in 2023 -24 to 2.1 per cent in 2025 -
26. However, owing to the commodity price shock and elevated global energy prices stemming from the 
West Asia Crisis and the expected unfavourable El Niño conditions, retail inflation rose to 4.38 per cent in 
June 2026, still within the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI)  inflation target of 4±2 per cent. The quarterly 
average for Q1 of 2026-27 stands at 3.9 per cent, which is below the inflation target of 4 per cent and RBI’s 
earlier forecast of 4.2 per cent for the said quarter.  

(c) and (d): The wholesale inflation rate declined from 1.7 per cent in 2024 -25 to 0.4 per cent in 2025 -26, 
but rose to 9.3 per cent in Q1 of 2026-27 owing to the global supply shock . Though the retail inflation also 
followed a similar path, the price pressures at retail level were much moderate and stable. The recent uptick 
in retail inflation  was largely driven by the unfavourable weather conditions that were exerting upward 
pressure on food inflation, especially on prices of protein-rich foods and select vegetables. The fuel inflation 
was relati vely modest, reflecting only a partial transmission of elevated global fuel prices to the energy 
commodities at the retail level. In Q1of 2026-27, the food and fuel inflation were 4.8% and 1% respectively. 
The Government continuously monitors the price sit uation in the country and undertakes fiscal, 
administrative and supply -side measures, as warranted by evolving economic conditions, to protect the 
purchasing power of households, particularly low- and middle-income households. Some of the recent fiscal 
measures include, reduction of Basic Customs Duty (BCD) on crude palm oil, crude soybean oil and crude 
sunflower oil from 20 per cent to 10 per cent in June 2025; on whole Tur to Nil with effect from 4 March 
2023; extension of duty rationalization for the imp ort of Tur and Urad under the 'Free Category' till 
31.03.2027; reduction of Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess (AIDC) on Masur to Nil from 13 
February 2022 to 7 March 2025; distribution of food grains free of cost to around 81 crore beneficiaries under 
the National Food Security Act;  reduction in the Central excise duty on petrol and diesel by ₹10 per litre in 
March 2026; rationalisation of the Goods & Services Tax (GST) rates in September 2025, especially on items 
consumed by the common man, such as food products, household articles, medicines, medical equipment, 
agricultural goods and specified automobiles etc. ; and increasing the disposable income of individuals by 
exempting annual incomes up to ₹12 lakh (and ₹12.75 lakh for salaried individuals with standard deduction) 
from income tax. These measures have supported household consumption, as evidenced by the share of 
private final consumption expenditure in GDP remaining broadly stable at 56.5 –56.7 per cent (base year 
2022-23). Moreover, as p er the latest GDP estimates released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme 
Implementation, per capita Private Final Consumption Expend

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO-3565 
ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Expected Years of Schooling 
 
3565. Shri Balashowry Vallabhaneni: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether it is true that Expected Years of Schooling in the Russia is 15 years whereas the expected 
years of schooling in India is 13.37 years, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether it is also true that labour productivity in the Russia is US $44.31 per hour whereas labour 
productivity in India is just US$10.68; 
(c) if so, the details of the efforts made by the Government to increase the expected years of schooling 
and labour productivity and by when India is going to touch Russia figures in years of schooling and 
labour productivity; and 
(d) expected increase in investment in education, especially school education combined with job-
oriented skilling, to push productivity into human capital for faster economic growth? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (d): Enhancement of expected years of schooling, labour productivity and skills of workers is 
continuous and dynamic process. The Government recognizes that improving learning outcomes, 
reducing school dropouts and addressing curriculum gaps are important for enhancing employability and 
workforce readiness. The National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 envisages a holistic transformation of 
the education system through foundational literacy and numeracy, competency-based learning, 
experiential education, multidisciplinary learning and greater integration of Skill Education to equip 
learners with the knowledge, skills and competencies required for higher education, employment and 
lifelong learning. 
 
At the school level, Skill Education has been integrated as a regular component of education 
under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Samagra Shiksha. NSQF-aligned skill courses are offered to 
students of Classes IX-XII to enhance employability skills including communication, self-management, 
Information and Communication Technology (ICT), entrepreneurship and green skills. In line with NEP 
2020, students of Classes VI-VIII are provided pre-vocational exposure through Bagless Days, 
internships with local vocational experts and experiential learning. The Government has also promoted 
digital learning through platforms such as DIKSHA, SWAYAM, SWAYAM PRABHA and Virtual Skill 
Laboratories, while PM SHRI Schools emphasize experiential learning, digital infrastructure and skill 
development. 
 
Also, Central Government assist States and UTs through the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of 
Samagra Shiksha and hot cooked meal provided from Balvatika to class 8 under Pradhan Mantri Poshan 
Shakti Nirman (PM POSHAN) Yojna. Financial assistance/grant is also provided to the States and UTs 
for various activities to reduce dropout and increase enrolment in Government schools, which include 
opening/strengthening of new schools up to Senior Secondary level, strengthening school infrastructure, 
setting up and up gradation and running of Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas (KGBV) upto class 12, 
setting up of residential schools/hostels named Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Avasiya Vidyalayas, hostels 
under Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN) and Dharti Aaba Janjatiya 
Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA), transport allowance, undertaking enrolment drives, seasonal 
hostels/residential camps, provision of vocational education and ICT facilities in schools, providing free 
text books and free uniform, transport/escort facility, etc.

entries.t: Impact Assessment of Diversion of Mhadei River
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3566 
                                        TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026  
 
Impact Assessment of Diversion of Mhadei River 
 
3566. SHRI CAPTAIN VIRIATO FERNANDES: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government  has undertaken or commissioned any independent environmental, 
ecological or cumulative impact assessment of proposed diversion of Mhadei River and if so, the 
details and findings thereof; 
(b) whether the Government has examined concerns raised by environmental experts, scientific 
institutions and civil society regarding likely impact of the proposed diversion on forests, 
biodiversity, river ecology, groundwater, estuarine salinity, drinking water availability in Goa, and 
risk of deforestation, desertification and ecological degradation in the Khanapur and Belagavi 
regions of Karnataka and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government has assessed likely impact of the proposed diversion on the Mandovi 
river basin, including saline ingress, freshwater aquifers and drinking water security in Goa; and  
(d) if so, the details thereof and the mitigation measures, safeguards and monitoring mechanisms 
proposed or directed by the Government  before permitting any diversion of Mhadei River? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (d) River diversion projects involving hydroelectric power generation and/or major or medium 
irrigation components require prior Environmental Clearance (EC) under Item 1(c) of the Schedule 
to the Environment (Impact Assessment) Notification, 2006, as amended. The Notification provides 
a detailed procedure for appraisal and assessment of anticipated environmental impacts viz. loss of 
biodiversity, impact on river ecosystem, impacts on forests, environmental flows, groundwater and 
water quality, associated with the river valley projects.  Study of the aforesaid and other related 
factors in the context of specific/individual project forms the basis for preparation of the 
Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA)/Environmental Management Plan (EMP).  
 
The Expert Appraisal Committee (EAC) comprising domain area experts, after detailed examination 
and deliberations on various environmental and social aspects of the project including possible 
environmental impacts of river valley and hydro-electric projects on the biodiversity, river ecology, 
groundwater, estuarine salinity, risk of deforestation, desertification, downstream water availability 
etc. in the river basin, recommend the project for grant of Environmental Clearance (EC) by 
suggesting suitable mitigation measures to minimize the environmental and social impacts 
associated with the project. It is only after such detailed study and analysis that environmental 
clearances are issued subject to compliance of necessary environmental safeguards and general and 
specific conditions by the Project Proponent before undertaking construction of the project.  
 

As per the procedure prescribed by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change 
(MoEF&CC), the concerned State Government is required to identify and furnish the details of river 
basins where a Cumulative Impact Assessment and Carrying Capacity Study (CIA&CCS) is 
required to be undertaken. The findings of such studies are taken into consideration by the Expert 
Appraisal Committee (EAC), wherever applicable, during the environmental appraisal of River 
Valley and Hydroelectric Projects for the grant of Environmental Clearance (EC) within the 
concerned river basin. In case such projects involve Inter-State rivers, clearance from Central Water 
Commission/ Inter-State River Water Dispute Tribunal is also required. No proposal or details in 
this regard have been submitted by the concerned State Government for the Mhadei/Mandovi river 
basin. Further, no proposal seeking Environmental Clearance for any river diversion project 
involving the Mhadei/Mandovi river is presently under consideration in the Ministry.

and full withdrawal of provident fund  balances and pens ion

(b)whether the Government has received representations or

(a) & (b): EPFO has introduced a 12 -month waiting period for 
premature final EPF settlement and a 36 -month waiting period for

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION  
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION AND LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO - 3568 
ANSWERED ON – 10/08/2026 
 
Vacancies of Teachers in Schools of Uttar Pradesh 
 
3568. Shri Rajeev Rai: 
 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of teachers serving in Government primary, middle and high schools in Uttar 
Pradesh as on 1 April 2014; 
(b) the number of teachers who have retired since 2014, year and category-wise; 
(c) the number of teachers recruited during the same period, year and category-wise; 
(d) the number of sanctioned, filled and vacant teaching posts as on date; and 
(e) whether the Government considers the present level of vacancies adequate to maintain the 
prescribed pupil-teacher ratio and if so, the details thereof?  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a)  to (e):    Education being a subject in the Concurrent List of the Constitution, the majority of 
schools in the country are under the administrative control of the respective State Governments 
and Union Territory Administrations. Accordingly, the recruitment, service conditions and 
deployment of teachers fall within the administrative domain of the concerned States/UTs. 
Teacher vacancies arise from time to time due to factors such as retirement, resignation, 
creation of new posts, rationalisation of teacher deployment and changes in enrolment. The data 
relating to sanctioned strength, teachers in position, vacant teaching posts and 
recruitment/retirement of teachers, including State/UT-wise, and level-wise details, is 
maintained by the respective State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. 
 
 As per the UDISE+, the details of teachers in position in Government schools in the 
state of Uttar Pradesh is as below: 
 
Year Primary Upper 
Primary  
Secondary Higher 
Secondary 
Total

2025-26 340103 259477 7025 20519 627124 
 
 
 The Central Government periodically advises States/UTs to fill vacant posts through 
transparent and merit-based recruitment processes, including through autonomous teacher 

recruitment boards or similar mechanisms. The progress of recruitment is regularly reviewed 
through meetings and advisories, with emphasis on competitive selection, consistency and 
technology-based teacher requirement planning and forecasting. 
 
 Further, the Central Government provides financial assistance to States/UTs under 
Samagra Shiksha to maintain appropriate Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) at various levels of 
schooling in accordance with the norms prescribed under the Right of Children to Free and 
Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009. 
 
 As per UDISE+ 2025-26 report, the PTR at National level   stands at 19 at Primary 
level, 17 at Upper Primary level, 15 at Secondary level, and 23 at the Higher Secondary level, 
while PTR at State level for the State of Uttar Pradesh stands at 19 at Primary level, 21 at Upper 
Primary level, 23 at Secondary level, and 33 at the Higher Secondary level, which is within the 
norms envisaged under NEP 2020.

SPECIAL FINANCIAL PACKAGE FOR MANIPUR 
 
3569. PROF. ANGOMCHA BIMOL AKOIJAM: 
 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government has formulated or proposes to formulate any special financial 
package for the State of Manipur in view of the prolonged humanitarian and economic 
crisis; 
(b) if so, the details thereof, including the amount sanctioned, components of the package 
and the timeline for implementation; 
(c) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of the financial requirements 
for the rehabilitation of internally displaced persons, restoration of livelihoods, 
reconstruction of damaged public infrastructure and revival of the State's economy; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (d): The Ministry of Finance has, under Special Assistance to States for Capital 
Expenditure/Investment (SASCI) scheme, approved an additional allocation of Rs. 700 crore 
for 105 projects to the State of Manipur during the year 2025-26, of which an amount of Rs. 
310.66 crore was released to the State as 1st installment. However, no proposal was received 
from State of Manipur for release of the 2nd instalment of additional allocation. 
 
The Scheme has been continued in the current financial year as well with an enhanced overall 
allocation of Rs. 2 lakh crore. A special window, namely Part-X: “Pride of Hills”, has been 
introduced under the scheme for the year 2026–27 under which an amount of ₹25,000 crore 
has been allocated for the current financial year to address the special needs of Hill States. In 

addition to capital expenditure, funds under this component may also be utilized for essential 
revenue expenditure. Accordingly, an amount of ₹2400 crore has been earmarked for Manipur 
under this component. This is over and above the funds available to the State under the Untied 
Part (Part-I) and other Parts of SASCI 2026–27.

Moreover, the Government of India is also providing substantial financial resources to State

recommends the quantum of devolution of central taxes & duties and grants to be made to 
States and the inter-se share of States in the devolution. Based on the recommendations of the

Jammu and Kashmir. Further, the 16th Finance Commission has also continued the 41%

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
 LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3572 
ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
National Centre of Excellence 
 
 
†3572. Smt. Sandhya Ray: 
 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has formulated any policy to set up National Centre of Excellence 
(NCE) in every Parliamentary Constituency of the country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof along with such centres proposed to be set up in Madhya Pradesh 
including Bhind and Datiya; and 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (c): The Government has framed the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020, which aims to 
promote research and innovation in higher education ecosystem. It envisages an active role for 
higher education institutions in conducting research in disruptive technologies, including Artificial 
Intelligence (AI). 
 
In line with this vision, the Government has established four Centres of Excellence (CoEs) in 
Artificial Intelligence (AI); one each in the domain of Education, Healthcare, Sustainable Cities 
and Agriculture at IIT Madras, IISc Bengaluru, IIT Kanpur and IIT Ropar respectively. These AI-
CoEs are designed to collaborate with academia, industry, startups and state governments. 

In addition, the Government has approved the IndiaAI Mission under the guiding principles of 
"Make AI in India" and "Make AI Work for India", fostering innovation, indigenous capabilities, 
and inclusive AI-driven solutions for socio-economic development. Under the IndiaAI Startup 
Financing pillar, a scheme for establishment of 58 AI Centres of Excellence (AI-CoEs) has been 
approved in collaboration with industry partners and State/UT Governments including Madhya 
Pradesh. 
 
Further, the Government has launched PM-SETU (Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability 
Transformation through Upgraded ITIs), a centrally sponsored scheme with an investment of 
Rs.60,000 crore. The PM-SETU scheme aims to enhance the overall quality and relevance of 
vocational training in the country. The Scheme has two components: under Component I, 
upgradation of 1,000 Government ITIs is envisaged and under Component II, establishment of five 
National Centres of Excellence for skilling are envisaged at Bhubaneswar, Chennai, Hyderabad, 
Kanpur and Ludhiana. The PM-SETU Scheme is being implemented across all States/UTs, 
including Madhya Pradesh. 
 
Additionally, Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship (MSDE) has released the 
guidelines for recognition of Centres of Excellence (CoE) under Skill India. Under this initiative, 
institutions having permanent and best-in-class infrastructure can be empanelled as CoE-skills 
across the country including in Madhya Pradesh. These CoE-Skills aim to enable better training 
outcome and stronger integration among skill development & education as envisaged under NEP 
2020.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

DEVELOPMENT OF TOURISM AND HERITAGE CIRCUIT IN DHANBAD 
 
†3575.  SHRI DULU MAHATO: 
 
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government proposes to develop the Dhanbad Lok 
Sabha Constituency as a  major eco -tourism and heritage circuit 
(such as Maithon and Panchet Dams, Topchanchi Lake,  Bhatinda 
Waterfall and the ancient temple located at Jinshi Hill) apart from 
its identity as 'coal capital'; 
(b) whether any proposal is under consideration to provide -financial 
assistance for the  infrastructure, beautification and security 
arrangements of these major natural and historical  tourist 
destinations of Dhanbad under the 'Swadesh Darshan 2.0 or 
Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual Heritage Augmentation Drive 
(PRASHAD) scheme;  
(c)  whether any funds have been sanctioned and allocated by the 
Central Government for  promoting tourism in Dhanbad during the 
last three years, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the details of immediate steps taken/being taken by the 
Government to bring Dhanbad on  the national tourism map and to 
create new employment opportunities for the local youth? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM       (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (d): The development and promotion of tourist destinations and 
tourism products, is primarily undertaken by the respective State 
Government and Union Territory (UT) Administration. However, the 
Ministry of Tourism, under its various schemes such as Pilgrimage 
Rejuvenation and Spiritual Heritage Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD) , 
Swadesh Darshan (SD), Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD2.0), Challenge Based 
Destination Development (CBDD) supplements the efforts of the 

States/UTs by providing financial assistance for the development of 
tourism related infrastructure and experiences across the country, 
including in the State of Jharkhand. 
 
No proposal regarding development of  Dhanbad Lok Sabha 
Constituency as a  major eco -tourism and heritage circuit (such as 
Maithon and Panchet Dams, Topchanchi Lake,  Bhatinda Waterfall and 
the ancient temple located at Jinshi Hill ) is presently under 
consideration. 
 
However, r eceiving proposals from the State Governments and 
Union Territory Administrations for financial assistance for tourism 
projects is a continuous process. The proposals received are examined 
with reference to the prescribed guidelines and financial assistanc e is 
extended for such projects subject to fulfilment of the stipulated 
conditions and availability of funds. 
 
The development of tourism infrastructure through the above -
mentioned Schemes is ensured in a holistic manner with the objective 
of promoting regional tourism and generating local employment.

Disinvestment and Asset Monetisation 
 
3577.  Shri Naveen Jindal: 
 
Will the Minister of Finance be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the disinvestment target set for 2025-26 and the amount actually 
realised; 
(b) the details of the Public Sector Units (PSUs) where disinvestment is proposed 
in 2026-27; and  
(c) the progress made under the National Monetisation Pipeline? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a):  As per Revised Estimates during FY 2025-26, an amount of Rs. 33,837 crore 
was kept under Miscellaneous Capital Receipts, which includes estimated receipts 
on account of management of equity investments and monetization of public assets 
through various mechanisms.   Government of India realized an amount of Rs. 
45,306.05 core in FY 2025-26, which included Rs 16,885.56 crore from 
disinvestment and Rs. 28,420.49 crore from Asset Monetization. 
 
(b): For Budget Estimates 2026-27, Rs. 80,000 crore has been kept under 
Miscellaneous Capital Receipts. Government of India has realized an amount of Rs. 
27,568.06 crore as on 05.08.2026, which included Rs 21,201.13 crore from 
disinvestment through Offer for Sale of Central Bank of India, Coal India Ltd, NHPC 
Limited, NLC India Limited, General Insurance Corporation of India, Indian Railway 
Finance Corporation Ltd. & Cochin Shipyard Ltd as well as strategic disinvestment of 
Indian Medicines Pharaceuticals Corporation Ltd and Rs. 6,366.93 crore from Asset 
Monetization. Further that, disinvestment is an ongoing process and 
execution/completion of specific transactions hinges upon market conditions, 
domestic and global economic outlook, geopolitical factors, investor interest and 
administrative feasibility and given the market-sensitive nature of the disinvestment 
transactions, drawing up timeline for disinvestment is not feasible. 
 
 

 
 
(c): The National Monetisation Pipeline 1.0 included assets with monetisation 
potential of Rs. 6 lakh crore during the period (2021-22 to 2024-25), against which 
around Rs. 5.3 lakh crore was achieved. Pursuant to the announcement made in the 
Union Budget 2025-26, the National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0 (NMP 2.0) was 
launched on February 23, 2026. NMP 2.0 estimated an aggregate monetization 
potential of Rs. 16.72 lakh crore, including private sector investment of Rs 5.8 lakh 
crore during the five-year period from FY 2026 to FY 2030. NMP enables recycling 
of productive public assets, thereby unlocking resources for reinvestment in new 
projects and capital expenditure.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

                             UN-STARRED QUESTION NO. 3578 
                 TO BE ANSWERED ON MONDAY, 10th August, 2026 
 
Women in Corporate Leadership 
 
3578. Ms. Sayani Ghosh: 
 
Will the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the number of women serving as Chairpersons, Chief Executive Officers 
(CEOs), Managing Directors, Executive Directors, Independent Directors, Chief 
Financial Officers (CFOs), Chief Technology Officers (CTOs) and Board 
Members in the top 500 listed companies, category-wise; 
(b) whether the Government has assessed the representation of women in 
senior corporate leadership and the major barriers affecting their progression, 
if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government has reviewed compliance with statutory 
requirements relating to women directors, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) the measures taken by the Government to promote women's participation 
in corporate leadership and board-level decision-making; and 
(e) whether any targets, incentives or policy interventions are under 
consideration of the Government to improve gender diversity in corporate 
governance and if so, the details thereof?                                             
 
ANSWER 
 
Minister of State in the Ministry of Corporate Affairs; Minister of State in the 
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways;  
 
                                                                             (Shri Harsh Malhotra) 
                                                                                                      
(a) Section 2 (51) of the Companies Act, 2013  (the Act)  defines the Key 
Managerial Personnel (KMP) of a company, which include the Chief Executive 
Officer (CEO), Managing Director (MD) or Manager, Company Secretary (CS), 
Whole-time Director (WTD), Chief Financial Officer (CFO) , such other officer  
not more than one level below the Directors who is in whole-time employment 
designated as key managerial personnel by the Board.  
The provisions of the Act recognize and use the term "Chairperson" but do not 
define the position of Chairperson. Further, the Act also does not define the 

position of Chief Technology Officer (CTO). Therefore, the Ministry does not 
maintain data on Chairperson, Chief Technology Officers (CTOs) in the MCA21 
database. 
Based on the information available in the MCA 21 database in respect of the 
top 500 listed companies on the basis of turn over, the category-wise details 
of women serving as Chief Executive Officers (CEOs), Managing Directors 
(MDs), Independent Directors (IDs), Chief Financial Officers (CFOs) and Whole-
time Directors (WTDs) are given at Annexure-A. 
(b) The term "corporate leadership" has not been defined under the Act. The 
measures taken by the Government to enhance women’s participation in the 
corporate board level decision making are provided in the  second proviso to 
section 149(1) of the Act read with rule 3 of the Companies (Appointment and 
Qualification of Directors) Rules, 2014, which states that every listed company 
and every unlisted public company having paid -up share capital of Rs. 100 
crore or more or having turnover of Rs 300 crores or more must appoint at 
least one woman director on its Board. 
Further as per Rule 3 of the Companies (Appointment and Qualifications of 
Directors) Rules, 2014, any intermittent vacancy of a woman director shall be 
filled-up by the Board at the earliest but not later than immediate next Board 
meeting or three months from the date of such vacancy whichever is later.  
 Furthermore, Rule 4 of the Companies (Appointment and Remuneration of 
Managerial Personnel) Rules, 2014 provides that a company may pay sitting 
fees to directors for attending meetings of the Board or Committees. The said 
Rule further provides that, in the case of Independent Directors and Women 
Directors, the sitting fee shall not be less than the sitting fee payable to other 
directors.  
As per the filings with the MCA, the total number of women directors 
associated with active companies is 11,60,933 and the total number of 
directors associated with active companies is 39,99,656. 
No such assessment regarding barriers to progression of Women Directors has 
been done by this Ministry. 
 
 
 

(c) Yes Ma’am. The details of action regarding noncompliance related to 
statutory requirements of appointments of women directors is given at 
Annexture B. 
(d) The measures taken by this Ministry to enhance women’s participation in 
the corporate board level decision making are provided in the reply to part (b) 
above.  
(e) In view of reply to part (b) above , no such specific policy intervention is 
under consideration of this Ministry.

OPERATIONALISATION OF THE INCOME TAX ACT, 2025 
3579.  SHRI PRAVEEN KHANDELWAL: 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has reviewed the preparedness for smooth operationalisation of the 
Income Tax Act 2025 with effect from 1 April 2026, including notification of simplified rules and 
forms and re-engineering of digital taxpayer systems; 
 
(b) if so, the details thereof, including the taxpayer awareness and transition support measures 
undertaken by the Government; 
 
(c) the details of the rule based automated processes introduced for small taxpayers, including 
lower or nil deduction certificates and the data on faceless assessments and appeals disposed of 
during the last three years, year-wise; 
 
(d) whether the Government has taken or proposes to take special outreach and facilitation 
measures for small traders and professionals in commercial hubs such as Chandni Chowk to help 
them transition to the simplified law and digital compliance; and 
 
(e) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a) (i) Income-tax Act, 2025 (“Act”) has replaced the Income -tax Act, 1961 and has come into 
force from 01.04.2026. Further, in order to ensure smooth transition and operationalisation of 
the Act, Income-tax Rules, 2026 (“Rules”) which replaced Income-tax Rules, 1962 were also 
notified on 20.03.2026 and has come into force from 01.04.2026. 
 
(ii) In order to ease the compliance, number of Income Tax Rules are reduced from 511 to 333 
and number of Income Tax Forms were reduced from 399 to 190. 
 
(iii) Further, to facilitate the seamless transition of taxpayers from the Income-tax Act, 1961 to the 
Income Tax Act, 2025, the Department  launched a nationwide awareness and  outreach 
campaign titled "PRARAMBH 2026" (Policy Reform  and Responsible Action for Mission  
Viksit Bharat). 
 

 
 
(iv) Digital Taxpayer Infrastructure has been upgraded with the ongoing efforts which are as 
under: 
a. New user -friendly Income Tax website was launched on March 2026 under 
PRARAMBH Initiative 2026. 
b. E-Forms utility development is under progress for the newly rolled out Income-tax Forms 
2026. 
(b) The taxpayer awareness and transition support measures undertaken under "PRARAMBH 
2026" are as follows:  
 
(i) Physical Outreach: A total of 304 physical outreach programmes were conducted across 
the country in English, Hindi, and various regional languages. Approximately 50,000 
taxpayers and stakeholders participated in these outreach programmes.  
 
(ii) Educational and Awareness Material : The Directorate developed and disseminated 
extensive multilingual educational material, including 12 brochures in English and 11 
regional languages (including Hindi) on newly introduced forms and procedures. More 
than 1.75 lakh copies of brochures and oth er publications were distributed through field 
formations and Aaykar Seva Kendras (ASKs).  
 
(iii) Digital Outreach: Technology-enabled communication was leveraged through QR code-
enabled brochures, providing access to digital explanatory content and Samvaad  video 
sessions. 
 
(iv) The Department also deployed the AI-enabled chatbot "Kar Saathi" to assist taxpayers in 
understanding the provisions of the Income Tax Act, 2025 
 
(c) Section 395(1) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 provides for issuance of certificate for deduction 
of tax at source at Nil or lower rates. Vide Finance Act, 2026, to ease the compliance burden of 
small taxpayers, an option has been enabled for the payee, to fil e the application for issuance of 
certificate for lower or nil deduction of income-tax electronically and the certificate may be issued 
or rejected electronically subject to fulfilment of conditions as may be prescribed. In this regard, 
the enabling rule is currently under preparation and shall be notified in due course.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3580 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
                                    National Plastic Waste Reporting Portal 
 
3580. SHRI RAJESH NARANBHAI CHUDASAMA:    
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the targets set under the initiative One Nation One Mission to end plastic pollution and the 
expected timeline for their achievement; 
(b) whether the Government plans to make the National Plastic Waste Reporting Portal mandatory 
for all local bodies and Panchayats, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the details of measurable impact of the plastic ban and recycling efforts since the introduction 
of Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) Guidelines; and 
(d) whether there is any penalty mechanism for non-compliance and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI V ARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) :  The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) celebrated World 
Environment Day 2025 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on 5th June 2025, with the theme ‘One 
Nation, One Mission: End Plastic Pollution’. As part of one month long pre-campaign activities 
undertaken before World Environment Day 2025, around 69,000 events were organized in which 
around 21 lakh people participated across the country. The World Environment Day 2025 saw the 
participation of members of industry, civil society, students and Government officers from States and 
concerned central Ministries, following the ‘Whole of Government’ and 'Whole of Society’ approach.  
 
The National Plastic Pollution Reduction Campaign (NPPRC), which had a series of planned 
activities was organized from 5th June 2025 to 31st October 2025. The Campaign included activities 
to reduce plastic pollution in urban and rural areas under “Swachhta Hi Sewa” programme. The 
activities also focussed on reducing use of avoidable single use plastics in government offices 
especially during Special Campaign 5.0. A Hackathon on eco-alternatives to single-use plastics was 
also organized by Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).  
 
(b)  As per Plastic Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2024, notified on 14th March, 2024, 
every urban local body and Panchayat at District Level shall prepare and submit annual report in the 
prescribed form online by the 30th June every year to the Urban Development Department and to 
Rural Development Department, respectively, and also to the State Pollution Control Board (SPCB) 
or Pollution Control Committee (PCC) concerned. The National Plastic Waste Reporting Portal was 
launched on 5th June 2025. The mandatory online submission of annual reports is a transformational 
step in moving away from multi step physical reporting.  
 
(c) MoEFCC notified Plastic Waste Management Amendment Rules, 2021, on 12th August 2021, 
prohibiting identified Single Use Plastic (SUP) items, which have low utility and high littering 
potential, with effect from 1 July 2022. The ban on identified single use plastic items has triggered 

development of innovative eco-alternatives. The “Compendium of Manufacturers / Sellers of Eco-
alternatives to Banned Single Use Plastic Items”, prepared by  MoEFCC was released on World 
Environment Day, 2025. It documents 1064 Manufacturers/Sellers of Eco-alternatives to Banned 
Single Use Plastic Items.  
 
65241 Producers, Importers and Brandowners and 3117 Plastic Waste Processors are registered on 
the Centralized EPR portal on plastic packaging. Since the notification of EPR Guidelines on plastic 
packaging on 16th February 2022, nearly 233 lakh tonne of plastic packaging waste has been 
recycled.  
 
(d) The Plastic Waste Management Rules has a specific provision for imposition of 
Environmental Compensation based upon ‘polluter pays’ principle. The CPCB has issued the revised 
Guidelines for Assessment of Environmental Compensation in August 2024. Regular enforcement 
drives have been undertaken to enforce ban on identified SUP items by CPCB/ SPCBs/PCCs along 
with local authorities across the country. As per details provided by SPCBs/PCCs and details available 
at SUP compliance monitoring portal, a total of 8,61,740 inspections have been conducted and 1985 
tonne of banned SUP items have been seized and a total of Rs. 19.82 crore of fine has been levied.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO - 3581 
ANSWERED ON – 10/08/2026 
 
 
Teachers Vacancies in Government Schools 
 
†3581. Shri Jaswantsinh Sumanbhai Bhabhor: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of sanctioned posts of teacher and those lying vacant out of them in Government 
schools of Dahod Lok Sabha Parliamentary Constituency under the Samagra Shiksha Scheme; 
(b) the steps being taken by the Government to address the shortage of teachers in this tribal 
dominated region; and 
(c) the number of teachers in said Constituency who have been imparted training in accordance 
with the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 during the last three years? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (c):    Education being a subject in the Concurrent List of the Constitution, the majority of 
schools in the country are under the administrative control of the respective State Governments 
and Union Territory Administrations. Recruitment, service conditions and deployment of 
teachers, including in backward and tribal areas, fall within the purview of the respective State 
Governments/UT Administrations. Teacher vacancies arise from time to time due to factors such 
as retirement, resignation, creation of new posts, rationalisation of teacher deployment and 
changes in enrolment. The data relating to sanctioned strength, vacant teaching posts is 
maintained by the respective State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. 
 
 
 The Central Government periodically advises States/UTs to fill vacant posts through 
transparent and merit-based recruitment processes. 
   
Financial assistance is provided under the Samagra Shiksha scheme, based on State-specific 
proposals, for in-service training of teachers, school heads, teacher educators, master trainers, 
resource persons and education administrators, including induction training of newly recruited 
teachers at elementary and secondary levels, including those in rural and remote areas. These 
training programmes are implemented through SCERTs and DIETs as nodal agencies.  
 
 As informed by the state of Gujarat, a total of 46244 teachers of Dahod Lok Sabha 
Constituency have been provided the prescribed training during period of three years from 2023-
24 to 2025-26.

entries.t: Technology Enabled Education for Children with Special Needs
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3582 
ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Technology Enabled Education for Children with Special Needs 
 
3582. Shri G Lakshminarayana:  
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the steps taken by the Government to promote the use of assistive technologies and digital 
tools for the education of Children with Special Needs (CWSN) in the country; 
(b) the details of schemes and initiatives supporting the development and deployment of 
assistive technologies, accessible digital content, adaptive learning platforms and inclusive 
educational infrastructure for CWSN; 
(c) the details of funds sanctioned, released and utilised for technology-enabled inclusive 
education since 2019, State-wise and year-wise; 
(d) the details of the number of Children with Special Needs benefitted through technology 
enabled educational interventions alongwith the number of schools equipped with assistive 
technologies in the country, State-wise, including district-wise details to Andhra Pradesh; and 
(e) the measures taken by the Government to improve teacher capacity, accessibility standards 
and availability of digital learning resources for Children with Special Needs, including 
collaboration with State Governments and specialised institutions to ensure equitable access to 
quality education? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (e) The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 is in consonance with the provisions of the 
Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016, that envisages providing an equitable and 
inclusive quality education for all children, including Children with Special Needs (CwSN).  
Education is a subject under the Concurrent List of the Constitution and the majority of 
schools are under the administrative control of the State Governments and Union Territory 
Administrations. To achieve universal access to education from pre-primary to Class XII, the 
Department of School Education & Literacy is implementing the centrally sponsored Samagra 
Shiksha scheme. Under the scheme funding support is provided to States/ UTs, based on the 

Annual Work Plan & Budget Proposals prepared by the States/UTs, which is appraised by the 
Project Appraisal Board in consultation with State/UT, funds are approved by the Department 
and released in lumpsum instalments to the States & UTs. The distribution of funds among 
districts, sanction of works and interventions, and implementation thereof are carried out by the 
respective State/UT Education Departments in accordance with their district level requirements, 
priorities and approved AWP&B. 
 Among the components of Samagra Shiksha there is a dedicated component on Inclusive 
Education for CwSN wherein financial assistance @ ₹3,500 per CwSN per annum is provided 
under the student-oriented component to cover aids and appliances, assistive devices, 
transportation, escort and scribe allowance, learning support such as Braille and large-print 
books, ISL based videos, learning materials, therapeutic services, and other support services.  
Distribution of aids, appliances and assistive devices under Samagra Shiksha is undertaken 
through the Assistance to Persons with Disabilities for Purchase/Fitting of Aids/Appliances 
(ADIP Scheme) which is implemented in convergence with the State/UT Education Departments 
and the Artificial Limbs Manufacturing Corporation of India (ALIMCO) under Department of 
Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD).  
 Individualized Education Plan (IEP), catering to the needs of each CwSN is prepared by 
the Special Educator at the Block/Cluster Resource Centres under Samagra Shiksha. 
NCERT, the Autonomous Body under the Department provides accessible learning 
content in audio, visual and multi-media format for children with visual and hearing impairment 
through the portals of DIKSHA, ePathshala and  PM eVidya channels.  Digital Infrastructure for 
Knowledge Sharing (DIKSHA) is the national digital platform for school education, providing 
curriculum-aligned e-content, including QR-coded Energised Textbooks (ETBs), teacher 
resources and other learning materials. The platform supports both online and offline access, 
enabling learners to download content and continue learning without internet connectivity, 
thereby ensuring wider and equitable access to quality educational resources.  
PM eVidya, launched on 17th May, 2020 as part of the Atma Nirbhar Bharat Abhiyaan, 
integrates digital, online and on-air education initiatives to enable multimode access to education 
across the country. States/UTs collaborate with NCERT to contextualize, monitor and evaluate 
these initiatives, while NCERT provides continuous academic support and guidance. A dedicated 
channel for the hearing impaired was launched under the PM e-Vidya initiative on 6th 
December, 202

National Dust Pollution Mitigation Mission 
3583. SHRI DHARAMBIR SINGH:  
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has examined the feasibility of launching a National Dust 
Pollution Mitigation Mission to address dust emissions from construction activities, rural 
roads, mining areas and open land across the country, if so, the details thereof;  
(b) whether standard operating procedures have been prepared for local authorities regarding 
scientific dust suppression, roadside plantation and real-time monitoring of particulate 
matter, if so, the details thereof;  
(c) the details of measures taken to provide financial assistance and technical support to States 
for implementation of dust control measures in non-attainment and rapidly urbanising 
districts; and  
(d) whether the Government proposes to undertake a comprehensive assessment of dust 
pollution in the Bhiwani–Mahendragarh Lok Sabha Constituency and implement 
appropriate mitigation measures? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
(a) to (d): Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) has issued ‘Guidelines on dust mitigation 
measures in handling construction material and C&D wastes’ in November, 2017 and these 
guidelines prescribe the dust mitigation measures during construction activities.  
CPCB issued directions on 20.12.2017 to all State Pollution Control Board/Pollution Control 
Committee (SPCBs/PCCs) to make the above mentioned guidelines to be part of the Consent 
management and direct Urban Local Bodies (ULB) to ensure compliance of these guidelines 
at construction sites in their jurisdiction.  
Building and Construction projects having ≥20,000 sq. m and <1,50,000 sq. m of built-up area, 
Townships and Area Development projects covering an area≥50 ha and/or built-up 
area≥1,50,000 sq. m, Mining Projects and Highway projects, as listed in the schedule to the 

EIA Notification, 2006, are required to obtain prior Environmental Clearance under the 
Environmental Impact Assessment Notification issued by Ministry of Environment, Forest and 
Climate Change (MoEF&CC) vide S.O. 1533(E) dated 14.09.2006. 
Further, SPCB/PCC grant Consent to Establish (CTE) and Consent to Operate (CTO) for 
Building construction projects, mining activities and highways and ensure compliance of 
implementation of pollution control measures under the Air (Prevention and Control of 
Pollution) Act, 1981 and the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974.  
Towards effective management and control of dust from the C&D activities through providing 
environmentally sound management of construction and demolition waste in the country, 
including its segregation, collection, recycling, treatment and disposal, and to discourage 
unscientific disposal, promote scientific waste management, prevent loss of recyclable value, 
and address pollution related issues emanating from dumping of such waste, Government of 
India notified Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2016 which was revised 
in 2025 and notified as Environment (Construction and Demolition) Waste Management Rules, 
2025. 
National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) emphasizes on source-specific mitigation measures 
through the implementation of city, state, and national-level Clean Air Action Plans. These 
plans focus on sectoral interventions such as road dust control, solid waste management, 
vehicular emissions, construction and demolition activities and industrial pollution. Action 
plans are prioritised by urban local bodies based on the identification of sources through 
scientific studies. Ministry of Environment Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) has issued 
the Guidance document for designing, construction and maintenance of urban roads and 
greening of traffic corridors for dust control under NCAP to be implemented by local bodies 
and road owning agencies. 
Air Quality Index (AQI) is disseminated on real-time basis in 292 cities. A centralised air 
quality portal and mobile app-SAMEER is functional for tracking and dissemination of near 
real-time air quality data and hourly Air Quality Index to the public.  
Performance based incentive grants of ₹16,423.56 Crore have been released to 130 cities across 
24 states/union territories for implementing City Clean Air Action Plans which includes action 
plan for implementation of dust control measures in NCAP Cities.  
Bhiwani and Narnaul (Mahendragarh District) in Haryana have prepared city action plans 
containing air quality improvement measures to address various sources of air pollution 
including road dust and construction & demolition activities. CPCB has sanctioned critical gap 
funding of ₹ 4.98 crore and ₹ 4.45 crore to Bhiwani and Narnau

assessment of the heritage, cultural and tourism potential of Mandawa, 
Fatehpur, Ramgarh, Sikar, Jhunjhunu, Churu and other historic towns in 
the Shekhawati region of Rajasthan, if so, the details along with its main 
findings; 
(b) whether the Government has prepared any special plan/scheme or is 
considering developing the said region as an integrated heritage 
tourism circuit and a national and international tourist center, if so, the 
details thereof along with financial provisions and current progress; 
(c) the details of fund approved and utilised by the Government on tourism 
development, heritage conservation, roads, lighting, tourist facilities 
and promotion in the said region during the last five years, year and 
district-wise; 
(d) whether the Government is implementing or has prepared any special 
plan for the conservation, restoration of the region's historic havelis, 
murals, historic buildings, forts, stepwells, chhatris and other cultural 
heritage and to promote local employment a nd economy through 
heritage tourism, if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) if not, whether the Government is considering coordinating with the

action plan? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM   (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 

(a) to (e): Development and promotion of tourism is primarily done by the 
concerned State Government (SG)/UT Administration (UTA). However, Ministry 
of Tourism under its various schemes such as Swadesh Darshan (SD), Swadesh

development of tourism infrastructure and experiences in the country, to th e

Guidelines of the Swadesh Darshan 2.0 scheme envisage development of

The Swadesh Darshan Scheme was initially designed for the integrated 
development of thematic tourism circuits. The same had been revamped as 
Swadesh Darshan 2.0 adopting a destination-centric approach with a focus on 
developing sustainable and responsible tourism destinations to enhance 
visitor experience and effective destination management. 
 
The details of the projects sanctioned under SD2.0 and SASCI schemes 
in the State of Rajasthan including projects at Sikar in the Shekhawati region 
is at Annexure. 
 
The tourism projects sanctioned in Rajasthan, including at Sikar, 
comprises need -based components such as parking and approach roads, 
tourist facilitation and interpretation facilities, toilets and other public 
amenities, pathways, landscaping, illuminatio n, signages and visitor -
experience facilities. The project DPRs are sanctioned as proposed by the 
State Government in accordance to the need of the tourist facilitated. 
 
Presently, no tourism project in Churu, Mandawa, Fatehpur, Ramgarh and
