entries.t: Student-Teacher Ratio in Government Schools in Dadra and Nagar Haveli
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION AND LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO: - 3585 
ANSWERED ON-10/08/2026 
 
Student-Teacher Ratio in Government Schools in Dadra and Nagar Haveli 
 
†3585. Smt. Delkar Kalaben Mohanbhai: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of habitations in tribal-dominated blocks of the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar 
Haveli where children do not have access to any Government primary or upper primary school 
within a radius of one kilometre and three kilometres respectively as per the mandatory provisions 
of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009; 
(b) the details of the Teacher-student Ratio in Government schools located in the tribal areas of the 
Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and the number of posts lying vacant out of the 
sanctioned strength; and 
(c) the details of the effective steps being taken or proposed to be taken by the Government to fill 
up the vacant posts at the earliest? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHOUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (c): Education is a subject in the Concurrent List of the Constitution and the majority of 
schools in the country are under the administrative control of the respective State Governments and 
Union Territory Administrations.  
As reported by the Union Territory of DD&DNH, there are no habitations in the tribal-dominated 
blocks of the Dadra and Nagar Haveli District where children are deprived of access to primary or 
upper primary schooling within the statutory neighborhood limits prescribed under the Right of 
Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009. As reported by the UT, the District 
has achieved 100% universal neighbourhood school coverage in compliance with the provisions of 
the RTE Act, 2009.  
Government schools in the Dadra and Nagar Haveli District maintain a student-teacher ratio of 1:30 
in accordance with the norms prescribed under the RTE Act, 2009. Recruitment of teachers is a 
continuous process, and vacancies arise due to factors such as retirement, promotion, resignation, 
opening of new schools and increased requirement of teachers due to growth in student enrolment.  
As reported by the UT, the Education Department of the Union Territory has completed the 
recruitment process for the posts of Post Graduate Teachers (PGTs), Trained Graduate Teacher 
(TGTs), and Primary and Upper Primary School Teachers pursuant to the recruitment advertisement 
dated 06.01.2024. Further, the recruitment process for 281 posts of Primary and Upper Primary 
School Teachers was advertised on 22.11.2025.

RATIONALISATION OF MANDATORY PUBLICATION OF FINANCIAL RESULTS IN 
NEWSPAPER 
 
3586. SHRI JAGANNATH SARKAR 
 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that under Regulation 47(1) and 47(4) of the Securities 
and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015, fr amed under Sections 11, 11A and 30 of the SEBI Act, 1992, listed 
companies are required to publish financial results in at least one English national daily and 
one regional language newspaper within forty -eight hours of approval by the Board of 
Directors, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government has examined the continued relevance of such mandatory 
newspaper publication requirements in the present digital era, when full financial statements 
are already made available on the company websites and stock exchange portals 
immediately after filing under Regulation 33, if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) whether the Government, in consultation with SEBI, intends to review or rationalise these 
delegated regulatory provisions to reduce compliance costs and op erational burden on 
companies, particularly in light of the QR -code-based and online disclosure mechanisms 
already prescribed and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a) to (c): Securities and Exchange Board of India ( SEBI) has informed that p rior to SEBI ’s 
amendment to the Regulation 47(1) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“LODR”), effective from December 13, 2024, every 
listed entity was required to publish detailed financial results in prescribed format in at least 
one English language national daily newspaper circulating in the whole or substantially the 

whole of India and in one daily newspaper published in the language of the region, where 
the registered office of the listed entity is situated within forty-eight hours of the conclusion 
of the meeting of Board of Directors at which financial results were approved . Pursuant to 
the amendment, which rationalised the publication requirement , listed entities are required 
to publish an advertisement only containing a Quick Response code (QR Code) and the 
details of the webpage where complete financial results of the listed entity is accessible to 
the investors. Pursuant to the amendment, publishing the detailed financial results in at least 
one English language national daily newspaper and in one daily newspaper published in the 
language of the region is made optional. The aforesaid advertisement containing QR Code  
and details of the webpage  is required to be published, within 48 hours of conclusion of 
Board meeting in which the financial results were approved. In terms of the Regulation 47(4) 
of the LODR, the aforesaid advertisement containing QR Code  and details of the webpage  
is required to be published in at least one English language national daily newspaper and in 
one daily newspaper published in the language of the region, where the registered office of 
the listed entity is situated. Further, this requirement is not applicable in case of listed entities 
which have listed their specified securities on Small and Medium Enterprises ( SME) 
Exchange.

entries.t: Financial Assistance to Lalit Narayan Mithila University
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3587 
ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Financial Assistance to Lalit Narayan Mithila University 
†3587. Shri Gopal Jee Thakur: 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether any financial assistance of approximately Rs. 100 crore has been sanctioned to 
Lalit Narayan Mithila University, Darbhanga under the Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha 
Abhiyan (PM-USHA) scheme; 
(b) if so, the details of the amount sanctioned, the amount released so far and the amount 
spent by the university, year-wise; 
(c) the details of buildings, academic infrastructure, laboratories, libraries, hostels, digital 
facilities and other development works constructed or upgraded in the university using the 
said amount; 
(d) the number of sanctioned projects that have been completed, those currently under 
construction and those pending along with the reasons for their pendency and the timeline 
for their completion; and 
(e) whether the Government is likely to conduct a review and audit of the utilization of the 
said Rs. 100 crore and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (e): The government has launched the third phase of Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha 
Abhiyan (RUSA) in June 2023 in the form of Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan 
(PM-USHA), with an outlay of Rs. 12,926.10 crore, including the committed liabilities of the 
earlier phases of RUSA, to cater to the needs of educationally unserved/ underserved 
areas. PM-USHA is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme aimed at funding specific State 
government Universities and Colleges, so as to improve their quality by ensuring their 
conformity to prescribed norms and standards. Under the Scheme, support is provided to 
States/UTs for strengthening infrastructure, including construction of hostels, academic and 
administrative buildings, laboratories and other facilities required for improving access and 
quality in higher education. The scheme has been further extended till 31st March, 2028, for 
completion of PM-USHA projects. 
 
 

Under PM-USHA, a total of 25 projects amounting to Rs. 388.85 Crore have been approved 
to the State of Bihar, including Lalit Narayan Mithila University (U-0068), Darbhanga, 
approved under the ‘Multidisciplinary Education and Research University (MERU)’ 
component of PM-USHA for a total amount of Rs. 100 Crore.  
 
With the funding support under PM-USHA, Lalit Narayan Mithila University has proposed for 
construction of G+3 Academic Block Building, Girls Hostel, Incubation and innovation Cell 
etc.; renovation of various science laboratories, Central Instrumentation Centre, etc.; 
acquisition of various IT products etc. for digital empowerment. 
 
As per the Monthly Progress Report (MPR) submitted by the University for the month of 
June 2026, the project has been reported as ongoing with 38% physical progress. In the 
current FY 2026-27, mother sanction amounting to Rs. 18.50 Crore has been issued to the 
State, for the utilization under various components. 
 
Education being in the Concurrent List, enhancing the quality of education is the 
responsibility of both the Central and State Governments. Under the scheme, as per the 
government rules and procedures, regular audit of the scheme is conducted at Central and 
State/UTs level. Based on the audited statements of expenditure of the various supported 
Higher Educational Institutions (HEIs), a consolidated Utilisation Certificate (UC) is sought 
from State/UTs for release of further grants to the State/UTs. The Centre and State 
Governments also reviews progress of works along with State Higher Education Councils 
(SHECs), through various review meetings, physical visits etc. under the scheme. 
Furthermore, under the scheme, funds are released through the SNA-SPARSH model for 
all States /UTs. Under the SNA-SPARSH model, funds are released ‘just in time’, and 
vendors and beneficiaries receive direct payments through daily sanction releases based 
on the submission of bills on the PFMS portal.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
DEPARTMENT OF FINANCIAL SERVICES 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 3588 
 
ANSWERED ON MONDAY, 10 AUGUST, 2026/SHRAVANA 19, 1948 (SAKA) 
Methodology adopted for CIBIL Score 
 
3588. SHRI SHAFI PARAMBIL: 
 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has reviewed the methodology adopted by Credit Information 
Companies, including Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited (CIBIL), for assigning credit 
scores, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government has received representations regarding irrational or 
disproportionate decline in credit scores despite timely repayment of loans, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(c) the details of complaints received and disposed of during the last five years; and 
(d) whether the Government proposes to introduce a regulatory framework to enhance 
transparency, accountability, consumer safeguards and independent review of credit scoring 
practices and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a) and (b): Credit Information Companies (CICs) function under the extant framework of Credit 
Information Companies (Regulation) Act, 2005 (CICRA), Credit Information Companies Rules, 
2006 (CIC Rules) and Credit Information Companies Regulations, 2006 (CIC Regulations). CICs 
are regulated and licensed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) under the CICRA. 
RBI has informed that the credit scoring models used by the CICs are proprietary in nature which 
are based on their respective experience in the business of credit information. CICs generate 
credit score of a borrower considering multiple factors, including but not limited to, recency and 
frequency of delinquency, debt level and payment history. RBI has not prescribed any 
methodology to be adopted by CICs for calculating credit scores.  However, with a view to 
facilitate the understanding and interpretation of credit scores in an easy and consistent manner, 
the extant RBI directions mandate that credit scores shall be calibrated from 300 to 900 by a CIC 
to enable common classification of credit scores. Further, in order to sensitize the public CICs 
have also uploaded on their website the knowledge material for improving the credit score. 
Score-related queries and complaints have been received by CICs from borrowers due to 
borrower's incomplete understanding regarding the methodology used to calculate credit scores. 
Borrowers may expect a higher credit score based primarily on timely repayments, however the 
credit score reflects a broader assessment of multiple credit -related factors and their interaction 
over time, including inter alia credit utilisation, credit exposure, balances, overdue, and historical 
credit behaviour. 

(c): As per RBI inputs, 15,093 complaints were received against the CICs during the period from 
FY 2022 -23* to FY 2025 -26. As on date, all such complaints have been disposed under the 
Reserve Bank Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021 (RB -IOS, 2021). ( *CICs were brought under the 
purview of RB-IOS, 2021 with effect from 1.9.2022) 
(d): In order to strengthen and enhance transparency, accountability, consumer safeguards and 
independent review of credit scoring practices provided by the credit institutions (CIs) and CICs, 
RBI has stipulated that the following measures be put in place by CIs and CICs. 
(i) All CIs are required to be members of all CICs and submit data to all of them. 
(ii) Standardized data formats have been prescribed for reporting of credit information to 
CICs by CIs under each of the three reporting segments – consumer, commercial and 
microfinance. 
(iii) With effect from 1.7.2026, RBI Directions require the CIs to submit credit information 
with greater frequency i.e. four times a month as against fortnightly reporting mandated 
earlier to CICs or at such shorter intervals as mutually agreed upon between the CI and 
CIC. 
(iv) CICs to send alerts through SMS/email to customers when their CIR is accessed by the 
Specified Users, wherever mobile number/email ID details of the customers are available. 
CIs to send alerts through SMS/email to customers while submitting information to CICs 
regarding default/days past due in existing credit facilities, wherever the mobile 
number/email ID details are available. 
(v) CIs to have a dedicated nodal point / official of contact for CICs for redressal of 
customer grievances. 
(vi) CIs to inform the customers regarding the reasons for rejection of their request for data 
correction, if any, to enable such customers to better understand the issues in the CIR. 
(vii) CIs to undertake Root Cause Analysis of the customer grievances at least on a half yearly 
basis. 
(viii) With a view to enable proactive detection of errors in credit reports and credit scores, if 
any, RBI has also mandated the CICs to provide access, upon request and after due

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
LOK SABHA

3589. SHRI PRABHAKAR REDDY VEMIREDDY: 
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to

which they have been employed; and 
(d)       whether the Government has any mechanism to track the post -placement status and 
long-term employment outcomes of candidates trained under the programme and if so, the 
details thereof?  
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP  
 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
  
(a)       The Skill India Programme (SIP)  which is under implementation since FY 2022 -23, 
comprises of three schemes (i) Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 4.0 (PMKVY 4.0), (ii) 
Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (PM -NAPS), and (iii) Jan 
Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) Scheme. 
 
Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) 4.0:  PMKVY 4.0 is a scheme for imparting 
skill development training through Short -Term Training (STT) and up -skilling and re -skilling 
through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) to youths across the country. Under PMKVY 4.0, 
the focus is to empower trained candidates to choose their varied career path and they are 
suitably oriented for the same through On -Job Training (OJT) embedded industry relevant skill 
courses.   
 
The Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) Scheme , initially launched as Shramik Vidyapeeth  (SVP) 
in 1967, aims to provide skill training in a non -formal mode at the doorsteps of the beneficiary 
through registered Societies (NGOs) with 100% grant from the Government of India. The 
objective of the scheme is to increase the household income by promoting self/wage 
employment through skill development training. The target beneficiaries of the scheme are 
non-literates and persons having rudimentary level of education, school dropouts up to class 
12th in the age group of 15-45 years. 
 
At present, 294 Jan Shikshan Sansthans (JSSs) are functional across the country, including 6 
JSSs in the State of Andhra Pradesh. 
  

National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) was launched in August, 2016 to 
promote apprenticeship training and enhance employability through industry -led, on -the-job 
learning. Since FY 2022 -23, the scheme is being implemented as NAPS -2 under the 
provisions of the Apprentices Act, 1961. Under NAPS -2, the Government provides partial 
stipend support to eligible apprentices, limited to 25% of the stipend paid, subject to a 
maximum of ₹1,500 per apprentice per month, which is disbursed directly into the apprentices’ 
bank accounts through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mechanism.

the Skill India Programme are given at Annexure I.

The district -wise details of candidates trained/ oriented / apprentices engaged and 
certified, along with number of operational centres, under the Skill India Programme in Andhra 
Pradesh are given at Annexure III.

PMKVY 3.0 implemented from FY 2015 -16 to FY 2021 -22. Under PMKVY 4.0 which is under 
implementation since FY 2022 -23, the focus is to empower trained candidates to choose their 
varied career path and they are suitably oriented for the same through On -Job Training (OJT) 
embedded industry relevant skill courses.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
  
LOK SABHA

ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Backlog of Reserved Category Posts in Central Educational Institutions 
 
†3592. Shri Dharmendra Yadav: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has data of the current status of backlog vacancies reserved for 
Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs) and Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in all 
Central Educational Institutions under the Ministry of Education; 
(b) if so, the institution-wise details thereof; and 
(c) whether the Government has any proposal or proposes to launch any time-bound special 
recruitment drive to fill up the backlog reserved posts and if so, the details there? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
 
(a) to (c) Occurring of vacancies in Central Educational Institutions and filling thereof is a 
continuous process. The vacancies arise due to promotion, retirement, resignation, death, opening 
of new institutions, schemes or projects, and additional requirements on account of enhanced 
students’ strength and expansion of capacity in existing institutions.  
 
Education being a subject of Concurrent List of the Constitution, an overwhelming majority of the 
schools in the country come under the administrative control of the concerned State Governments/ 
Union Territory administrations. 
 
The Government notified the Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Teachers Cadre) 
Act, 2019 on 09.07.2019 to provide for the reservation of posts in appointments of persons 
belonging to the Scheduled Castes (SCs), the Scheduled Tribes (STs), the socially and 
educationally backward classes and the economically weaker sections, to teachers’ cadre in these 
CHEIs. The reservation is provided in teachers cadre to the extent of 15% for SCs, 7.5% for STs, 

27% for socially and educationally backward classes and 10% for Economically weaker sections, 
as per notification dated 12.7.2019 issued in pursuance of the said Act.   
 
In August, 2021, all the Central Higher Educational Institutions (CHEIs) under Ministry of 
Education were requested to undertake special drive to fill backlog vacancies in their institutions 
in Mission Mode. The CHEIs undertook special recruitment drives to fill the vacancies including 
of Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs) and Other Backward Classes (OBCs). In 
September 2022, Ministry of Education had also exhorted all the CHEIs to fill up the vacancies in 
Mission Mode. In October 2025, all the CHEIs have again been requested to fill up all the backlog 
vacancies in Mission Mode. From September 2022, all CHEIs have undertaken Mission Mode 
recruitment drive to fill the vacancies. Up to 23.05.2026 (i.e. the date of last Rozgar Mela), a total 
number of 32114 posts (3851 SC, 1643 ST, 6785 OBC) have been filled up by all CHEIs, including 
18757 faculty positions (2315 SC, 910 ST, 3986 OBC), in Mission Mode.

entries.t: Removal of Invasive Foreign Species in Reserved Forests
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3594 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Removal of Invasive Foreign Species in Reserved Forests 
 
3594. PROF. SOUGATA RAY: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has identified invasive/foreign plant species in Reserved Forests that are 
adversely affecting native biodiversity, groundwater recharge and water availability and if so, the 
details thereof, State-wise; 
(b) whether any programme has been launched for the removal of such invasive species and 
restoration of native vegetation in Reserved Forests and other protected forest areas and if so, the 
details and present status thereof; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to promote the cultivation and regeneration of 
indigenous/native plant species, grasses, shrubs and other ecologically suitable species to improve 
soil moisture, groundwater recharge and water retention in forest ecosystems and, if so, the details 
thereof; and 
(d) the funds allocated and utilised during the last five years for invasive species management, 
ecological restoration and watershed development in Reserved Forests, State-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (d) The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) and its line 
institutions, actively identify and monitor Invasive Alien Plant Species (IAPS). For identification of 
invasive species, a separate album of 45 major invasive species has been prepared by Forest Survey 
of India (FSI). According to FSI, invasive plants show a very dense  to a  moderate-to-dense and 
scanty occurrence in the Reserved Forest Areas. Botanical Survey of India (BSI) has recently 
prepared and submitted a comprehensive, state-wise inventory of potential invasive species spreading 
across forest and non-forest areas to the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) to facilitate 
preparation of the National Management Plan of Invasive Species.  
 
The management and removal of invasive plant species and cultivation of indigenous plant species 
in Reserved Forests and other protected forest areas are undertaken by the respective State 
Governments/Union Territory Administrations and concerned agencies, in accordance with local 
requirements and the provisions of the approved forest and wildlife management plans. 
 
The Government promotes conservation, regeneration and enrichment of indigenous/native tree 
species through sustainable forest management practices. The National Forest Policy, 1988 envisages 
maintenance of environmental stability, restoration of ecological balance and increasing forest/tree 

cover through afforestation and regeneration using native/indigenous species. Further, the National 
Working Plan Code, 2023 provides for ecosystem-based forest management, including invasive 
species management restoration of degraded forest landscapes, soil and moisture conservation 
measures, watershed management and preference for site-specific indigenous/native species in 
regeneration and restoration activities, taking into account local ecological conditions. These 
measures contribute to improving soil moisture, groundwater recharge, water retention and overall 
ecosystem resilience. 
 
***

entries.t: Strengthening Statutory Audit and Public-Interest Oversight Framework
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3595 
ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Strengthening Statutory Audit and Public-Interest Oversight Framework 
3595. Shri Parshottambhai Rupala:  
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
(a) whether the Government has undertaken a comparative review of global best practices, 
particularly those adopted in the UAE and Estonia, to further strengthen India's statutory audit and 
public-interest oversight framework, if so, the details thereof;  
(b) whether the Government proposes to introduce reforms such as a National Digital Audit 
Registry, mandatory cooling-off periods for statutory auditors, AI-enabled risk-based inspections 
and fixed audit quality review mechanisms, if so, the details thereof; and  
(c) whether the Government is considering measures to strengthen technology-driven audit 
supervision, cyber and forensic audit standards, auditor independence and transparency to enhance 
investor confidence, financial stability and public trust in corporate financial reporting and if so, 
the details thereof?  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION  
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (c) The Ministry of Education regularly interacts with reputed global ranking institutions 
which conduct audit of educational institutions on a varied parameters and incorporates relevant 
best practices as appropriate for the Indian context.  
 
The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 envisages the establishment of robust institutional 
governance, transparency, accountability and efficient financial management across educational 
institutions, and provides that all education institutions will be held to similar standards of audit 
and disclosure as a ‘not for profit’ entity.  
 
Further the NEP 2020 also provides for: 

(i) a ‘light but tight’ regulatory framework to ensure integrity, transparency, and resource 
efficiency of the educational system through audit and public disclosure while encouraging 
innovation and out-of-the-box ideas through autonomy, good governance, and empowerment, and 
(ii) periodic reviews of the progress of implementation of the policy, in accordance with the 
targets set for each action.  
Under various extant statutory and regulatory frameworks, Ministry of Education along with the 
designated bodies, including UGC, AICTE, NCERT, CBSE, NCTE, ensures the governance, 
financial management and oversight of educational institutions. 
 
While at present there is no proposal to introduce a National Digital Audit Registry, the NEP 2020 
encourages the use of technology for improving governance, institutional efficiency, transparency 
and accountability and in this context, Ministry of Education is implementing various digital 
governance initiatives like SWAYAM, SWAYAM+, NISTHA, SAMARTH, ONOS etc. in the 
public interest for the use of diverse stakeholders.

entries.t: Malpractices by Institutions Seeking University Recognition
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION  
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3596 
ANSWERED ON – 10/08/2026 
 
Malpractices by Institutions Seeking University Recognition 
 
3596.  Shri Kunduru Raghuveer: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has received complaints regarding submission of false 
information, fabricated documents and misrepresentation of infrastructure, faculty and 
financial resources by institutions seeking recognition as Universities or Deemed-to-be 
Universities; 
(b) if so, the number of complaints received, verified and found genuine during the last five 
years, along with the action taken thereon, State-wise; 
(c) whether the Government has noticed instances where institutions, after obtaining 
recognition, remove qualified faculty shown during inspections and appoint unqualified or 
inadequate qualified teaching staff in violation of prescribed norms, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether periodic inspections, surprise audits and digital verification of faculty, 
infrastructure and academic standards are conducted after recognition to ensure continued 
compliance, if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the measures taken by the Government to strengthen transparency, ensure continuous 
compliance with UGC norms and impose stringent penalties, including suspension or 
withdrawal of recognition, against institutions found indulging in such malpractices and 
compromising the quality of higher education?  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (e): As per the University Grants Commission (UGC) Act, 1956, a University is 
established by or under a Central Act, a State Act or a Provincial Act and an Institution is 
declared as Deemed to be University by the Central Government, on the advice of UGC, under 
Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956. In order to regulate the process of declaration of an institution 
as Institution Deemed to be University and also to maintain the quality of higher education 
imparted by such Institutions Deemed to be Universities, UGC notified the UGC (Institutions 
Deemed to be Universities) Regulations, 2023. As per these Regulations, a sponsoring body of 
an institution, fulfilling the eligibility criteria as mentioned in the regulations, is required to 
upload all its documents viz. infrastructure, faculty, academic standards, governance, research 
activities, and financial resources on web portal of UGC.  

 The Expert Committee constituted by UGC conducts a comprehensive virtual 
assessment of an institution seeking Deemed to be University status. It verifies the institution's 
claims regarding infrastructure, faculty, academic standards, governance, research activities, 
and financial resources, and assesses compliance with the applicable UGC Regulations. Based 
on its findings, the Committee submits a detailed evaluation report with recommendations to 
the UGC. Also, sponsoring body gives a legal undertaking that all the information, facts and 
figures provided before the inspection and during the inspection are true and correct and shall 
follow and abide by all the rules, regulations, and guidelines issued from time to time by UGC 
and concerned Statutory Council(s). 
As per these Regulations, the sponsoring body is also required to ensure that the copies of the 
documents uploaded on the UGC’s web portal are disclosed on the website of the institution, 
duly certified by the Head of the institution or sponsoring body, as the case may be. However, 
upon receipt of any complaint against the accuracy and veracity of the information submitted 
to the Commission and also hosted on the website of the institution, the Commission shall 
decide on the physical verification of an institution deemed to be University or constitute teams 
for such verification on its own. 
Further, National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 contemplates that HEIs shall be responsible 
and accountable to the stakeholders through transparent self-disclosure of all relevant records. 
In view of the provisions of the NEP, 2020, the UGC has issued the Public Self-Disclosure 
Guidelines, 2024. Accordingly, every Higher Education Institution is required to maintain a 
functional website for making relevant self-disclosure to the stakeholders.

LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3598

Implementation of National Education Policy in HEIs 
 
3598. Dr. Alok Kumar Suman:  
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the manner in which the National Education Policy (NEP) is being implemented in the country; 
(b) the steps taken by the Government to improve the quality of Higher Education Institutions 
(HEIs); 
(c) the efforts being made to promote digital education; 
(d) the present status of skill development programmes in the education sector; and 
(e) the schemes being implemented by the Government to improve education in rural areas? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) and (b):  After announcement of National Education Policy 2020 (NEP 2020), a number of 
transformative changes have taken place both in school and higher education for its 
implementation.  
In School Education  several initiatives have been taken such as PM SHRI (PM Schools for Rising 
India) for upgradation of schools; Samagra Shiksha for providing quality education with an 
inclusive and equitable classroom environment for all children; National Initiative for Proficiency 
in Reading with Understanding and Numeracy (NIPUN Bharat) for ensuring foundational literacy 
and numeracy by Grade 3; Vidya-Pravesh–Guidelines for Three-month Play-based School 
Preparation Module; PM e-VIDYA to unify all efforts related to digital/online/on-air education to 
enable coherent multi-mode access to education; launch of National Curriculum Framework for 
Foundational Stage (NCF FS) and Jadui Pitara for play-based learning teaching material tailored 
for children between the age group of 3 to 8 years; NISHTHA (National Initiative for School 
Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Advancement) 1.0, 2.0 and 3.0; Vidya Samiksha Kendra; Integrated 
Teacher Education Programme; National Digital Education Architecture (NDEAR) for creating a 
unifying national digital infrastructure to energise and catalyse the education ecosystem; 
implementation of a scheme “New India Literacy Programme or ULLAS” targeting all non-
literates age 15 years and above, etc. 
In Higher Education, various initiatives / reforms have been carried out such as National Credit 
Framework (NCrF) and National Higher Education Qualification Framework (NHEQF) in 

conjunction with guidelines / regulations like Curriculum and Credit Framework for 
Undergraduate Programme; Multiple Entry and Exit in Academic Programme offered by Higher 
Education Institutions; Transforming HEIs into multi-disciplinary Institutions; pursuing two 
Academic Programme simultaneously; Automated Permanent Academic Account Registry 
(APAAR ID)  of individual student which will act as lifelong identity to track their educational 
journey and achievements from, pre-primary to higher education; introduction of PM-Vidyalaxmi 
scheme to provide financial support to meritorious students inter-alia enabling collateral free, 
guarantor free loan through a simple, transparent and student-friendly and entirely digital 
application process; revised regulation of ODL / Online Education; re-envisioned Malaviya 
Mission Teacher Training Program to build competencies in faculty for better teaching; permitting 
up to 40% credits in regular courses using SWAYAM platform;  launch of new SWAYAM Plus 
portal with aim to enhance skill and upskilling and reskilling of existing manpower employed in 
different sectors; Integration of technology in administration of HEIs from admission to grant of 
degree through SAMARTH; guidelines on Professor of Practice to enable HEIs to work with 
industry experts; guidelines for supernumerary seats for admitting students from abroad in Indian 
HEIs; Academic collaboration between Indian and Foreign HEIs to offer Twinning, Joint Degree 
and Dual Degree Programmes; Regulation for permitting Foreign HEIs to setup campuses in India; 
enhanced reputation of the Indian HEIs in international ranking; embedding of Indian Knowledge 
system in the education etc. 
Education is subject of concurrent list and both Central and State government work collaboratively 
to ensure comprehensive, and progressive enhancement of overall quality and growth within the 
education sector. NEP 2020 provides different timelines as well as principles and methodology 
for its implementation. Accordingly, Ministry of Education, State Governments, education-related 
Ministries, the regulatory and implementing bodies of school and higher education such as 
University Grants Commission, All India Council for Technical Education, National Council for 
Teacher Education, National Council of Educational Research and Training, Central Board of 
Secondary Education, Universities/Colleges/Schools etc. have started taking initiatives for 
implementation of NEP 2020.

PROMOTION OF MONSOON TOURISM IN KERALA 
 
3599.SHRI KODIKUNNIL SURESH: 
 
 Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has formulated any policy or action plan for 
promoting Monsoon Tourism in Kerala as a distinct tourism product; 
(b) the details of financial assistance, promotional support and 
infrastructure development provided by the Government for monsoon 
tourism in the said State during the last five years, year-wise; 
(c) whether any proposals have been received from the State Government of 
Kerala for the development and promotion of monsoon tourism and if so, 
the details thereof along with the action taken thereon; 
(d) whether the Government proposes to include monsoon tourism circuits, 
wellness tourism, backwater tourism and eco-tourism destinations in the 
said State under any Central tourism schemes and if so, the details 
thereof; and 
(e) the details of steps taken/being taken to promote Kerala as a global 
monsoon tourism destination through international marketing 
campaigns, improved connectivity, sustainable tourism initiatives and 
public-private partnerships? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM   (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (e): Development and promotion of tourism including promotion of 
monsoon tourism in Kerala is primarily done by the concerned State 
Government (SG)/UT Administration (UTA). However, Ministry of Tourism under 
its various schemes such as Swadesh Darshan (SD), Swa desh Darshan 2.0 
(SD2.0), Challenge Based Destination Development (CBDD) – an initiative under 
Swadesh Darshan and Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual Heritage

scheme guidelines, Government dire ctions, availability of funds, inter -se

‘Ashtamudi Biodiversity and Eco -recreational Hub in Kollam’ for Rs. 59.71 
Crore and ‘Global Gateway to Malabar’s Cultural Crucible in Sargaalaya’ for Rs. 
95.34 Crore under its initiative for ‘Special Assistance to States for Capital 
Investment (SASCI)-Development of Iconic Tourist Centres to Global Scale’. 
 
Details of the projects sanctioned under SD2.0 and CBDD schemes in the 
state of Kerala including wellness tourism, backwater tourism and eco-tourism 
destinations in last five years is annexed. 
 
Various aspects of sustainable and responsible tourism are embedded in 
the guidelines of Swadesh Darshan 2.0 Scheme. In addition, the Ministry of 
Tourism has also formulated “National Strategy for Sustainable Tourism”. 
 
Ministry of Tourism promotes various tourism destinations and products 
of the country including monsoon tourism in Kerala and including 
sustainability, responsible tourism practices. Ministry also promotes various 
tourism destinations through various medium including social media, websites 
and participation in fairs and exhibitions etc. 
 
Ministry of Tourism regularly encourages the SGs/UTAs to undertake 
robust Operation and Management of assets created under Swadesh Darshan 
scheme and also to explore the possibility of engaging partners under Public 
Private Partnership model for sustained O&M. As part of Swadesh Darshan 2.0

(b) the details of the reasons identified for such dropouts; and 
(c) the measures taken to reduce dropout rates particularly among Scheduled Castes, Scheduled 
Tribes and girls? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a): As per Unified District Information System for Education Plus (UDISE+), State/UT-wise 
dropout rate from the year 2021-22 to 2025-26 at the primary and secondary levels are available 
at annexure.  
 
(b): As per report titled ‘Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)’ for the year 2025 released by 
Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), the major reasons for the students 
who never attended the schools are to supplement household income, to attend domestic chores, 
etc. 
 
(c): Education is in the concurrent list of the Constitution and majority of the schools are under 
the domain of respective State and UT Governments.  The Central Government assist States and 
UTs through the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Samagra Shiksha and hot cooked meal provided 
from Balvatika to class 8 under Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman (PM POSHAN) Yojna. 
Financial assistance/grant is also provided to the States and UTs for various activities to reduce 
dropout and increase enrolment in Government schools, which include opening/strengthening of 
new schools up to Senior Secondary level, strengthening school infrastructure, setting up and up 
gradation and running of Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas (KGBV) upto class 12, setting up 
of residential schools/hostels named Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Avasiya Vidyalayas, hostels 
under Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN) and Dharti Aaba 
Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA), transport allowance, undertaking enrolment drives, 
seasonal hostels/residential camps, provision of vocational education and ICT facilities in schools, 
providing free text books and free uniform, transport/escort facility, etc. 
 
Government has also taken initiatives such as Vidya Samiksha Kendra (VSK) and 
implementation of Automated Permanent Academic Account Registry (APAAR) ID to monitor 
the drop out and other education indicators. VSK has been developed with strategies designed to 
enhance the effectiveness of monitoring of educational initiatives and their eventual outcomes. A 
key feature of VSK is student tracking to prevent dropouts, monitoring of students migrating from 
one school to the other, progress of learning outcomes and real-time monitoring of various 
interventions, aimed at improving access, students' academic performance and enhancing teachers' 
accountability in schools. APAAR, as part of the 'One Nation, One Student ID' programme, is a 
12-digit lifelong student ID that is linked to Aadhar.

entries.t: Monitoring of NATS Diploma Holders in Andhra Pradesh
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
LOK SABHA 
 UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.3604 
ANSWERED ON: 10.08.2026 
 
MONITORING OF NATS DIPLOMA HOLDERS IN ANDHRA PRADESH 
3604. DR. D. PURANDESWARI: 
Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to 
state: 
 (a)  whether the Government has monitored the implementation of the National Apprenticeship 
Training Scheme (NATS) for graduate and diploma holders during 2025-2026 in Andhra Pradesh; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof, including the total number of technical graduates who have 
successfully secured apprenticeship positions in the said State; 
(c)  the total amount of stipend reimbursement released to the participating technical 
institutions and industries in Andhra Pradesh during the last one year and the current year;  
(d) whether the Government has observed delays in the processing of subsidy claims by the 
regional boards, causing financial strain on the participating employers; and 
(e) the specific steps taken/being taken by the Government to integrate non -technical degree 
graduates into the apprenticeship framework within Andhra Pradesh? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP  
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
(a) to (e): The Government of India monitors the implementation of the National Apprenticeship 
Training Scheme (NATS) through four autonomous bodies, namely Board of Apprenticeship 
Training (Northern Region), Kanpur; Board of Apprenticeship Training (Western Region), 
Mumbai; Board of Practical Training (Eastern Region), Kolkata and Board of Apprenticeship 
Training (Southern Region), Chennai. Further, NATS 2.0 portal has been introduced as a 
technology enabled platform for management of apprenticeship training.  In Andhra Pradesh, 
NATS is implemented through Board of Apprenticeship Training (Southern Region) (BoAT -SR) 
which undertakes activities for engagement of apprentices, industry outreach and monitoring of 
NATS implementation. During 2025 –26, a total of 1,851 apprentices were engaged in Andhra 
Pradesh, comprising 1175 Technical Apprentices and 676 Non-technical Apprentices.  
Under NATS, The prescribed minimum monthly stipend ranges from ₹ 12300 for graduates 
apprentices and ₹ 10,900 for diploma apprentices. The Government of India provide 50% of the 
prescribed minimum stipend as support for a maximum period of 1 year. The Ministry of 
Education releases grants under the stipendiary head to the four implementing Boards for 
disbursement of stipend through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) and for settlement of eligible 
reimbursement claims of establishments after verification. 
 

From 1st November 2025, the Government share of stipend is being transferred directly to the 
bank accounts of apprentices through DBT. Before DBT, reimbursement model was followed 
wherein establishment used to pay government share of apprenticeship training to apprentices  
and may claim for reimbursement of the Government’s share from the respective Board of 
Apprenticeship Training (BoAT) within three years from the date of payment of stipend. Claims are 
released by respective BoAT after verification of the documents received from the establishments. 
During 2025 –26, ₹ 75.69 lakh was reimbursed towards stipend to participating industries in 
Andhra Pradesh.   
 
To facilitate the participation of graduates/diploma holders from all streams including non -
technical degree graduates in apprenticeship training under NATS, BoATs are conducting various 
outreach activities in their respective regions. BoAT -SR has also conducted career guidance 
programmes, institution visits, apprenticeship fairs and placement -officer sensitisation 
programmes. Further, 20 MoUs have been signed with Universities/Colleges under the 
Apprenticeship Embedded Degree Programme (AEDP) in the state of Andhra Pradesh by BoAT 
(SR). An extension office has also been established at Acharya Nagarjuna University, Guntur, 
Andhra Pradesh for on-ground implementation support of NATS.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3606 
ANSWERED ON MONDAY , 10th August, 2026 
 
Pending Cases under Company Law 
 
QUESTION 
Will the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
3606 Smt. Manju Sharma 
Will the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS 
(a) the steps that have been taken by the Government to reduce the number of 
pending cases under company law in the country: 
(b) the details of statistics regarding the number of cases withdrawn or reduced 
as part of the Government's efforts to alleviate the litigation burden; and 
(c) whether the Government is taking any steps to improve the ease of doing 
business and strengthen the corporate governance framework in the country and 
if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS AND 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS. 
 (SHRI. HARSH MALHOTRA)  
(a): The Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) has taken several steps to review & 
reduce pending cases under company law. This includes withdrawal of pending 
prosecutions involving procedural & technical offences; decriminalization of 51 
offences under the Companies Act, 2013 in 2019 & 2020 ; and introduction of e -
Adjudication mechanism for disposal of cases at the level of Regional 
Directorates (RDs) & Registrars of Companies (ROCs). 
(b): 20,514 prosecution cases were withdrawn from various courts between 2017 
and 2025 . Withdrawal of prosecutions is a continuous process which is 
undertaken by this Ministry. 

(c): To improve ease of doing business and enhance corporate governance, 
Ministry has taken several steps, of which some of the major steps are as under:-  
(i) Setting up of a Centralized Registrar of Companies (CRC) for 
incorporation and introducing new e-Forms for providing different services, 
such as PAN, opening of Bank Accounts, etc., at one place at the time of 
incorporation of companies & LLPs, to start the business immediately. 
(ii) Conversion of more than 50 e-forms to Straight Through Process ( STP) 
which earlier required approval of field offices; 
(iii) Setting up of a Central Processing Centre (CPC) for centralised 
processing of specified non-STP e-forms; 
(iv) Setting up of a Centre for Processing Accelerated Corporate Exit (C -
PACE) for voluntary exit of companies; 
(v) Definition of small companies has been amended by increasing the 
threshold limit of a small company, having a paid -up capital not exceeding 
Rs. 10 Crores and turnover not exceeding Rs. 100 Crores. Similarly, concept 
of small LLP has been introduced which is subject to lesser compliances, 
lesser fee to reduce the cost of compliances;  
(vi) Zero fee for incorporation of company with authorized capital up to 
Rs.15 Lakh; 
(vii) Extension of fast-track process for mergers under the Companies Act, 
2013 to include mergers of Startups with other Startups and with small 
companies, so that the process of mergers & amalgamations is expedited; 
(viii) Zero cost for shifting of the registered office of a company;  
(ix) Notification of Companies (Listing of Equity Shares in Permissible 
Jurisdictions) Rules, 2024 allowing Indian public companies to list their 
equity shares on international stock exchange(s) at International Financial 
Services Centre (IFSC) in India. 
(x) Allowing convening of Annual General Meeting (AGM) and Extra-ordinary 
General Meeting (EGM) of a company through Video Conference (VC)  to 
increase shareholder participation  and reduce costs associated with 
conduct of general meetings for companies; 
(xi) The Companies (Accounts) Second Amendment Rules, 2025 prescribed 
revised AOC electronic forms for filing financial statements and director’s 
report, for collection of structured corporate information directed towards 

more effective & disclosure-based accountability and data -based 
regulatory scrutiny, wherever necessitated in public interest.  
Similarly, Companies (Management and Administration) Amendment Rules, 
2025 prescribed r evised MGT electronic forms aimed towards  improving 
structured disclosure of annual-return and governance information filed on 
MCA21.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION  
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3607 
ANSWERED ON – 10/08/2026 
 
Grant of Deemed University Status to NCERT 
 
3607. Shri V K Sreekandan: 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether it is a fact that an Expert Panel had recommended the grant of deemed-to-be 
university status to the National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) and 
if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that the University Grants Commission (UGC), based on the said 
recommendations, has granted deemed-to-be university status to NCERT and if so, the details 
thereof; 
(c) whether it is true that the new status will empower NCERT to design academic programmes 
and expand its role from curriculum body to a higher education and research institution; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (d): The application of National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT), 
New Delhi for grant of Institution Deemed to be University status was examined by the 
University Grant Commission (UGC) through its Expert Committee as per the provisions of 
the UGC (Institutions Deemed to be Universities) Regulations, 2023. The Committee, after 
overall assessment, recommended for grant of Institutions Deemed to be University to NCERT, 
New Delhi. Considering the advice of UGC, the Ministry of Education, vide Notification dated 
30.03.2026, declared NCERT, New Delhi as an Institution Deemed to be University under 
Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956. The said declaration was subject to condition that it shall take 
appropriate steps to commence research programmes as well as doctoral and innovative 
academic programmes.   
The status of Institution Deemed to be University will strengthen the NCERT to promote 
educational research & innovation and collaborate with national and international agencies. It 
will further reinforce its role as a think tank and as national resource institution engaged in 
providing technical support to the Central Government as well as State Governments.

entries.t: HEIs Integrated with ABC and APAAR Ecosystem in Bulandshahr
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO-3608  
ANSWERED ON-10/08/2026 
 
HEIs Integrated with ABC and APAAR Ecosystem in Bulandshahr 
 
3608. Dr. Bhola Singh: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of schools, colleges and Higher Educational Institutions (HEIs) in Bulandshahr 
Lok Sabha Constituency integrated with the Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) and Automated 
Permanent Academic Account Registry (APAAR) ecosystem; 
(b) whether the Government has reviewed the implementation of ABC and APAAR in the said 
Constituency and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the number of students registered under APAAR and ABC in Bulandshahr district; 
(d) the measures taken by the Government to facilitate integration of Government and private 
institutions under the framework; and 
(e) the steps taken by the Government to create awareness among students and educational 
institutions in Bulandshahr Lok Sabha Constituency? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (e): The Government of India has framed the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 to 
promote holistic & multidisciplinary education, enable multiple entry and exit system and 
establish a lifelong learning ecosystem. NEP envisions the establishment of an Academic Bank 
of Credit (ABC) to digitally store the academic credits so that the degrees from a Higher 
Education Institution (HEI) can be awarded taking into account credits earned.  
 
Accordingly, the Ministry of Education launched the Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) 
Scheme in July 2021 to provide a 12-digit unique digital identity for every learner to facilitate 
the identification and to enable the systematic tracking of their learning. This unique id has 
been termed “Automated Permanent Academic Account Registry” (APAAR ID). APAAR ID 
is designed to accumulate credits earned from academic, skill and experiential learning. 

 
As on date, more than 2900 award granting institutions from the higher education ecosystem 
have been registered on ABC portal. Further, over 4.8 crore APAAR IDs have been created in 
the higher education ecosystem, with more than 10 crore credit records mapped.  
As per the All India Survey on Higher Education (AISHE) 2023-24 report, the only university 
in Bulandshahr district has been onboarded on the ABC portal as an Award Granting Institution. 
So far, this university has uploaded more than 4,500 academic records for more than 1100 
APAAR IDs of its students in ABC portal. More than 4.90 lakh school students from 
Bulandshahr have APAAR ID.  
Ministry of Education has conducted regular interaction with HEIs and States to review the 
progress of the scheme including the state of Uttar Pradesh. Further, Digital India Corporation 
(DIC) under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) is the technology 
partner for the Ministry of Education for the implementation of the ABC scheme. To ensure 
seamless implementation and stakeholder support, DIC has established a comprehensive 
support ecosystem for the academic institutions through daily video conferencing sessions on 
all weekdays, around 10 awarding bodies participate in each session. Further, an integrated 
ticketing system for timely resolution of queries; which resolves nearly 200 queries per day. A 
dedicated toll-free helpline (1800-889-3511) for students & educational institutions has been 
established which resolves most of the issues during the call.  
 
Zonal and State Nodal Officers have also been designated to strengthen coordination with State 
Governments, Higher Education Departments, and award-granting academic institutions 
across the country. Further, to promote awareness and enhance stakeholder engagement, DIC 
has also organized the Digital India Talk Show at universities and higher education institutions. 
In addition, online knowledge-sharing initiatives, such as "Ask Our Experts", are conducted 
through digital platforms to address implementation challenges, clarify stakeholder queries, 
and disseminate best practices related to the ABC ecosystem. 
 
*****

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TOURISM  
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.3609 
ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
DEVELOPMENT OF TOURISM IN KASHMIR 
 
3609. SHRI ABDUL RASHID SHEIKH: 
 
 Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has any Proposal for development of tourism

Gurez, if so, the details thereof; and 
(b) whether the Government has proposed New Eco -tourism projects in 
Baramulla, Kupwara, Budgam and Bandipora districts? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM  (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (b): Development and promotion of tourist destinations and tourism 
products, including Eco -tourism destination is primarily undertaken by the 
concerned State Government (SG) /Union Territory Administration (UTA). 
However, the Ministry through its existing schemes of ‘Swadesh Darshan (SD)’, 
‘Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD2.0)’, ‘Challenge Based Destination Development 
(CBDD)’ – a sub-scheme of SD2.0, and ‘Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual, 
Heritage Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD)’ complements the efforts of tourism 
infrastructure development by extending financial assistance to the State 
Governments/UT Administrations including Jammu & Kashmir; subject to 
adherence to scheme guidelines, submission of Detailed Project Reports 
(DPRs) by them, availability of funds, Government directions, inter -se priority 
etc. 
 
The Ministry of Tourism has revamped the Swadesh Darshan scheme as 
Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD2.0) with the objective to develop sustainable and 
responsible tourism destinations in the country, following a destination and 
tourist centric approach. 

 
Sanctioning of new project under the above -mentioned schemes is a 
continuous process. 
 
At present, no proposal for development of tourism infrastructure in 
Baramulla, Kupwara, Budgam and Bandipora districts of UT of Jammu & 
Kashmir is under consideration in the Ministry of Tourism. 
  
The details of the projects sanctioned under SD and PRASHAD schemes 
in the UT of J&K are annexed.

entries.t: Alignment of NCERT Syllabus with National Education Policy 2020
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3610 
ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Alignment of NCERT Syllabus with National Education Policy 2020 
 
3610. Shri K C Venugopal: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the steps adopted by National Council of Educational Research and Training 
(NCERT) to align its syllabus with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020; 
(b) the details of the process followed in deciding the academic curriculum, guidelines and learning 
outcomes at the NCERT; 
(c) the details of the stakeholders involved in the above said process and whether there is any high-
level expert committee to review the same, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the manner and extent to which the syllabus and curriculum of NCERT textbooks is often 
updated? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (d): As per the recommendations of National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, the National 
Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) has brought out the National Curriculum 
Framework for Foundational Stage (NCF-FS) 2022 and the National Curriculum Framework for 
School Education (NCF-SE) 2023. These frameworks provide the basis for stage-wise and subject-
wise curricular goals, competencies, learning outcomes, syllabi, textbooks, pedagogy and 
assessment. 
 
For developing National Curriculum Frameworks, National Steering Committee was constituted 
which followed bottom -up approach of seeking inputs for the National Curriculum Frameworks 
from diverse stakeholders including teachers, parents, students, educational institutions, neo- and 
non- literates, subjects’ experts, scholars, Anganwadi personnel etc., from across the states and UTs, 
a massive process of public consultations in face-to-face as well as digital mode was conducted. 
This process had benefited from the engagement of over 13 lakh interested citizens including 
students and parents at the national level through citizen-centric mobile app survey and over 1.5 
lakh teachers, parents, students, and educationists at the state level through mobile app survey. 
 
Over 1550 district-level consultations in 32 States and Union Territories were conducted.  Inputs 
were also received from 35 groups of institutions, 8000 stakeholders who attended 12 consultations 

with Universities and Civil Society Groups. More than 600 position papers on 25 specifically 
relevant themes written by Focus Groups constituted by the States and UTs which all together had 
over 4000 experts, and 25 papers from the National Focus Groups by expert groups with over 175 
members, constituted by the NCERT. These inputs were analyzed and relevant suggestions were 
included in the NCFs. Taking cognizance of these inputs, the NCF-FS was released on 20th October, 
2022 and NCF-SE was released on 23rd August, 2023. 
 
As a follow-up of the NCFs, NCERT has constituted National Syllabus and Teaching-Learning 
Material Committee (NSTC). Under this Committee, 13 Curricular Area Groups (CAGs) and 
Textbook Development Teams (TDTs) for all the subjects and grades have been set up. NSTC has 
been assigned the task of development of teaching-learning material including textbooks. NCERT 
has also constituted National Curriculum Framework Oversight Committee (NOC) to look into the 
translation of NCF perspective in the new teaching-learning material including textbooks. NSTC, 
NOC and CAG include scholars, subject experts, renowned players, artists, teacher educators, 
faculty members of NCERT, officials from SCERTs, etc. TDT includes scholars, subject experts, 
teachers, teacher educators, faculty members of NCERT, faculty members from SCERTs, etc. With 
the support of NSTC, NCERT has brought out new syllabus and textbooks for Grades 1-9 and also 
a collection of learning resources- Jaadui Pitara and e Jaadui Pitara for Balvatika 1, 2, and 3.  
 
New teaching-learning material including textbooks and learning material are developed through 
detailed mapping of curricular goals, competencies and learning outcomes. The drafts undergo 
multiple rounds of academic, pedagogical, language and sensitivity review. The review process 
examines academic accuracy, age-appropriateness, inclusivity, constitutional values, gender 
sensitivity, cultural and linguistic relevance, pedagogical suitability and alignment with NEP 2020, 
NCF-FS 2022 and NCF-SE 2023. As a follow-up of the NCF-SE, Learning Outcome Document and 
Mandate Documents were developed, which served as guidelines for the development of new syllabi 
and textbooks along with NCF-FS and NCF-SE. 
 
NCERT while reprinting its textbooks, every year, updates its textbooks in alignment with the 
relevant feedback from students, teachers and other stakeholders, without making any structural 
changes. For this purpose, also, if required, NCERT invites experts for finalizing the c

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3611 
ANSWERED ON 10/08/2026 
 
Faculty-to-Student Ratio in IITs 
 
3611.  Dr. Shashi Tharoor: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government or the IIT Council has prescribed any faculty-to-
student ratio for the Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), if so, the details  
thereof and the actual faculty-to-student ratio in each IIT; 
(b) the number of permanent and visiting faculty in each IIT during the last 
five years and whether the number of visiting faculty has increased during 
the said period, year-wise; 
(c) the number of sanctioned, filled and vacant faculty posts in each IIT  
during the last five years, along with the vacancy percentage in each IIT, 
year-wise; and 
(d) whether the IIT Council has prescsribed any incentive scheme,  
performance  parameter or funding condition to induct doctoral alumni as 
permanent faculty and to convert long-serving visiting/ad-hoc faculty into 
permanent positions, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons 
therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (d):  The Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) are autonomous institutes 
governed by the Institutes of Technology Act, 1961 as amended from time to 
time and the Statutes framed there under.  
 
          The IIT Council, in its various meetings, has deliberated on measures to 
facilitate and strengthen faculty recruitment in the IITs. The Council has 
recognised faculty recruitment as a core institutional priority, given its direct 
bearing on academic quality, teaching capacity and research excellence. The 
measures discussed include rolling and special recruitment drives; engagement 
of guest, adjunct, visiting faculty and Professors of Practice; facilitation of the 

recruitment of foreign faculty and eligible Overseas Citizens of India (OCI) 
cardholders; institutional performance-review mechanisms; and strengthened 
recruitment monitoring through regular reporting. 
 
                The creation of vacancies and filling thereof is a continuous process. 
Vacancies arise due to retirements, resignations and the creation of additional 
positions necessitated by the expansion of student enrolment and academic 
programmes. In order to attract high-quality talent, the IITs issue rolling 
advertisements for faculty recruitment, which remain open throughout the year. 
Further, in September 2022, the Ministry of Education advised all Central 
Higher Educational Institutions (CHEIs) to fill vacancies in mission mode. Under 
the mission-mode recruitment drive undertaken from September 2022 to May 
2026, the IITs filled more than 3,500 faculty vacancies. At present, around 460 
visiting faculty members are engaged in teaching and academic activities across 
the IIT system. 
IITs also engage Professors of Practice (PoP) to enhance students' 
experiences by providing insights into real-world best practices. PoPs also serve 
as a bridge between industry and the institute to identify teaching and research 
opportunities that support the public interest and societal needs. Further, IITs 
also hire visiting faculty members who are from academics or senior industry 
professionals joining IITs for a short duration to promote a cross-cultural 
exchange of ideas and perspectives. 
IITs encourage the alumni of their Institutes to appear for faculty positions 
as per year-round open advertisements. Measures have been taken to attract 
quality faculty which includes recruitment through search-cum-selection 
procedures, special recruitment drive, mission mode recruitment and invitation 
to alumni/scientists/faculty, etc. The faculty recruitment process is carried out 
by the IITs by inviting applications in a transparent manner, as part of a multi-
step and robust screening process. 
Further, in the QS World University Rankings 2027, Indian Institutes of 
Technology (IITs) have achieved notable positions. IIT Delhi has been placed at 
118th (123rd in 2026), IIT Madras at 170th (180th in 2026), IIT Kharagpur at 
205th (215th in 2026), IIT Kanpur at 221st (222nd in 2026). 
*********

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TOURISM  
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.3612 
ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
PROGRESS ACHIEVED UNDER SWADESH DARSHAN SCHEME 
 
3612. SHRI THARANIVENTHAN M S: 
 
  Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of progress achieved under the Swadesh Darshan Scheme 
(SDS) during the last five years, including the number of projects 
sanctioned, completed and pending, State / UT-wise including Arani Lok 
Sabha Constituency of Tamil Nadu; 
(b) the details of funds allocated, released and utilised under the scheme 
during the said period, along with the details of tourist circuits covered; 
(c) whether the Government has conducted any assessment of the impact 
of the scheme on tourism infrastructure development, tourist footfall, 
employment generation and local economic growth and if so, the details 
thereof; 
(d) the details of reasons for delays, if any, in completion of sanctioned 
projects and the steps taken to ensure timely implementation, quality 
monitoring and effective utilisation of funds; and 
(e) whether the Government proposes to expand the scope of the Swadesh 
Darshan Scheme by including more destinations, heritage sites, rural 
tourism locations and lesser -known tourist  attractions and if so, the 
details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM  (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (e): The Ministry had launched the Swadesh Darshan Scheme (SDS) in 
2014-15 for integrated development of tourism infrastructure under 15 
identified thematic circuits. Under the Scheme, 76 projects have been 
sanctioned across different States with a total sancti oned cost of ₹5295.24 

crore and have been implemented in accordance with the scheme guidelines. 
75 projects out of 76 sanctioned projects are reported physically complete.  
  
The Ministry regularly encourages State Governments/ UT Administrations to 
engage with local communities and to ensure robust operation & management 
(O&M) of completed projects so as to increase footfall, generate local 
employment and enhance overall tourist satisfaction. 
 
Ministry of Tourism regularly monitors progress of its ongoing projects 
through review meetings with SGs/UTAs, which are held at various levels from 
time to time. Ministry of Tourism has also developed a Program Management 
Information System (PMIS) which i s a unified digital platform to facilitate 
seamless information communication, sharing and reporting system in respect 
of the projects undertaken as parts of Ministry’s various schemes. Ministry of 
Tourism and SGs/UTAs including project implementing agenci es are integral 
part of this system. 
 
The Ministry of Tourism has revamped the Swadesh Darshan scheme as 
Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD2.0) with the objective to develop sustainable and 
responsible tourism destinations in the country, following a destination and 
tourist centric approach and the Minis try has sanctioned 53 projects for Rs. 
2207.08 crore under this scheme in the country. Further, Challenge  Based 
Destination  Development (CBDD) – a sub-scheme of  Swadesh Darshan 2.0 has 
also been initiated in 4 categories viz. Ecotourism and Amrit Dharohar, 
Spiritual Tourism, Culture & Heritage and Vibrant Village Programme and the 
Ministry has sanctioned 37 projects for Rs. 687.99 crore under this initiative in 
the country.  
 
The details of projects sanctioned by the Ministry under SD, SD2.0 and 
CBDD Schemes in the county including Tamil Nadu are annexed.

entries.t: Development of a Temple Tourism Circuit for Srisailam
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TOURISM 
 
LOK SABHA 
   UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.3613 
ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
DEVELOPMENT OF A TEMPLE TOURISM CIRCUIT FOR SRISAILAM 
 
 3613.  DR. BYREDDY SHABARI: 
 
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has received any proposal from the State 
Government of Andhra  Pradesh or any other agency for the 
development of a temple tourism circuit including Srisailam during 
the last five years, if so, the details and current status thereof; 
(b) whether any master plan or Detailed Project Report (DPR) has been 
prepared or submitted for the development of Srisailam and 
surrounding temple destinations and if so, the present status 
thereof; 
(c)  the details of measures taken or proposed to improve connectivity, 
tourist amenities, heritage conservation, safety and other tourism 
infrastructure in and around Srisailam during the last five years; 
(d) the details of Central assistance sanctioned, released and utilised 
for tourism infrastructure  in Srisailam during the last five years, 
scheme and year-wise; and 
(e) whether the Government proposes to include Srisailam under any 
existing or proposed temple/spiritual tourism circuit and if so, the 
details along with timeline thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM       (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (e): The development and promotion of tourist destinations and 
tourism products, is primarily undertaken by the respective State 
Governments and Union Territory (UT) Administration s. However, the 
Ministry of Tourism, under its various schemes such as Pilgrimage 
Rejuvenation and Spiritual , Heritage Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD) , 

Swadesh Darshan (SD), Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD2.0), Challenge Based 
Destination Development (CBDD) supplements the efforts of the 
States/UTs by providing financial assistance for the development of 
tourism related infrastructure and experiences across the country, 
including in the State of Andhra Pradesh. 
 
Receiving proposals from the State Governments and Union 
Territory Administrations for financial assistance for tourism projects is 
a continuous process. The proposals received are examined with 
reference to the prescribed guidelines and financial assistan ce is 
extended for such projects subject to fulfilment of the stipulated 
conditions and availability of funds. 
 
The Ministry has sanctioned a project, namely, ‘Development of 
Srisailam Temple’, at a cost of Rs. 43.08 Crore under its PRASHAD 
Scheme. The entire amount of Rs. 43.08 Crore has been released and 
utilized. The said project stands completed.  
 
The major components developed under the said project includes 
Illumination, Tourist Amenity Centre , Changing Rooms, Parking, Ramp, 
Toilet Complexes, Drinking Water Facility and Road Improvement Works 
etc. 
 
*****

1 
 
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS 
   LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3614 
ANSWERED ON MONDAY , 
AUGUST 10, 2026 
 
Deregistered Shell Companies 
 
3614. Ms S Jothimani: 
          
Will the Minister of Corporate Affairs be pleased to state: 
(a) the total number of shell companies identified and deregistered/struck 
off from the register of companies under section 248 of the Companies Act, 
2013 during the last five years, State-wise and year-wise; 
(b) the details of the action taken by the Government against such shell 
companies and their directors; 
(c) whether the Government has initiated any fresh regulatory measures, 
technological interventions or enforcement steps to improve financial 
transparency and curb the menace of shell companies; and  
(d) if so, the details thereof, including the progress made in utilizing artificial 
intelligence and data analytics tools for early detection of financial fraud?  
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS  AND 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS. 
          (SHRI HARSH MALHOTRA) 
**** 
(a) & (b). The term ‘shell company’ is not defined under the Companies Act, 2013. 
Therefore, t he requisite information pertaining to action taken against such 
companies and its directors  is not maintained by the Ministry of Corporate 
Affairs. 
(c)&(d). The provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and the rules made 
thereunder contain adequate provisions to ensure financial accountability and 
transparency. These provisions inter alia require maintenance of books of 
accounts and statutory registers at the reg istered offices, preparation of 
financial statements in accordance with applicable financial 
reporting/accounting standards and filing them with the Registrar after due 
approvals. The financial statements are required to be audited by an 
independent chartered accountant. Crucial parameters such as risk 
management, state of company's affairs, material changes affecting company's 
financial position are required to be reported in the Board’s Report.  

2 
 
Further, through the Companies (Accounts) Second Amendment Rules, 2025 
revised AOC electronic forms for filing financial statements and director’s 
report, for collection of structured corporate information directed towards 
more effective & disclosure -based accountability and d ata-based regulatory 
scrutiny, wherever necessitated in public interest have been prescribed. 
Similarly, through the Companies (Management and Administration) 
Amendment Rules, 2025 revised MGT electronic forms aimed towards 
improving structured disclosure of annual -return and governance information 
filed on MCA21, have been prescribed.  
The Registrar of Companies take s suitable  action against the defaulting 
companies who fail to file their Annual Returns and/or Financial Statements 
under the provisions of s ection 92, 96, 99, 137  and 129 of the Companies Act 
2013. Action under section 248 (1) of the Act read with Companies (Removal of 
names of companies from the Register of Companies) Rules, 2016, to strike off 
names of companies is also undertaken. 
As regards technological intervention, MCA21 V3 functions on web -based 
filings which provides for real time validation with pre -filled master data, 
thereby reducing possibility of falsification of data. 
*******

(a) whether the Government has fixed any transparent policy, 
eligibility criteria and assessment system to setup national Centres 
of Sports excellence, high performance training Centres and regional 
excellence Centres in the country and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the details of number of such centres and the details of basis of

talent assessment;

[DR. MANSUKH MANDAVIYA]
