(a) to (d): The establishment of National Centres of Excellence 
(NCoEs) and other Sports Authority of India (SAI) Training Centres is 
considered on the basis of proposals received from the respective 
State Governments/UT Administrations. Such proposals are 
examined with reference to the availability of sports infrastructure, 
sporting potential, technical and financial feasibility, regional 
requirements and other relevant factors. 
 
At present, 181 SAI Centres, including NCoEs, STCs, Extension

other prescribed parameters.

districts; and 364 Khelo India Accredited Academies (KIAAs) 
covering 128 districts are operational. Details are available at 
https://dashboard.kheloindia.gov.in/khelo-india-center-dashboard.

The scheme provided assured pension and strengthened the social security of eligible senior

entries.t: ESIC Coverage and Healthcare facilities for Workers
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3618 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
ESIC COVERAGE AND HEALTHCARE FACILITIES FOR WORKERS 
 
3618. SHRI PARIMAL SUKLABAIDYA: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a)the details of employees and establishments registered under the 
Employees’ State  Insurance Corporation (ESIC) in Assam, district -
wise, particularly for Cachar district; 
(b)the details of  steps taken by the Government to extend ESIC 
coverage to workers  employed in tea gardens, small industries, 
plantations, construction and other unorganised  sectors in Cachar 
district; 
(c)whether the Government proposes to establish or upgrade ESIC 
hospitals, dispensaries and diagnostic facilities in Cachar district to 
improve access to quality healthcare for insured  workers and their 
families and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d)the details of measures taken by the Government to strengthen 
awareness, soc ial security  benefits, cashless treatment, maternity 
benefits, disability support and digital ESIC services for  workers in 
Cachar district, especially those residing in rural and remote areas? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (d): The district -wise details of employees and establishments 
registered under the Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) in 
Assam is placed at Annexure.  
 
  The provisions of the Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 
have been subsumed under the Code on Social Security, 2020, which 
came into force with effect from 21st November 2025. As per the First 
Schedule to the Code, Chapter IV relating to the Employees' State 
Insurance Corporation (ESIC) applies to every establishment employing 
ten or more persons, other than a seasonal factory. It is further provided 
that an employer of a plantation, may opt the application of Chapter IV 
in respect of the plantation by giving willingness to the corporation, 
where the benefits available to the employees under that Chapter are 
better than what the employer is providing to them. 
Contd..2/- 
 

:: 2 :: 
  At present, unorganised workers are not covered under the 
ESIC framework. However, Section 45 of the Code on Social  Security, 
2020 empowers the Central Government to frame a scheme for 
extending ESIC benefits to unorganised workers, gig workers and 
platform workers.  
  Currently, there is one ESI Dispensary at Silchar, Cachar 
District for providing healthcare services to the Insured Persons and 
their families. At present, there is no proposal under consideration to 
establish any ESI Hospital, dispensary, diagnostic centre or upgrade 
exiting dispensary in that district.  
  ESIC has conducted 103 awareness camps in the Ca char 
district for awareness on various social security benefits including 
disability support under ESI Act. Also, a total amount of Rs. 19,91,814/- 
has been disbursed as Cash Benefit out of which Rs. 8,57,948/ - was 
disbursed as Maternity Benefit during the Financial Year 2025-26 in the 
Cachar District. ESIC provides digital services in the form of Insured 
Person (IP) Portal which can be accessed by the IP from any location to 
submit his online claims of Cash Benefits and also to generate requests 
to change his particulars in the e-Pehchan card.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
DEPARTMENT OF FINANCIAL SERVICES 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3619 
ANSWERED ON MONDAY, 10 AUGUST, 2026/SHRAVANA 19, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
Accounts opened under Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana 
3619. DR. KALANIDHI VEERASWAMY: 
 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the total number of bank accounts opened under Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) since 
its launch and the number of accounts that are active as of the latest date within Tamil Nadu; 
(b) the total deposits mobilized, credit disbursed and insurance coverage provided under  PMJDY 
accounts; 
(c) the percentage of PMJDY account holders from rural, marginalized and underprivileged  
communities and the specific measures taken to ensure financia l inclusion for women and  weaker 
sections; 
(d) the reasons for accounts  becoming dormant or inactive and the steps planned to increase  account 
usage for productive purposes; 
(e) the progress made in linking PMJDY accounts with Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT) and other social 
welfare schemes; 
(f) the financial literacy and awareness programs conducted to educate beneficiaries about PMJDY and 
their effectiveness; and 
(g) the monitoring and evaluation mechanisms in place to assess the  impact of PMJDY on  reducing 
financial exclusion and poverty?  
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) A total of 58.84 crore Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) accounts have been opened across 
the country since the launch of the Scheme . As on 22.07.2026, 1.49 crore PMJDY accounts are active in 
the state of Tamil Nadu. 
 
(b) As on 22.07.2026, the total deposits under PMJDY accounts are ₹3,11,291 crore. With regard to credit 
disbursement, the overdraft facility under PMJDY has been availed in 34.69 lakh accounts, with an 
outstanding amount of ₹374.25 crore (as on 24.06.2026). As regards insurance coverage, 8.27 crore PMJDY 
account holders have been enroll ed under the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)  and 
19.41 crore PMJDY account holders have been enrolled under the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana 
(PMSBY). 
 
(c) With the aim to further financial inclusion w.e.f 14.08.2018, the focus to opening of accounts shift ed 
from “every household” to “every unbanked adult”.  
The percentage of PMJDY account holders in rural/ semi-urban areas and PMJDY women accounts, as on 
22.07.2026, are:

(d) PMJDY accounts becomes dormant or inactive due to reasons such as non-operation of the account for 
a prolonged period, migration of account holders, opening of multiple accounts, lack of regular transactions 
or demise of the account holder not reported.  
Banks continuously make concerted efforts to reduce the number of in operative accounts by organising 
camps to create awareness about banking habits including the benefits of keeping the account active. Banks 
have also been advised to take necessary steps to reduce the number of inoperative accounts and make the 
process of activation of such accounts smoother and hassle free. 
 
(e) The data regarding the number of PMJDY accounts linked to various DBT Schemes is not centrally 
maintained. However, PMJDY guidelines envisage channeling Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) from the 
Government to the beneficiaries’ Jan-Dhan accounts. Beneficiaries of different Government schemes are 
being given benefits directly in their bank accounts, including PMJDY accounts. 
 
(f) & (g) Several initiatives have been taken to promote financial/digital literacy and increase awareness of 
Government schemes, which are as under: 
i. The Centre for Financial Literacy (CFL) Project has been initiated by the RBI since 2017 with an 
objective to adopt community-led innovative and participatory approaches to financial literacy. A total 
of 2,421 CFLs have been set up across the country with one CFL covering three blocks on an average. 
ii. Banks have been advised to conduct camps through their Financial Literacy Centres (FLCs) on "Going 
Digital" through UPI for general public and tailored camps for different target groups. 
iii. Rural branches of banks are required to conduct one camp per month covering all the messages that are 
part of the Financial Awareness Messages (FAME) booklet, which, inter alia, contains messages on 
various facets of financial literacy incl uding basic banking, digital financial literacy, consumer 
protection etc. 
iv. Financial Literacy Week (FLW) has been conducted every year since 2016 to propagate the message 
of financial education on various themes among members of the public across the country.

entries.t: Construction of Nilambar-Pitambar Singh Adivasi Degree College
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 3620  
ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
 
Construction of Nilambar-Pitambar Singh Adivasi Degree College 
 
†3620. Shri Chhotelal: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
 
     the time by which the construction of Nilambar-Pitambar Singh Adivasi Degree College 
and University is likely to be completed in Robertsganj Lok Sabha Constituency? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(Dr. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
 
Ministry of Education is implementing Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA) 
which is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme aimed at funding specific State government 
universities and colleges, so as to improve their quality by ensuring their conformity to 
prescribed norms and standards. The government has launched the third phase of 
Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA) in June 2023 in the form of Pradhan Mantri 
Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (PM-USHA), with an outlay of Rs. 12926.10 crore for the 
period 2023-24 to 2025-26 to cater to needs of educationally unserved/ underserved 
areas.  
Since the inception of the scheme, a total of 204 projects amounting to Rs. 1942.27 crore 
have been approved to the State of Uttar Pradesh, including 66 projects approved under 
PM-USHA for an amount of Rs. 1025.19 crore. 
Under PM-USHA, all the proposals submitted by the State under various components 
were placed before the Project Approval Board (PAB) for its consideration and approval. 
However, no proposal for Nilambar-Pitambar Singh Adivasi Degree College and 
University was submitted by the State of Uttar Pradesh. Further, under the scheme, 9 
projects amounting to Rs. 35.61 crore have been approved in the Robertsganj Lok Sabha 
Constituency, including 3 colleges with an approved amount of Rs. 13.61 crore under the 
Grants to Strengthen Colleges (GSC) component of PM-USHA.  
 
****

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3621 
ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Financial Literacy in School Curriculum 
 
†3621. Shri Rajkumar Roat: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the present rules, guidelines and policies regarding the inclusion of topics such as savings, 
banking, investment, insurance, taxation system, digital payments, stock market, mutual funds 
and loans in the school curriculum for classes 6 to 10, along with the number of States/Union 
Territories where pilot projects or schemes for financial literacy are currently being run by the 
Central Government; 
(b) whether due to lack of practical financial knowledge, students are facing problems related 
to economic decision-making, online fraud, digital transactions and money management, thereby 
preventing them from becoming financially aware and self-reliant citizens, if so, the details 
thereof; and 
(c) whether the Government proposes to bring policy or action plan to implement 
literacy/commerce as a mandatory or elective subject at the national level for classes 6 to 10, if 
so, the timeline therefor and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (c): The National Education Policy 2020 has recognised twenty first century skills as one of 
the important components for multi skill formation among young learners and connecting 
knowledge to life outside school, wherein financial literacy is seen as an important component for 
school education. As a follow up of NEP-2020, the National Curriculum Framework for School 
Education (NCF-SE), 2023 has been developed by the National Council of Educational Research 
and Training (NCERT) which, inter-alia, provides integration of commerce related components in 
Social Science across grades 6-10. The Social Science textbooks developed by NCERT provides 
considerable scope to develop financial literacy among learners. The curriculum includes topics like 
the evolution of money, the banking system, forms of credit, money and other financial institutions 
such as the stock exchange, etc., to promote financial skills. The Central Board of Secondary 
Education (CBSE) prescribes textbooks developed by the NCERT.  
Under Vocational Education component of ‘Samagra Shiksha’, vocational courses are offered to the 
students from grade IX to XII in the schools covered under the scheme, which are aligned with the 

National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF). Financial literacy is an important area covered 
by Vocational Education. Under the Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance (BFSI) sector, 4 
Job Roles are approved by this Department under this component which are as follows: 
 
i. Microfinance Executive 
ii. Business Correspondent/ Facilitator 
iii. MIS Data Analyst - Financial Services 
iv. Customer Service Associate – Financial Services 
 
Further, since education is a subject in the Concurrent List of the Constitution the implementation 
of school curriculum and introduction of any State-specific initiatives, including projects or schemes 
relating to financial literacy, are within the domain of the respective State Governments/Union 
Territory Administrations. 
 
 
****

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION AND LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO: - 3622 
ANSWERED ON-10/08/2026 
 
Educationally Backward Districts 
 
3622. Shri Vijay Kumar Hansdak: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the total number and names of districts officially identified as educationally backward districts 
(EBDs) in the country, State-wise; 
(b) the details of the socio-religious and marginalized communities that exhibit the lowest literacy 
and school enrolment rates within these identified districts of States; 
(c) the specific Central schemes, budgetary allocations, and financial utilization during the last 
three years aimed at improving educational infrastructure in these areas; and 
(d) the targeted steps taken by the Government to upgrade school facilities, digital infrastructure 
and teacher deployment to mitigate educational backwardness among these specific communities? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHOUDHARY) 
 
(a) & (b):  The Department of School Education and Literacy implements the Centrally Sponsored 
Scheme of Samagra Shiksha - an Integrated Scheme for School Education, it is an overarching 
program for the school education sector extending from pre-school to class XII. It lays down 
detailed guidelines (programmatic/financial) for various interventions of the Scheme reinforcing 
the commitment to ensure that all children have access to quality education with an equitable and 
inclusive classroom environment taking care of their diverse background, multilingual needs, 
different academic abilities and make them active participants in the learning process as envisaged 
in the National Education Policy 2020. 
 
This Department had identified Educationally Backward Blocks (EBB) in States/UTs, where the 
female rural literacy rate was below the national average, under the erstwhile Sarva Shiksha 
Abhiyan. The Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas (KGBVs) were sanctioned in EBB as residential 
schools at upper primary level for girls belonging to disadvantaged groups such as SC, ST, OBC, 
Minority and Below Poverty Line (BPL) under the erstwhile Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan.  
 
With the launch of the Aspirational Districts Programme by NITI Aayog in January 2018 to 
improve the social outcomes of the backward districts, the programs of the government are now 

 
 
 
 
aligned to fill in the infrastructure gaps and improve the learning outcomes in the Aspirational 
Districts of the country. Under Samagra Shiksha, due preference is also given to cover initiatives 
like KGBVs undertaken under Educationally Backward Blocks (EBBs), apart from Aspirational 
districts in the implementation of various interventions to promote equitable and quality school 
education, with a focus on addressing educational gaps and disparities. 
 
The State-wise details of the list of 112 Aspirational Districts, across 26 States and 1 Union 
Territory is provided in Annexure – I.  NITI Aayog being the nodal agency for Aspirational District 
Program maintains the champion of change portal (https://championsofchange.gov.in/) for 
aspirational districts. The district wise details of the educational indicators for aspirational districts 
can be accessed through the portal. 
 
(c) & (d): Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Samagra Shiksha, this Department provides 
financial assistance to States and Union Territories for strengthening Government and 
Government-aided schools by bridging identified infrastructure gaps, including digital 
infrastructure. The assistance is provided based on the gaps reflected in the Unified District 
Information System for Education Plus (UDISE+) and the Annual Work Plan & Budget (AWP&B) 
proposals submitted by the respective States/UTs.

entries.t: Social Security Benefits through e-Shram Portal
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3623 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
SOCIAL SECURITY BENEFITS THROUGH E-SHRAM PORTAL 
 
†3623. SHRI BABU SINGH KUSHWAHA: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a)the details of steps taken by the Government to provide minimum 
wages, health insurance  and social security to delivery partners 
and online platform workers working in gig economy  through e-
Shram portal; 
(b)whether the Government is aware that unorganized labourers in 
many areas of Uttar  Pradesh including Jaunpur are facing 
difficulties in e-Shram registration and details updation; 
(c)if so, the action taken by the Government to address the said issue; 
(d)whether the Government proposes to use the e-Shram database to 
provide employment to youth in unorganized sector of Jaunpur Lok 
Sabha Constituency in industrial units and projects  and if so, the 
details thereof; and 
(e)whether the Government proposes to implement a long-term policy 
to ensure pension,  social security and sustainable livelihood for 
workers registered under e-Shram and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (e): The Code on Social Security, 2020, which came into effect 
on 21 November 2025, provides the definitions of ‘gig workers’ and 
‘platform workers’ and lays down specific provisions relating to their 
social security and welfare. 
 
  The Code provides for framing of suitable social security 
schemes for gig workers and platform workers on matters relating to 
life and disability cover, accident insurance, health and maternity 
benefits, old age protection, etc. The Code provides for setting up of 
a Social Security Fund to finance these welfare schemes. The Code 
also has provisions to constitute a National Social Security Board for 
the purposes of the welfare of gig workers and platform workers.  
Contd..2/- 
 
 

:: 2 :: 
  Further, the Social Security (Central) Rules, 2026, notified 
on 08.05.2026, mark a significant step towards extending formal 
social protection to gig and platform workers. The Rules 
operationalize the provisions of the Code by mandating registration 
of gig and platform workers on the Central Government portal.  
 
  The Ministry of Labour and Employment launched eShram 
portal (eshram.gov.in) on 26th August, 2021 for creation of a 
comprehensive National Database of Unorganised Workers (NDUW) 
including platform workers, migrant workers etc. The eShram portal 
registers the unorganised workers and provides them a Universal 
Account Number (UAN) on a self-declaration basis. 
 
  Over 31.85 crore unorganised workers have already been 
registered on eShram portal includi ng 8.46 crore registrations in 
Uttar Pradesh and 21,61,909 registrations in Jaunpur district. 
 
  To enhance the availability and accessibility of eShram 
and its associated services to unorganised workers, the Ministry of 
Labour and Employment officially la unched the eShram mobile 
application on 24th February 2025. This application facilitates real -
time access to welfare schemes integrated with the eShram 
platform, thereby significantly strengthening both accessibility and 
user convenience. 
 
  In keeping wit h the vision of the Budget Announcement 
2024-25, Ministry of Labour and Employment launched the eShram –
“One-Stop-Solution” on 21st October 2024 which entails integration 
of different social security/ welfare schemes at single portal and 
enables unorganised workers including platform based gig workers 
registered on eShram to access social security schemes and see 
benefits availed by them so far, through eShram. 
 
  So far, fifteen (15) schemes of different Central Ministries/ 
Departments have already been integrated/ mapped with the eShram 
to extend benefits and access to social security schemes to eShram 
cardholders including Pradhan Mantri Street Vendors Atmanirbhar 
Nidhi (PMSVANidhi), Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY), 
Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY), Viksit Bharat -
Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB -G RAM G), 
Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Gramin (PMAY-G), Ayushman Bharat – 
Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY), Pradhan Mantri Awas 
Yojana – Urban (PMAY-U), Pradhan Mantri Matsya  Sampada  Yojana 
Contd..3/-

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3624 
ANSWERED ON MONDAY, 10TH AUGUST 2026 
SHRAVANA 19, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
STRENGTHENING FARMER PRODUCER COMPANIES IN TAMIL NADU 
 
3624. THIRU ARUN NEHRU : 
 
Will the Minister of Corporate Affairs be pleased to state : 
 
(a)  the total number of Farmer Producer Companies (FPCs) 
incorporated in the agricultural districts of Tamil Nadu, with particular 
reference to the Perambalur Lok Sabha Constituency, during the 
financial year 2025-2026; 
 (b)  whether the Government has noted significant compliance 
challenges faced by these rural FPCs regarding mandatory digital 
filings, maintaining statutory registers and conducting annual corporate 
audits, if so, the details thereof: 
 (c)  the specific regulatory relaxations, compliance fee waivers or 
extended deadlines extended to agro -based producer companies 
operating in the economically backward and parched regions of 
Perambalur in Tamil Nadu; 
(d)  the total number of capacity -building awareness workshops 
conducted by the Registrar of Companies in Tamil Nadu to assist local 
maize and cotton farmers in managing corporate governance; and  
(e)  whether the Government proposes to simplify the statutory 
compliance and reporting framework for Farmer Producer Companies to 
encourage greater formalisation of farmer collectives and if so, the 
details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS; 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND 
HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI HARSH MALHOTRA) 
 
(a) D uring the financial year 2025 -26, the total number of Farmer 
Producer Companies (FPCs) incorporated in the districts of Tamil 
Nadu are forty -nine (49) and no Farmer Producer Company was 
incorporated in Perambalur district during the said period. 
Constituency-wise data is not maintained.  
 

 
 
(b) No such specific instances of compliance challenges have come 
to the notice of this Ministry.  
 
(c) MCA administers the compliance framework under the Companies 
Act, 2013, through its e -Governance platform, MCA21, which 
facilitates statutory e -filings by companies (including Farmer 
Producer companies/ agro -based companies) and LLPs. As per 
section 378C(5) of the Companies Act, 2013 an FPC is deemed to be 
a private company. T he Ministry has undertaken several steps to 
simplify corporate compliance requirements for all companies 
including Producer Companies. These steps include:- 
 
i.  Allowing companies to conduct Annual General Meetings 
(AGMs)  and Extraordinary General Meetings (EGMs) through 
Video Conferencing (VC) or Other Audio -Visual Means 
(OAVM). 
 
ii.  Producer companies are entitled for lesser penalties as per 
section 446B of Companies Act, 2013.  As per Section 378C 
(5) of the Companies Act,2013 , a Producer Company is 
deemed to be a private company under the Companies 
Act,2013. Relaxations have been provided to private 
companies under Companies Act,2013  which are also 
applicable to the Producer Companies. In addition to this, 
other relaxations offered to companies from time to time like 
extension of AGMs, relaxation on timelines for annual fillings, 
etc. are also applicable to Producer Companies. 
 
The law does not require rural farmers to personally manage 
digital filings, statutory registers, or corporate audits. 
Instead, section 378W(1) mandates the appointment of a full-
time, professional Chief Executive who must be an outsider 
and not a member -farmer. Under section 378W(5), this 
professional is legally responsible for maintaining the books, 
handling the audit process, and managing all legal and 
regulatory matters. Therefore, the statutory framework 
ensures that a professional personnel handles co mpliance 
and regulatory aspects. 
 
iii.   FPCs are usually Small companies and Companies Act, 2013 
provide for reduced compliance for all small companies such 
as:- 
 
• Abridged annual return prescribed for small companies. 

 
 
 
 
• Zero fee is charged for incorporation of all companies with 
authorized capital up to Rs. 15 lakh or with up to 20 
members for companies limited by guarantee. 
 
iv.    As per section 378Z-O of the Companies Act,2013, any dispute 
relating to the formation, management, or business of a 
Producer Company, shall be settled by conciliation or 
arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. 
 
v.   As per section 378D of the Companies Act,2013, in a case 
where the membership consists solely of individual Members, 
the voting rights shall be based on a single vote for every 
Member, irrespective of his shareholding or patronage of the 
Producer Company. 
 
vi. The Ministry has introduced Companies Compliance 
Facilitation Scheme, 2026 (CCFS-2026) vide General Circular 
No. 01/2026 dated 24 th February, 2026. Through this scheme 
Companies (including Farmer Producer Companies) can file

APPRENTICESHIP OPPORTUNITIES IN ASSAM 
 
3626. MD.RAKIBUL HUSSAIN: 
Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether the Government has observed a decline in apprenticeship opportunities in 
Assam during the last five years and the current year; 
(b) if so, the details  of number of apprentices engaged and the sectors in which the decline 
has been most pronounced year-wise; 
(c) the reasons for such decline, including industry participation, regulatory issues or lack of 
awareness among youth; and 
(d) the specific policy interventions undertaken by the Government to expand 
apprenticeship coverage, particularly in Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and 
emerging sectors in Assam? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP  
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
(a) The National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) is being implemented across 
the country, including Assam, to promote apprenticeship training and enhance the 
employability of youth through industry -led, on -the-job learning.  Under NAPS/NAPS -2, 
apprenticeship engagement in Assam shown down trend   from  FY 2021 -22 to  FY 2024 -25 
However, apprenticeship engagement recovered significantly thereafter, with 10,028 
apprentices engaged during FY 2025 -26, indicating renewed momentum in apprenticeship 
adoption in the State. One of the key initiatives supporting this growth is the North Eastern 
Region (NER) Apprenticeship Promotion Pilot , launched on 20 May 2025 , under which 
eligible apprentices from NER receive an additional financial assistance of ₹1,500 per month 
over and above the stipend support available under NAPS-2. 
(b) Under NAPS-2, 49,064 apprentices have been engaged in Assam from FY 202 1-22 to 
FY 2026-27 (Upto June 2026). Year-wise engagement details are as follows:

The down trend in apprenticeship engagement observed up to FY 2024 -25 was more 
pronounced in sectors such as IT-ITeS, Food Processing, Domestic Workers, 
Construction, Automotive , which traditionally account for a significant share of 
apprenticeship opportunities in the State. However, apprenticeship engagement rebounded 
during FY 2025 -26 following enhanced outreach efforts and the launch of the North Eastern 
Region (NER) Apprenticeship Promotion Pilot . Sector-wise details of apprentices engaged 
in Assam under NAPS during the last five years and the current year are placed at Table-I of 
the Annexure. 
(c) Apprenticeship engagement under NAPS is demand -driven and is influenced by factors 
such as participation of establishments, sector -wise workforce requirements, prevailing 
economic conditions, availability of apprenticeship opportunities, and willingness of eligible 
youth to undertake apprenticeship training. The decline observed in apprenticeship 
engagement in Assam up to FY 2024 -25 may be attributed to variations in industry demand 
and establishment participation across sectors. However, apprenticeship engagement 
witnessed a significant improvement during FY 2025 -26, supported by enhanced outreach 
efforts, increased mobilisation of candidates, and targeted initiatives for promotion of 
apprenticeship in the North-Eastern Region. 
(d) To expand apprenticeship opportunities in Assam, including among MSMEs and 
emerging sectors, the Government has undertaken the following measures: 
• Providing stipend support under NAPS -2 through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) 
mechanism, with Government reimbursement of 25% of the prescribed stipend, 
subject to a maximum of ₹1,500 per apprentice per month.  
• Launching a special pilot initiative for promotion of apprenticeship in the North-
Eastern Region, providing an additional ₹1,500 per month  to eligible apprentices 
from NER.  
• Organising Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Melas (PMNAMs)  every 
month since June 2022 to facilitate mobilisation of candidates and support 
establishments in engaging apprentices.  
• Conducting awareness and outreach programmes to encourage participation of 
establishments, particularly MSMEs, and eligible youth in apprenticeship training.  
• Promoting apprenticeship opportunities across diverse sectors, including IT-ITeS, 
Retail, Food Processing, Logistics, Electrical (including Renewable Energy), 
Tourism & Hospitality, BFSI, Automotive and Production & Manufacturing , 
which have recorded significant apprenticeship engagement in Assam.

entries.t: Implementation of Mission LiFE and Green Credit Programme
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3627 
                                       TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Implementation of Mission LiFE and Green Credit Programme 
 
3627. MS KANGNA RANAUT: 
   
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has developed measurable indicators to assess the impact of Mission LiFE 
and whether any incentive mechanism for States is under consideration; 
(b) whether the Meri LiFE portal has been made available as a public dashboard and whether any 
proposal exists to incentivise better-performing Green Districts; 
(c) whether any institutional framework has been developed to integrate Mission LiFE with the 
functioning of Panchayats, Urban Local Bodies and industries; 
(d) whether the Green Credit Programme provides incentives for individuals, communities and 
Himalayan States, including Himachal Pradesh; and 
(e) whether any time-bound action plan has been formulated for Mission LiFE through sustainable 
public procurement and third-party evaluation, and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (e) Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) is a mass movement aimed at nudging individuals 
and communities to practice an environment friendly lifestyle following a Whole-of-Government and 
Whole-of-Society approach focusing on seven key themes viz., Save Energy, Save Water, Reduce 
Waste, Reduce E-Waste, Say No to Single Use Plastic, Adopt Healthy Lifestyles and Adopt 
Sustainable Food Systems.   
To promote sustainable lifestyles, the Ministry, in collaboration with Line Ministries, Departments, 
and State/UT Governments, is mainstreaming the principles of Mission LiFE by integrating them into 
existing sectoral schemes, programmes, and citizen outreach initiatives. This includes nationwide 
campaigns such as One Nation One Mission: End Plastic Pollution, Harith Yoga, Swachhata Hi Seva, 
World Environment Day,  e-waste awareness campaigns, and various other citizen engagement 
initiatives on MyGov and MYBharat portals, thereby expanding the reach of Mission LiFE across 
urban and rural communities. Additionally, under the flagship "Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam" initiative, over 
310 crore saplings have been planted across the country. 

Meri LiFE portal has been developed for structured reporting and monitoring of LiFE events and 
activities by various stakeholders, which include Central Government/State Government Departments, 
Civil Society Organizations, Industry partners and individuals. The MeriLiFE portal dashboard is a 
public dashboard and shows that over 10 crore participants have engaged in more than 45 lakh LiFE 
events across the country. 
The Green Credit Programme (GCP), notified through the Green Credit Rules, 2023 under the 
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, is an innovative voluntary mechanism to incentivise 
environmentally positive actions and advance the objectives of Mission LiFE by promoting sustainable 
lifestyles and behavioural change. The Programme encourages individuals, public entities, and private 
entities to participate in the restoration of degraded forest lands, enhancing timber, non-timber forest 
produce, fodder, water resources, and other ecosystem services while generating ecological and 
livelihood benefits for local communities. The Programme is open to all eligible public and private 
entities, including those in Himachal Pradesh. 
Time-bound drives espousing the principles of Mission LiFE are carried out through co-ordinated 
actions of individuals and communities encouraging them to make eco-friendly choices and push 
demand for sustainable products.

ii. In 2024, a three -month campaign was conducted, from 16.10.2024 to 15.01.2025. A 
four-month “Financial Inclusion Saturation Campaign” was launched across the country 
in 2.70 lakh gram panchayats and Urban Local Bodies from 01.07.2025  to 31.10.2025,

entries.t: Dependence on Guest Faculty against Vacant Teaching Posts in Universities
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO-3630 
ANSWERED ON- 10/08/2026 
 
Dependence on Guest Faculty against Vacant Teaching Posts in Universities 
 
3630. Shri Vishnu Datt Sharma:  
  
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the increasing dependence of Central 
and State Universities on Guest Faculty against long-standing vacant teaching posts, 
resulting in insecure employment, disparities in honorarium and lack of uniform 
service conditions, if so, the details thereof;  
 
(b) whether the Government is aware that prolonged reliance on such engagements 
has caused financial insecurity, uncertainty regarding recognition of teaching 
experience and has adversely affected academic continuity and faculty retention, if 
so, the details thereof;  
 
(c) whether the Government proposes, in consultation with University Grants 
Commission (UGC), to formulate a uniform national framework prescribing minimum 
service conditions, equitable honorarium, transparent engagement norms and time-
bound filling of regular vacancies; and  
 
(d) if so, the details thereof and the proposed timeline for implementation? 
 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (d): Education is a subject under the Concurrent List of the Constitution of 
India, wherein both the Central and State Governments are empowered to make 
laws. State Public Universities are established under Acts of the respective State 
Legislatures, and their administrative and service-related matters, including 
appointments of teaching faculty are governed by the provisions of the concerned 
State Acts, Statutes, Rules and Regulations. Recruitment and filling up of faculty 

positions in State Public Universities fall within the domain and responsibility of the 
respective State Governments. 
All Central Higher Education Institutions (CHEIs) including Central Universities (CUs) 
adopt different methods/processes which inter-alia, include hiring ad-hoc Faculty, 
Guest Faculty, Contract Faculty, and re-employed teacher so as to ensure that the 
teaching-learning process is carried out in an effective manner.  
UGC has issued guidelines on 28.01.2019 for the appointment and honorarium of 
Guest Faculty in the Universities. It regularly issues instructions to the Universities to 
prepare a time-bound action plan and fill up their vacant posts at the earliest. It has 
also launched a common portal 'CU-CHAYAN' for faculty recruitment, making 
provision for listing of vacancies/ advertisements/jobs across all CUs, thus making 
the entire recruitment process more efficient, transparent and accessible.  
Ministry of Education had exhorted all the CHEIs including CUs to fill up all the 
backlog vacancies in Mission Mode. From September 2022 & up to 23.05.2026, a 
total number of 32114 posts have been filled up by all CHEIs, including faculty 
positions, in Mission Mode. Further, this Ministry has also written a letter on 
28.10.2025 to Education Secretaries of all State Governments to initiate recruitment 
process for the appointment of the optimum number of teachers for the allocated 
courses. 
 
****

(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (d): Education being a subject in the Concurrent List of the Constitution, the majority of schools 
in the country are under the administrative control of the respective State Governments and Union 
Territory Administrations. Accordingly, the recruitment, service conditions and deployment of school 
teachers fall within the administrative domain of the concerned States/UTs. The data relating to 
sanctioned teaching posts and vacant teaching posts in Government schools, including State-wise details, 
is maintained by the respective State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. 
As per the UDISE+, the State/UT-wise details of teachers in-position in Government schools across the 
country are placed at Annexure-I. 
Recruitment of teachers is a continuous process undertaken by the respective State Governments/UT 
Administrations in accordance with their recruitment rules and procedures. Vacancies arise from time to 
time due to factors such as retirement, resignation, creation of new posts consequent to enhanced student 
enrolment and establishment of new schools. The timeline for filling up such vacancies is also 
determined by the respective State Governments/UT Administrations. 
The Central Government, on its part, periodically advises States/UTs to fill up vacant posts of teachers 
through transparent and merit-based recruitment processes, including through autonomous teacher 
recruitment boards or similar organisations. The progress regarding filling up of teacher vacancies 

through competitive selection by the States/UTs, with due care for consistency and sanctity and after a 
technology-based comprehensive teacher requirement planning and forecasting exercise, is periodically 
reviewed by the Department of School Education & Literacy with the States/UTs. 
Further, the Central Government, through the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Samagra Shiksha, 
provides financial assistance to States/UTs to maintain appropriate Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) at various 
levels of schooling as per the norms prescribed under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory 
Education (RTE) Act, 2009, as amended from time to time. 
The National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 emphasises maintenance of a pupil-teacher ratio of under 
30:1 in each school and under 25:1 in areas having large numbers of socio-economically disadvantaged 
students. As per UDISE+ 2025-26, the national PTR stands at 10 at the Foundational Stage, 12 at the 
Preparatory Stage, 17 at the Middle Stage and 21 at the Secondary Stage. 
In respect of Higher Educational Institutions under the Ministry of Education, the Central Higher 
Education Institutions (CHEIs), including Central Universities, are statutory autonomous organisations 
established under the respective Central Acts of Parliament and governed by the provisions of the Acts, 
Statutes and Regulations made thereunder. Faculty recruitment is undertaken by the respective 
institutions in accordance with their Acts and Regulations, and the recruitment powers vest with their 
respective Board of Governors, Executive Committee or Board of Management. Vacancies arise on 
account of promotion, retirement, resignation, death, opening of new institutions, schemes or projects, 
and expansion of student strength and institutional capacity. 
To fill faculty vacancies, the Ministry has, from time to time, advised all Central Higher Education 
Institutions to undertake Mission Mode Recruitment Drives, including special drives for filling backlog 
vacancies. In August, 2021, all CHEIs under Ministry of Education were requested to undertake special 
drive to fill backlog vacancies in their institutions in Mission Mode. The CHEIs undertook special 
recruitment drives to fill the vacancies including of Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs) and 
Other Backward Classes (OBCs). In September 2022, Ministry of Education had also exhorted all the

MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
LOK SABHA

ENTREPRENEURSHIP DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME IN DAKSHINA KANNADA 
  
3632. SHRI CAPTAIN BRIJESH CHOWTA: 
  
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to state: 
             
(a)  whether the entrepreneurship-development programmes has been conducted in Dakshina 
Kannada during the last three years and the current year; 
  
(b)   the details of number of persons trained, enterprises established, beneficiaries who obtained 
credit and enterprises continuing to operate under such programme for entrepreneurship in the 
said district during the said period; 
  
(c)  whether the Government has conducted any assessment to identify sector -wise gaps in 
mentoring, credit and market access and the measures taken/proposed to improve enterprise 
conversion and survival of such enterprises; and 
 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
(a) to (d) : The Government of India promotes entrepreneurship, self -employment, enterprise 
creation and sustainable livelihoods through schemes and programmes of the Ministry of Skill 
Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) and other Ministries/Departments. MSDE thro ugh 
its autonomous organizations, namely, National Institute for Entrepreneurship and Small 
Business Development (NIESBUD) and Indian Institute of Entrepreneurship (IIE) implements  
various Entrepreneurship Development Programmes (EDPs) and Entrepreneurship and Skill 
Development Programmes (ESDPs) across the country including Dakshina Kannada in the state 
of Karnataka. These EDPs and ESDPs are designed to impart entrepreneurial, fina ncial, 
managerial and digital marketing skills and also to offer post-training support through mentorship, 
handholding, and access to credit/finance, market linkages and incubation facilities. 
Under Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) 4.0, emphasis is placed on 
entrepreneurship and livelihood creation through industry -relevant skill courses. The Skill India 
Digital Hub (SIDH) platform provides access to skilling, employment, apprenticesh ip and 
entrepreneurship-related opportunities, including access to loans for entrepreneurship. 
The scheme-wise details of entrepreneurship-related interventions undertaken by MSDE in the 
State of Karnataka including Dakshina Kannada during the last three years and the current year 
are given in Annexure-I. 

Furthermore, the details of various entrepreneurship development initiatives being implemented 
by other Ministries/Departments of Government of India across the country, including Dakshina 
Kannada in the State of Karnataka are placed at Annexure-II. 
MSDE periodically assesses challenges faced by entrepreneurs through programme monitoring, 
feedback from participants, stakeholder consultations, follow -up interactions and field -level 
engagement. These assessments help identify gaps relating to mentoring,  access to credit, 
market linkages and enterprise development support. To improve enterprise conversion and 
sustainability, the Ministry has undertaken several measures, including capacity building in 
entrepreneurship and business management, mentoring and  handholding support under 
schemes, facilitation of credit and market linkages, promotion of digital and e -commerce 
platforms, and strengthening of entrepreneurial ecosystems through partnerships with industry, 
financial institutions and other stakeholders. 
Under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, the Agri -Clinics and Agri -Business 
Centres (AC&ABC) Impact Assessment conducted during 2009 and 2019 identified gaps in credit 
access for agripreneurs  and delays in loan sanctioning. To address the credit support gaps 
identified, state -wise AC&ABC workshops are conducted by NABARD involving bankers and 
other stakeholders including MANAGE, Hyderabad to strengthen credit facilitation. In addition, 
MANAGE and NABARD participate in the State Level Bankers' Committee (SLBC) and District 
Level Consultative Committee (DLCC) meetings to address credit support issues for 
agripreneurs. 
In addition, the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises has conducted an evaluation of 
the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) through a third party agency 
covering PMEGP beneficiary units across all States/UTs to assess the performance of the 
PMEGP units established. Most of the PMEGP units reported increase in average annual income 
and positive profitability across sectors over the years.

HEIs Progress in NIRF Ranking 
 
3633.  Shri Balram Naik Porika: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the progress of higher education institutions ranked in National Institutional Ranking 
Framework (NIRF) and the steps taken to improve global rankings; 
(b) the status of setting up of new Indian Institute of Technologies (IITs) and Indian Institute 
of Managements (IIMs) and central universities with expected timelines and cost overruns; 
and 
(c) the measures taken by the Government to promote skill-integrated education and generate 
employment through vocational courses in schools and colleges? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
 (a) to (c): The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, lays emphasis on improving the overall 
quality of education in Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) through a set of initiatives that 
include promotion of multidisciplinary education, nurturing critical thinking and analytical 
ability, promoting research and innovation, improving the quality of infrastructure, effective 
and qualitative teacher training etc.  
 
National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) was launched in 2015 by the Government 
of India for the annual ranking of institutions/ universities of higher education in India (called 
India Rankings), to promote a healthy competition among educational institutes and 
universities. The methodology of these rankings is based on five broad parameters which are 
“Teaching, Learning and Resources,” “Research and Professional Practices,” “Graduation 
Outcomes,” “Outreach and Inclusivity,” and “Peer Perception”. The number of applications 
received under NIRF increased from 6,272 in 2021 to 14,163 in 2025.The number of unique 
institutions participating in NIRF increased from 4,030 to 7,692 during 2021-2025. 

 
Since, the launch of NIRF, there has been increase in the number of institutions appearing in 
the QS World University Rankings, it has increased from 11 institutions in QS WUR 2015 to 
52 in QS WUR 2027. 
 
To improve Quality of Education, several initiatives have been institutionalised in Centrally 
Funded Institutions. Government of India also provides financial support to State Governments 
under Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA)/ Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha 
Abhiyan (PM USHA) scheme under three components namely, “Enhancing Quality and 
Excellence in select State Universities”, “Infrastructure Grants to Universities” and “Multi-
Disciplinary Education and Research Universities (MERU)” for improvement in Higher 
Education. 
  
Further, World Class Institutions Scheme, also known as Institutions of Eminence (IoE) 
Scheme was launched in 2017 to create distinct category of institutions with great deal of 
autonomy in academic, administrative and financial matters so as to enable them to emerge as 
World Class Academic and Research Institutions in a reasonable time period.  
 
Government of India has established 43 new premier institutes since 2014 which include, seven 
IIT’s, eight Central universities and 9 IIM’s. Most recently, IIM Guwahati was inaugurated in 
February 2026 as the 22nd IIM. The institute is currently operating from its transit campus in 
Kamrup district, Assam. To support its development, the government has allocated ₹555 crores 
for setting up the temporary campus, initiating construction of the permanent facility, and 
ensuring smooth operations during its first five years.  
 
Further Government of India has approved expansion of academic and infrastructure capacity 
including creation of Research Park of five new IITs which had been established in the 
State/UT of Andhra Pradesh (IIT Tirupati), Kerala (IIT Palakkad), Chhattisgarh (IIT Bhilai), 
Jammu & Kashmir (IIT Jammu) and Karnataka (IIT Dharwad) with a total outlay of Rs. 
11,828.79 crore in May, 2025.  
 
To promote skill-integrated education with industry requirements in schools and colleges, 
several initiatives have been undertaken by Ministry of Education including: 
 
 To upgrade school curricula, the National Council of Educational Research and 
Training (NCERT), in collaboration with Central Board of Secondary Education 
(CBSE), has developed resources for computational thinking and AI Curriculum for 
both teachers and students from grade 3 to 8.  
 To develop the capacity of teachers in leveraging technology, focused efforts have been 
made by NCERT in organising training activities on AI, covering more than 96,000 
beneficiaries though these programs.  Similarly, CBSE organises capacity building 
programme to sensitise teachers to the application of AI tools in teaching, learning, and 

assessment, as well as their relevance in educational management and administration.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
  MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
        LOK SABHA 
          UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3634 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Conservation of Lakes and Wetlands 
 
3634. SHRI NARAYAN TATU RANE: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) the number of rivers in the country categorized as polluted at present; 
(b) the details of action taken to check industrial pollution during the last five years; and  
(c) whether the Government has implemented any new scheme for the conservation of lakes and 
wetlands? 
 
     ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE 
CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (c)  State Pollution Control Boards/Pollution Control Committees monitor the water quality 
of aquatic resources in line with the criteria/ guidelines of Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) 
namely, Guidelines on Water Quality Monitoring, 2017. The water quality data is utilized for 
identification of Polluted River Stretches (PRS) based on the level of organic load which is 
measured in terms of Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) levels.  The Polluted River Stretches 
being monitored by CPCB in the country have progressively reduced from 351 in 2018 to 296 in 
2025. 
 
Industrial pollution across the country is regulated by concerned State Pollution Control Boards 
(SPCBs) or Pollution Control Committees (PCCs) through Consent mechanism (Consent to 
Establish and Consent to Operate) under the provisions of the Air (Prevention and Control of 
Pollution) Act, 1981 and the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974. Additionally, 
specific categories of industries are regulated under the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) 
Notification, 2006 through grant of Environmental Clearance (EC) and filing of half-yearly 
compliance reports by the industries for post project monitoring. 
 
Further, in order to strengthen self-regulation, 17 categories of highly polluting industries are 
mandated to install Online Continuous Emission/Effluent Monitoring Systems (OCEMS), for real-
time monitoring and alert system with connectivity to the server of SPCBs/PCCs and Central 
Pollution Control Boards (CPCB). Based on the alerts generated from OCEMS, CPCB also 
conducts surprise inspection of selected industries and appropriate action is initiated by CPCB 
under Section 5 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 against the non-complaint industries. 
 

MoEF&CC is implementing a centrally sponsored scheme, namely, National Plan for 
Conservation of Aquatic Ecosystems (NPCA) for conservation and management of wetlands 
including lakes in the country, on cost sharing basis between Central Government and respective 
State Governments. The scheme covers various activities such as interception, diversion and 
treatment of wastewater, shoreline protection, in-situ cleaning i.e., desilting and deweeding, 
biodiversity conservation, storm water management, bioremediation, catchment area 
treatment including tree plantation and aided natural regeneration, survey and demarcation, 
bio-fencing, sustainable livelihood development including fisheries, eco-tourism 
development, education and awareness creation, community participation, etc.  
 
The NPCA scheme promotes eco-tourism in and around the wetlands. Further, in accordance with 
“Whole of the Government Approach”, various other Ministries/Departments of the Government 
have been playing important role in restoration and conservation of wetlands. Some such crucial 
Programmes/Schemes are Repair, Renovation & Restoration (RRR) of water bodies under Pradhan 
Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY), Jal Shakti Abhiyan, Mission Amrit Sarovar, Mahatma 
Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS), Atal Bhujal Yojana and 
Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT).

Environmental Clearance for Bengaluru Tunnel Road Project 
 
3635. SHRI TEJASVI SURYA: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) whether the State Government of Karnataka or any of its agencies has approached the 
Central Government seeking environmental clearance, appraisal, opinion or any other statutory 
approval in respect of the proposed Bengaluru Tunnel Road Project, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government has examined or proposes to examine the likely environmental 
impact of the said project including its implications for groundwater, urban hydrology, tree 
cover, air quality and climate resilience, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether any Environmental Impact Assessment, hydrogeological assessment, cumulative 
impact assessment or other technical studies have been sought by the Government, if so, the 
details thereof; and 
(d) whether the Central Government proposes to seek information from the State Government 
of Karnataka or otherwise examine the environmental implications of the proposed project, if 
no such proposal is received from the said State, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (d): As per the provisions of the Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) Notification, 
2006, only projects or activities specified in the Schedule to the Notification require prior 
Environmental Clearance (EC) from the Central Government or the State Environment Impact 
Assessment Authority, as applicable. Standalone tunnel projects are not included in the 
Schedule to the EIA Notification, 2006. However, where tunnels form an integral component 
of a highway project falling under the Schedule to the EIA Notification, 2006, the entire 
highway project, including the tunnel component, is comprehensively appraised by the 
Ministry. During such appraisal, detailed assessment of environmental aspects such as 
groundwater, hydrology, drainage, tree cover, biodiversity, air quality, geology, disaster risks 
and climate resilience is undertaken through the Environmental Impact Assessment study, and 
appropriate environmental safeguards are prescribed as conditions of Environmental 
Clearance. 
 
No proposal seeking Environmental Clearance in respect of the proposed Bengaluru Tunnel 
Road Project has been received by the Ministry.

MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
DEPARTMENT OF FINANCIAL SERVICES 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3636 
 
ANSWERED ON MONDAY, 10 AUGUST, 2026/ SHRAVANA 19, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
Restoration of OPS 
 
3636.   SHRI ADITYA YADAV 
 
Will the Minister of Finance be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the official stance, fiscal calculations, and policy analysis conducted by the Central Government 
regarding the growing demands from Central and State Government employees for the restoration 
of the Old Pension Scheme (OPS); 
(b) the core structural infirmities, market risks, and annuity deficits identified by employee federations 
within the current National Pension System (NPS); 
(c) whether any high-level review committee has been constituted to modify the NPS to guarantee a 
defined, inflation-linked minimum pension to employees without burdening State finances and if 
so, the status of its report; and 
(d) the total corpus accumulated under the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority  
(PFRDA) from Central employees' contributions as of date? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (c) The Government had moved away from Old Pension Scheme (OPS) due to its unsustainable fiscal 
liability on the Government exchequer. The restoration of OPS in the States falls exclusively under State 
policy discretion. However, Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG), in its recent State Finance Audit 
Reports, has highlighted the fiscal implications of reversion to OPS by the States. The National Pension 
System (NPS) is a defined contribution -based scheme which was introduced for Central Government 
employees (except armed forces) joining service on or after 01.01.2004.  With a view of improving upon 
the pensionary benefits for such employees, a Committee was constituted under the chairpersonship of the 
then Finance Secretary to suggest measures to modify the NPS. Based on the deliberations of the Committee 
with stakeholders, Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) has already been introduced, w.e.f. 01.04.2025, as an 
option under NPS with the objective of providing inflation linked defined benefits with a minimum assured 
payout of Rs. 10,000/- per month, after retirement to the Central Government employees covered under the 
NPS. The UPS is a fund -based payout system that relies on the regular and timely accumulation and 
investment of applicable contributions made by both the employee and the employer (Central Government) 
to provide an assured monthly payout after retirement.  
 
(d) The total Asset under Management under NPS for Central Government employees as on 26.07.2026 is 
Rs. 3.65 lakh crores.

entries.t: Projects under National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3640 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Projects under National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change 
 
3640.  SHRI GAURAV GOGOI: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has commissioned any study attributing the rising frequency and 
intensity of floods in Sivasagar, Charaideo, Jorhat and Majuli districts to climate change, if so, the 
findings thereof and if not, whether the same is proposed; 
(b) whether climate vulnerability and flood-risk assessments have been completed for Assam and if 
so, the districts covered and their current risk classification, district-wise; 
(c) the details of wetland restoration, floodplain conservation and ecosystem-based flood mitigation 
projects sanctioned for Assam under the National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change, including 
any project covering Majuli or the affected Upper Assam districts; and 
(d) the details of funds released, utilised and outcomes achieved thereunder? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (d) Under the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC), the Department of Science 
and Technology (DST) implements the National Mission for Sustaining the Himalayan Ecosystem 
(NMSHE). Under the Mission, the Assam State Climate Change Cell has been established to provide 
assistance to the State for undertaking vulnerability and risk assessment, human capacity building 
programmes, public awareness programmes and institutional capacity building. The objective is to 
address the sustenance of the Himalayan ecosystem and for implementation of actions identified by 
the State as part of its State Action Plan on Climate Change (SAPCC). 
 
Further, DST has supported a study on vulnerability and risk mapping of Indian States and published 
the reports titled "Vulnerability Profiles for India: State and District Level using a Common 
Framework" and "District-Level Climate Risk Assessment for India: Mapping Flood and Drought 
Risks Using Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Framework". 
 
The vulnerability report identifies Assam as the 5th most climate-vulnerable State in India with a 
vulnerability index of 0.62. Additionally, 15 of the 25 most vulnerable districts in India are from 
Assam, with Karimganj being the most vulnerable district in India with a vulnerability index of 0.753. 
 
The risk assessment study reports that Assam has very high to high flood hazard-prone districts, and 
24 districts fall under the 'Very High' flood as well as drought risk category. Further, according to the 

 
 
   
 
study, 11 districts are at dual risk of flood and drought, including Charaideo, Dibrugarh, Sibsagar, 
South Salmara-Mankachar and Golaghat in Assam. 
 
Under the National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change (NAFCC), the Government of India 
sanctioned a project titled "Management of Ecosystem of Kaziranga National Park by Creating 
Climate Resilient Livelihoods for Vulnerable Communities through Organic Farming and Pond-
based Pisciculture" with total grant assistance of Rs. 24.57 crore. The entire amount of Rs. 24.57 
crore released for the project has been utilized. The project was implemented in the peripheral areas 
of Kaziranga National Park across the districts of Golaghat, Nagaon and Sonitpur in Assam.  
 
The major outcomes of the project include rejuvenation of selected beels (wetlands), resulting in 
enhanced water-holding capacity and improved ecosystem resilience; creation of climate-resilient 
livelihood opportunities for vulnerable communities residing in the vicinity of Kaziranga National 
Park through the promotion of organic farming and pond-based pisciculture; and improved watershed 
management through the implementation of various water conservation measures, contributing to 
sustainable natural resource management.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO-3641 
ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Performance Grading Index for States and Districts 
 
3641. Shri Lavu Sri Krishna Devarayalu: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the objectives of the Performance Grading Index for States/UTs (PGI-S) and Performance Grading 
Index for Districts (PGI-D) and the key outcomes achieved through their implementation; 
(b) the details of performance of Andhra Pradesh under PGI-S and the district-wise performance 
under PGI-D, particularly for Palnadu district, during the last three years; 
(c) whether the Government has identified key areas requiring improvement based on the PGI 
assessments and if so, the details thereof with respect to Andhra Pradesh and Palnadu district; 
(d) the corrective measures, technical assistance and financial support provided by the Central 
Government to States and districts with lower performance to improve learning outcomes, 
governance, infrastructure and digital learning; and 
(e) whether any targets or timelines have been fixed by the Central Government to improve the PGI 
rankings of States and districts including Andhra Pradesh, particularly Palnadu district, if so, the 
details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) and (b): The Department of School Education and Literacy (DoSEL), Ministry of Education has 
prepared 70-indicator based Performance Grading Index (PGI) 2.0 for States/UTs to measure key 
driving performance and critical areas of school education at State/UT level. Most of the States/UTs 
has improved their score in 2025-26 as compared to 2024-25 including Andhra Pradesh. The domain-
wise performance of the States/UTs including Andhra Pradesh in PGI 2.0 reports for last three years 
can be accessed at https://spgi.udiseplus.gov.in. Similarly, domain-wise performance of districts in 
PGI-D report has been released for last 3 years can be accessed at https://dpgi.udiseplus.gov.in. Total 
of 473 out of 782 districts improved their PGI score in 2025-26 as compared to 2024-25. 
 
 
(c) to (e): Indicators of PGI 2.0 and PGI-D have been aligned to policy initiatives and interventions 
introduced post implementation of National Education policy (NEP) 2020 for proper tracking the 
progress.  
 
The DoSEL, Ministry of Education has shared the findings of PGI 2.0 report and PGI-D report 
with all the States/UTs including Andhra Pradesh to suggest the gaps at the disaggregated level and 
for further improvement by prioritizing areas of intervention to ensure that the school education 
system is robust at every level. PGI-D also provides insight into intra State comparison of progress 
of School education which is useful to assess the intervention required at district level and to take 
mid-course correction, wherever required for the holistic development of district as a whole in school 
education. 
 
 

 
The Performance Grading Index of all States and UTs has been discussed during the Project 
Approval Board (PAB) meetings. Based on the performance of the States, the activities suggested to 
the States/UTs in such PAB meetings, includes teacher training in assessment as learning, State text 
book analysis, use of early language kit and early mathematics kit developed by NCERT, training in 
child friendly assessment practices for teachers, documentation of best practices in the States/UTs for 
improvement in learning levels, etc. 
 
Further, Central Government helps States and UTs under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of 
Samagra Shiksha, which is an overarching scheme of school education covering all levels from pre-
primary to senior secondary. Financial assistance is provided to the States and UTs for various 
activities to improve enrolment in Govt. schools, which include opening/strengthening of new schools 
up to senior secondary level, strengthening school infrastructure, setting up, up gradation and running 
of Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas (KGBV) upto class 12, setting up of residential schools/hostel 
named Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Avasiya Vidyalayas, transport allowance, undertaking enrolment 
drives, seasonal hostels/residential camps, provision of vocational education and ICT facilities in 
schools, etc, financial assistance is also provided for aids and appliances for children with special 
needs hostels/residential camps, provision of vocational education and ICT facilities in schools, 
providing free text books and free uniform, transport/escort facility, etc.

entries.t: Implementation and Impact of the National Credit Framework (NCrF)
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO-3643  
ANSWERED ON-10/08/2026 
 
Implementation and Impact of the National Credit Framework (NCrF) 
 
3643. Dr. Shrikant Eknath Shinde: 
Shri Naresh Ganpat Mhaske: 
Shri Shrirang Appa Chandu Barne: 
Shri Ravindra Dattaram Waikar: 
Smt. Bharti Pardhi: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the National Credit Framework (NCrF) has achieved full horizontal and vertical 
mobility between general and vocational education in July 2026, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether a formal "Equivalence Mechanism" has been established to treat years of industrial 
experience as academic credits, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether this framework has allowed Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) and Polytechnic 
graduates to enroll directly into the third year of degree programmes during the current 
academic session, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether this "Skill-Degree Integration" has led to a significant increase in the Gross 
Enrolment Ratio (GER) in higher education, if so, the details thereof; 
(e) whether the industry has formally recognized these "Credit-Based Skill Certifications" for 
senior-level hiring, if so, the details thereof; and 
(f) whether this unified credit system is now being benchmarked against the European Credit 
Transfer System (ECTS), if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (f): The Government of India has framed the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 with an aim to provide holistic, multidisciplinary, flexible and student-centric education. It encourages integration of skill education & envisions a detailed National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF) as the basis for Recognition of Prior Learning.  

 
In alignment with the objectives of NEP 2020, the Government has approved National Credit 
Framework (NCrF) as a comprehensive credit framework encompassing elementary, school, 
higher, and skill education. The NCrF provides for creditisation of all learning and assignment, 
accumulation, storage, transfer & redemption of credits, subject to assessment; and establishes 
academic equivalence between skill, general and experiential education while enabling 
mobility within & between them. As reported in AISHE 2023-24, more than 700 Universities 
and over 7500 affiliated colleges have adopted NCrF. 
 
The University Grants Commission (UGC) has notified “SOP for Operationalisation of 
National Credit Framework in Higher Education” as a practical guide for implementation of 
NCrF. The SOP allows up to 50% of the total credits for a program to be earned from the skill-
based courses.  
 
The All India Council of Technical Education (AICTE) in its Approval Process Handbook 
(APH) 2023-27, sets norms for Entry Level Qualifications for the Technical Programmes in 
accordance with NCrF. It allows 10th + 2-year ITIs students to be eligible for admission to 
Second Year Diploma course(s) in any branch of Engineering and Technology. Further, lateral 
entry to Third Year is available for candidates possessing a 2-year UG Diploma in Engineering 
(NCrF Level 5.0). 
 
Further, the National Council of V ocational Education and Training (NCVET) has developed 
“Guidelines for Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)”. The guidelines delineate a roadmap for 
the seamless implementation of RPL, and empower the industrial bodies to conduct RPL 
assessments for their workforces. This aligns the assessment process in a manner that meets 
the industry's needs. Credits are awarded based on assessment of learning outcomes of the 
specific skills, competencies and knowledge acquired. 
 
Due to concerted efforts by the Government, India’s Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) in higher 
education increased from 23.7 in 2014–15 to 30 in 2023–24. Female GER rose from 22.9 to 
31.2 during the same period. The rise in GER has been accompanied by significant growth in 
student enrolment, with total higher education enrolment increasing from 3.42 crore in 2014–
15 to 4.50 crore in 2023–24, adding more than 1.08 crore students to the higher education 
system. 
 
NEP 2020 envisions an education system rooted in Indian ethos that contributes directly to 
transforming India, into an equitable and vibrant knowledge society, by providing high-quality 
education to all. NCrF aims to contribute to vision this by establishing equivalence and mobility 
between general and skill education so that lifelong learning, recognition of prior learning, 
multiple entry and exit, and continuous professional development is encouraged in the 
education ecosystem. 
*****

Approval of Loan Proposals 
†3646. SHRI OMPRAKASH BHUPALSINH ALIAS PAVAN RAJENIMBALKAR:  
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:  
(a) whether it has come to the notice of the Government that the approval of crop loan proposals 
of farmers in nationalised banks takes longer time from regional/higher offices, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(b) whether the Government proposes to delegate powers to Branch Managers working at the 
branch level in nationalised banks to sanction crop loans to eligible farmers up to a prescribed 
limit, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and  
(d) the steps being taken or proposed to be taken by the Government to provide crop loans to 
farmers in a time-bound and simplified manner? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (d) Major Public Sector Banks have informed that financial powers for sanction of crop 
loan has already been delegated to Branches/Agri Processing Cells/Field Staff/Specified 
Processing Cells etc. depending upon the delegated financial powers in accordance with  their 
respective Board Approved Policy. Eligible proposals for crop loans within delegated limits 
are sanctioned in a time bound manner at the B ranch/Agri Processing Cells/Field 
Staff/Specified Processing Cells level by major PSBs, thereby minimising delays.  
 
Moreover, the Government has taken various initiatives to provide crop loans to farmers in a 
time-bound and simplified manner, which, inter-alia, includes: - 
i. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has issued Directions dated 19.06.2026 on Kisan 
Credit Card Scheme, the scheme aims at providing adequate and timely credit support 
from the banking system under a single window with flexible and simplified procedure 
to the farmers. 
ii. RBI has further advised Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs) to deal with loan 
proposals with in appropriate timelines  and establish a monitoring mechanism for 
reviewing the applications pending beyond the specified period.

(a) whether the Government is aware that existing tourism infrastructure, 
including executive huts and honeymoon resorts at Kadmat Island, is 
currently lying vacant and left unattended; 
(b) whether the Government has any concrete plans to revive and 
operationalize both cruise tourism and staying tourism at Kadmat by 
leveraging these pre-existing facilities; and
